News.title: Three men in their 20s injured after being attack with ‘mystery substance’ in Notting Hill – day before carnival starts
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

ATTACK PROBE Three men in their 20s injured after being attack with ‘mystery substance’ in Notting Hill – day before carnival starts

THREE men have been injured after being attacked with an “unknown substance” in Notting Hill – just hours before the carnival begins.

Cops have launched an investigation after the attack outside a Sainsbury’s store in Ladbroke Grove, West London, last night.



Emergency crews, including cops and ambulance teams, rushed to the area shortly after 10.45pm.

Two of the three men, all aged in their 20s, were rushed to hospital following the assault with an “unknown substance”.



Their injuries are not believed to be life-threatening, the Metropolitan Police confirmed.

The third victim was treated for a hand injury, but he did not require further treatment.

A Met spokesperson said: “Police were supported by the London Fire Brigade and British Transport Police.

“Two men in their 20s were taken to hospital and their injuries have since been confirmed as non-life-threatening.

“A third man in his 20s was treated at the scene for a hand injury and did not require further treatment.

“Police enquiries are ongoing and no arrests have been made at this early stage.



“Enquiries indicate that this was an isolated incident, with no wider threat to the public.

“Anyone with information is asked to contact police by calling 101, quoting reference CAD 7927/27AUG.

“Alternatively, information can be provided anonymously via Crimestoppers on 0800 555 111.”

The London Ambulance Services (LAS) confirmed teams were scrambled to the Ladbroke Grove Tube station yesterday.

An LAS spokesperson added: “We were called at 10:41pm yesterday to reports of an assault by Ladbroke Grove Underground Station, W10.



“We sent ambulance crews, a paramedic in a fast response car, an incident response officer and paramedics from our Hazardous Area Response Team (HART).

“We treated three patients at the scene and took two to hospital”.

News.title: ‘Incredibly kind’ mum found dead in caravan is pictured as family pay tribute – after man, 72, arrested over ‘murder’
News.content:
MURDER PROBE ‘Incredibly kind’ mum found dead in caravan is pictured as family pay tribute – after man, 72, arrested over ‘murder’

A “KIND” mum who was found dead in a caravan has been pictured, as her family pay tribute after a 72-year-old man was arrested on suspicion of murder.

Police were called to a holiday park in Sywell, Northamptonshire, in the early hours of Monday morning.

They tragically found Sue Lumsden dead in a caravan and launched a murder probe into the tragedy.

A man, 72, was subsequently arrested on suspicion of murder in connection with the death.





Sue’s heartbroken family have since paid tribute, describing her as “caring and incredibly kind.”

The family continued: “Mum was a beautiful person inside and out — fun, bubbly, caring and incredibly kind.

“She loved to laugh and had a special way of making those around her smile. Her warmth and loving nature touched so many lives.

“We have chosen this photo because it captures her happy spirit and the person she truly was — full of love, laughter and life.



“Above all, she was a wonderful Mum and a much-loved Nanny Sue, Sister, Auntie and friend.

“She was deeply cherished by her family and everyone who had the privilege of knowing her.

“Her kindness, laughter and loving nature will always be remembered.

“Mum will be missed more than words can say, but the love she gave, the laughter she shared and the memories we made together will remain in our hearts forever.



“She was truly special and will always be loved.”

On Monday Northamptonshire Police said the 72-year-old man remained in custody.

Detective Chief Inspector Ryan Catling said at the time: “This is an extremely tragic incident in which a woman has sadly lost her life, and our thoughts are with her family, friends and loved ones at what will be an incredibly difficult and distressing time.

“Specialist officers are supporting her next of kin, and we ask that their privacy is respected while they come to terms with this terrible loss.

“Our investigation is moving at pace, and we are committed to securing all available evidence and doing everything we can to get justice.



“There will be an increased police presence in the area while our enquiries continue, and even though we have made an arrest, I would encourage anyone who may have information that could assist our investigation to contact us.”

News.title: New Middlesbrough house-ramming by gang on A66 teen’s mum ‘revealed as catalyst for grim chain of events that killed 9’
News.content:
GANGLAND rivals rammed the home belonging to the mum of one of the A66 crash victims just minutes before the fatal collision, we can reveal.

The woman’s silver Audi – which was parked on the driveway – was shunted into the front of the three-storey property in the early hours of last Saturday.



Extraordinary pictures show the crumpled convertible parked outside the boarded-up home, with a blue tarpaulin covering the damage to the building.

Her son Theo Rae, 17, was stalking the streets of Middlesbrough in the VW Passat looking for the rival gang responsible for the attack on the day he was killed in the horror crash.



His nan’s home is also believed to have been rammed, along with a property owned by the dad of another one of the A66 victims, Cole Worthy, 17.

In total, three properties linked to the gang were targeted by rivals in a Volvo XC60 in the early hours of last Saturday.



But it was the attack on Rae’s family that incensed them most, sources said.

Rae and Worthy were joined in the VW Passat by Michael Cahill, 23, Jakub Matusiak, 23, and Makai Saddington, 18, as they sought revenge.



They were spotted by marked police cars who immediately gave chase.

The pursuit through the streets of Middlesbrough lasted for seven minutes before the gang entered the A66 on the wrong side of the road in a bid to shake them off.

Chasing police officers abandoned their pursuit.

But 10 seconds later the gang’s Passat collided head-on with an armed response unit being driven by PC Matthew Blades, 37, and PC Tom Clough, 38.

All seven died instantly in the crash.



The fallout saw a gangland feud which had been bubbling up for months burst out into the open.

One source said: “Cole’s dad’s home was rammed first, but it was empty at the time. No one gave a s**t about it.

“But they were furious that Theo’s house was rammed and his nan’s.

“There was a large police presence at the property but by then Theo and the others were already in the Passat looking for the gang responsible.

“This is the reason it all exploded.”



The source said homes in Middlesbrough have been rammed for months as part of a tit-for-tat campaign involving rivals amid a gangland feud over “drugs and money“.

Two hundred specialist cops have been called in to restore order but residents fear the presence of more uniforms will only inflame gangs in the South Bank, Eston, Pallister Park and Grangetown areas.

Last night, cars were torched at a twisted vigil for one of the young men killed in the A66 wrong-way crash.



Five motors were burned to a crisp in remembrance of Michael Cahill, 23, after he and six others died in the A66 smash on Saturday morning.

His pals paid tribute to him by skidding the cars around a farmer’s field and churning up the ground before setting the motors alight. It is not clear who the cars belonged to.

Cahill’s mum had urged for people to bring “bikes, jeeps, cars and quads” and give her son “the send off he deserves” as she encouraged people to the memorial.



Days earlier a crowd of 200 had gathered to commemorate another of the joyriders, Jakub Matusiak, 23, by lighting flares and tearing around on off-road bikes in his honour.

The vigils were in stark contrast to the quiet church service for PC Matthew Blades, 37, a former teacher, and PC Tom Clough, 38, a former soldier who served in Iraq and Afghanistan.

Cops have so far made 17 arrests following the A66 crash as they crack down on the disorder.

The offences range from suspicion of participating in an organised crime group to possession of firearms or drugs.



On Wednesday, a house fire killed a little girl and her aunt just a few streets away – also feared to be linked to organised crime in the area.

Seven-year-old Valentina Foster and her aunt Natalie McDonald, 34, died in the blaze at 5.23am

Armed cops guarded the fire-hit property as the underworld war burst into the open.

Two men, aged 23 and 31, were arrested on suspicion of murder over the fire and remain in custody.



Valentina had tragically begged relatives to let her spend the night to help celebrate Natalie’s daughter’s 15th birthday.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Family friends say the girl, who escaped the blaze by jumping from a bedroom window with a friend, has now tragically lost both her parents.

Yesterday, a stabbing unfolded down the road with armed cops rushing to the scene.

News.title: World’s ‘youngest king’ who was crowned at just three-years-old dies aged 34 after secret illness
News.content:
ROYAL'S END World’s ‘youngest king’ who was crowned at just three-years-old dies aged 34 after secret illness

OYO Nyimba who was dubbed “the world’s youngest King” has died aged 34 after battling a secret illness.

The King had ascended to the throne of Tooro in western Uganda when he was just three years old after the death of his father.



Last year he was recognised by Guinness World Records as the world’s youngest reigning monarch.

His cause of death has not been revealed but a Ugandan government minister said he had been critically ill and seeking treatment in the US, BBC reports.



The news of his sudden death was announced by the country’s prime minister Calvin Armstrong Rwomiire Akiiki.

He posted on X: “It is with profound sadness and a heavy heart that I announce the passing of His Majesty the Omukama of Tooro, King Oyo Nyimba Kabamba Iguru Rukidi IV.”



He added that the king died at around 10pm local time on Thursday without revealing the cause of his death.

He said: “I call upon all the people of Tooro to remain united, calm and prayerful during this profoundly difficult time.”

The late King leaves behind a son whose identity has not been revealed.

Tooro premiers have confirmed that the continuity of the crown is “assured” and the identity of the heir will be officially revealed at the appropriate time.



His death has shocked many Ugandans as the King’s illness was not disclosed publicly.

Rukidi IV was crowned at just three years old on September 12, 1995 after the death of his father, Rukirabasaija Patrick David Matthew Kaboyo Olimi III.

As a child he was very curious and was adored by his millions of subjects.

He was a mesmerising figure, even for world leaders introduced to him at national events.

The kingdom of Tooro was ruled by regents until he came of age at 18.



As he grew older, Oyo lived a quiet and private life.

He was seen as one of Uganda’s most eligible bachelor’s and never married.

In September, the parliamentary speaker pledged to pay the bride price whenever Oyo determined to get married, to which the king sat in his throne and smiled.

Libyan leader Moammar Gadhafi was one of those who befriended the Tooro monarchy, treating them as if they were part of his extended family.

Gadhafi made multiple trips to Uganda and supported Oyo and the queen mother for years before Gadhafi’s death in October 2011.



Tooro was banned as a kingdom by a republican president when Uganda gained independence from British colonial rule.

The president said he wanted to unify the country, but in 1993, traditional kingdoms were restored in Uganda.

Although they have no political authority, monarchs are seen as guardians of tribal culture.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Africa has only three sovereign monarchies, Eswatini, Lesotho and Morocco, while several other countries recognise traditional kingdoms as cultural institutions without political power.

News.title: How ‘open-air strip club’ red light area has plunged to new, depraved low as sick pimps parade girls as young as 12
News.content:
IT WAS the all singing, all dancing £10billion football tournament that set new attendance records and was watched by millions of excited sports fans around the globe.

But while all eyes were on the World Cup, for those living near ‘The Blade’ red light district in Seattle, the tournament brought yet another wave of misery – as violence and sex trafficking span out of control with gangs running amok.





Terrified residents have even resorted to erecting makeshift metal barricades to keep out the pimps and gun-toting gangs that make it too dangerous to go out at night.

The Sun first reported on prostitution around Aurora Avenue in North Seattle last year, after footage of a half-naked sex worker shopping at a petrol station went viral.

Campaigners likened it to an “open-air strip club” and authorities pledged to crack down.

But since then the problem has got even worse, we can reveal.

Peter Orr, a member of Neighbours of North Aurora group, says shootings have become a nightly occurrence on roads where the police fear to tread.

He is demanding the city council “immediately shut down the streets to separate the pimps from our neighbourhood”.

He adds: “You’ve got people trying to live here and not get shot at night.

“In the meantime, the pimps aren’t taking a break. It’s ratcheting up.





“FIFA coming into town brought an extra wave of sex trafficking.

“It’s seen all over the world and Aurora is the number two hotspot for human trafficking in the US.

“Pimps are only going to want to make it number one so we need to combat that with some kind of action.

“Living along Aurora right now is waking up to gunfire at any time from 10pm. You never know exactly where it’s coming from.

“All you can do is call the police and hope for the best.”

At least 60 sex workers prowl The Blade most nights, underpinned by an army of pimps who battle for control of the most lucrative spots.

US news crews have captured footage of drive-by shootings and gun fights that have broken out on roads where scores of houses are peppered with bullet holes.

Politicians say the constant bloodshed has reached unprecedented levels.



In June, around 300 fed-up residents marched down Aurora Avenue carrying a banner reading: ‘Stop sex trafficking, no more shootings.’

Large metal barricades were hastily erected on streets leading into North Seattle in a desperate bid to keep out the criminals.

One protester, who declined to give his name, said: “A pimp shoot-out right across the street from my house put bullets into my home right above where my six-week-old baby was sleeping. Today we march for no more bullets in our bedrooms.”

Campaigners say many of the sex workers are trafficked from Central and South America as well as other parts of the US.

Horrifyingly, a significant number of them are under the age of 16.

Seattle council member Debora Juarez said: “What we are seeing in the years I have lived there, is a much more violent Aurora than I have ever seen in the last decade.

“It is a public safety issue. It’s more predatory and we have more sex trafficking.”

Council member Joy Hollingsworth added: “The first thing I want to talk about is shutting the streets down. That is by far the most important thing.



“The second thing is the 12, 13 and 14-year-old girls that are being raped and exploited by paedophiles on Aurora – that needs to be addressed.

“Right now, we can shut those streets down to ensure they are safe.

“Point blank, they have the authority to do that and then we can look at the next steps.”

Aurora’s plight became international news when campaigning journalist Jonathan Choe posted a social media video titled: “North Seattle is lost.”

His film showed a young prostitute clad in nothing little more than high heels, skimpy knickers and a pink top, shopping for food in the middle of the day.

When she realised Choe was filming, she asked: “What are you recording for?”

Then – showing how normalised vice has become in the area – she added: “This is the Blade and we are selling ass over here so you can put your camera down. I ain’t got no shame in my game.”

Aurora Avenue, also known as State Route 99, became a notorious red light district due to it being a main route for truckers travelling to and from the Canadian border.



However, recent studies have shown that many of the men paying for sex are white collar workers working for major corporations such as Amazon, Microsoft and Starbucks.

Between 2013 to 2021, at least 77 per cent of sex buyers were employed, with about 30 percent of those working in tech and business, according to local government statistics.

Ben Gauen, a senior deputy prosecuting attorney who focuses on human trafficking and commercial sexual exploitation cases, calls the men that inhabit Aurora an “incredibly privileged sector of our society”.

He added: “I can’t think of any other subset of offenders that we see who have that level of employment at the time they committed their offence.”

Some prostitutes boast they can make $4,000 (£3,061) to $7,000 (£5,355) a day, picking up the wealthier clients.

But most will only make a few hundred, turning tricks for between $60 (£45) for oral sex and $100 (£76) for full sex.

One sex worker, called Winter, told the Taboo Room YouTube documentary: “I’ve been kidnapped and tortured but this lifestyle – and the money – is very addictive.

“I got out of it before. I got a job as a paralegal. But I wasn’t making the amount of money that I was making doing this so I was like, it’s easier to come and do this.

“On a slow day I will make $1,000 at least and the most I’ve made out here is $4,000.”

Violent crime has shot up by 43 per cent in the last decade, according to the King County Prosecuting Attorney’s Office.



Last year 427 serious crimes known as felony cases were recorded along Aurora Avenue North.

The cases included 99 felony assault cases, 30 unlawful gun possession cases, 44 residential and commercial burglaries, and 67 organised retail thefts.

Drug use is rife and pimps feed the sex workers’ addiction to crack cocaine and fentanyl, an opioid that induces zombie-like behaviour.

One person writing on the Reddit site commented: “Many of the girls aren’t there by choice. They were conned into the trade by their “boyfriend” AKA pimp.

“The pimps then use pretty extreme measures to keep them in the trade.

“Those measures can lead to drug addiction and PTSD worse than a combat veteran. And the vast majority are under 18 when they start, on average around 13.”

Another outraged local chipped in: “I drive this section daily as I live about six blocks from this area.

“It’s really ramped up in the last two years. I really am like most in that I don’t have a problem with it if the girl wants to do it and she is of age (18 at least please).

“But some of these girls are definitely not 18 and that I have a huge issue with. I saw a girl recently that had to be no older than 12 or 13 and it broke my heart.”

Seattle City council caved into pressure and installed concrete barriers to keep out the gangs late in June.



The delayed action coincided with the start of the World Cup, when a total of six games were played in Seattle including the controversial round of 16 grudge match between the USA and Belgium.

Whilst fans enjoyed the spectacle, Seattle police launched Operation Circuit Breaker and Operation Red Card to clamp down on the vice scourge.

Three juveniles were removed from The Blade and four pimps and johns were arrested during simultaneous two-day operations.

Seattle Deputy Chief Andre Sayles said: “There were a lot of pimps and sex workers that left the area because they understood what we were doing.

“We were able to contact 60 individuals that we identified as sex workers and 10 of those individuals took the services we provided.

“We have the pimps and criminals that are controlling these individuals and we have to be aware of that, and also be aware of our safety and the safety of these sex workers as we bring them back to their families.

“We are going to continue these efforts not just along the Aurora corridor area but throughout Seattle as a whole.”

News.title: Huge fire erupts by Wembley Stadium & IKEA with smoke billowing into air as more than 100 firefighters tackle blaze
News.content:
OVER 100 firefighters are bravely battling a huge blaze near Wembley Stadium and IKEA.

Twenty fire engines and 125 firefighters have been deployed to tackle the fierce inferno on Hannah Close in Neasden, London.



Shocking images from the scene show thick black smoke billowing into the sky, visible from miles away.

Locals have been warned to close their doors and windows due to the amount of smoke in the area.



Stunned residents watched on from high-rise flats as the drama unfolded before midday on Friday.

Locals have also been told to stay inside “where possible” while the fire still rages.



The cause of the blaze is not yet known, with no injuries or casualties reported at this stage.

The fire is raging less than a mile away from Wembley Stadium and Ikea.



A nearby Amazon warehouse, which is not related to the industrial unit involved, has been evacuated

Crews from Wembley, Park Royal, Willesden and surrounding fire stations were mobilised to the scene after the first reports just after 11.30am.

The fire is located at a mixed waste facility with an industrial estate on fire, said London Fire Brigade.

The Jubilee Line has been affected with “severe delays” due to the proximity of some of the line to the fire.

There is no service between Willesden Green and Wembley Park.



There is also no service on the entire Metropolitan line as emergency services respond to the fire alert at Neasden.

Transport for London says tickets will be accepted on London Buses, DLR, Elizabeth line, Mildmay line, c2c and Thameslink services.

Passengers with Metropolitan line tickets can use London Buses, London Overground, London Northwestern, Chiltern Railways and Thameslink services.

Rail services into London Marylebone have also been disrupted.

Three of the Fire Brigade’s 32m ladders were quickly mobilised to the scene.



Firefighters have also deployed a Hose Laying Unit and High Volume Pump to the scene.

This will increase the amount of water available to firefighters as they work to bring the fire under control.

More than 70 calls were made reporting the blaze.

London Fire Brigade said in a statement on social media: “Twenty fire engines and around 125 firefighters are responding to a fire on Hannah Close, Neasden.

“Residents in the immediate area should close doors and windows, remaining inside where possible, due to the large amount of smoke being produced.”



“The brigade’s control room took the first of over 70 calls reporting the fire at 11.34am. Crews from Wembley, Park Royal, Willesden and surrounding fire stations have been mobilised to the scene.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“The cause of the fire is not yet known.”

A spokesperson for London Ambulance Service said an incident response officer has been sent to the scene and currently no patients are being treated.

News.title: Protesters set fire to migrant camp in Ceuta as tensions flare over ‘invasion’ & rioters clash with police
News.content:
FURIOUS protestors have torched migrant camps in Ceuta as tensions flare over repeated border breaches into the Spanish territory.

Shocking footage shows flames engulfing tents and thick smoke billowing in the air over the huge camps where thousands have been staying since a major border “invasion” last month.



Cueta locals were seen waving Spanish flags after swarming the area and clashing with police guarding the camps.

The locals took out their frustrations by smashing up the makeshift tents on the beaches.



Witnesses claimed some of the migrants responded by throwing rocks at protesters.

Tensions boiled over after a horde of around 70 migrants attacked a military vehicle on Thursday – sparking angry retaliation from locals.



One soldier inside the truck was injured by a flying stone with cops arresting 12 Moroccans over the suspected ambush.

Many people are blaming the government’s lack of action to remove the migrants.

Kissy Chandiramani, a finance councillor, told local news that “the tension in the city of Ceuta is very high” because there is “no response” from the government.

“We feel abandoned”, she said on Thursday, adding that protestors should nonetheless stay calm because growing hostility would not solve the crisis.

A local wrote on X: “These brave patriots cannot be blamed, considering that a month has passed since invasion began and no one has done anything.”



Clashes between rioters and police have increased in recent days.

On Thursday, dozens of protestors staged a sit-in to block Red Cross food packages from reaching the migrants.

Many waved Spanish flags and chanted “they should leave” and “out with the Red Cross” before cops stormed the area and dispersed the crowds.



A day earlier, police fired tear gas to disperse protestors near migrant camps.

Beefed up “containment barriers” have been erected by the Civil Guard – but on Thursday another boatload landed on the beach.

Dramatic footage shows large groups of migrants jumping from the vessel before scrambling on to the shore in Calblanque Regional Park, near Murcia.

Last month, false rumours circulated on social media sparked a mass invasion of Ceuta – with a tide of mostly men swimming across the 8-mile stretch from Morocco to the enclave.

More than 140 people died in the attempt, according to officials.



Tens of thousands of migrants went back across the border but those who stayed sparked fury.

One man was accused of breaking into a woman’s flat and creeping into her bed wearing just his underwear.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The intruder was arrested and handed a 16-month prison sentence, which was substituted for deportation and a five-year ban on entering Spain.

Others were seen smashing up windows and breaking into buildings before Spain sent in the army to crack down on the chaos.

News.title: Urgent probe launched after two teenage girls ‘sexually assaulted at popular UK music festival’ as man, 27, arrested
News.content:
FESTIVAL PROBE Urgent probe launched after two teenage girls ‘sexually assaulted at popular UK music festival’ as man, 27, arrested

TWO teenage girls have allegedly been sexually assaulted at a popular UK music festival, as a 27-year-old man is arrested.

The reported incident took place at the This Ain’t Texas country music festival at Home Park, Plymouth, on July 18.

A 27-year-old man from Tavistock has been arrested on suspicion of sexual assault.

He has since been released on bail as enquiries into the horror continue.





Police are appealing for anyone with any information that may assist their investigation to come forward.

Devon and Cornwall Police said: “Officers are investigating a report that two teenage girls were sexually assaulted at a music festival in Plymouth.

“The incident took place at the This Ain’t Texas Festival at Home Park, Plymouth, on July 18, at around 6pm.

“Officers are asking any witnesses to the incident to come forward.

A 27-year-old man, from Tavistock, has been arrested on suspicion of sexual assault and has been released on bail while enquiries continue.

“If you witnessed the incident or have any information that could help with the investigation please contact us via our website or by calling 101 quoting reference number 50260189190.”

News.title: Disorder at balloon release for man who died in A66 car crash 'put lives at risk', MP says
News.content:
Serious disorder at a balloon release for one of the young men who died in the A66 car crash is "unacceptable", an MP has said.

Durham Police said a large crowd gathered on a privately owned field near Haswell, County Durham, on Thursday evening where five vehicles were set on fire and balloons, flares, and fireworks were released.

Assistant Chief Constable Jon McAdam said: "We utterly condemn anyone who would use that tragedy as an excuse for disorder."

Redcar MP Anna Turley said the event "put lives at risk" and left residents "frightened and angry in their own communities"

Turley added: "People have a right to grieve and to pay their respects - but people also have a right to feel safe in their own homes and neighbourhoods."

Seven people, including PC Matthew Blades and PC Tom Clough, died in the crash near Middlesbrough on Saturday, followed by a house fire in Grangetown on Wednesday that claimed the lives of a woman and a seven-year-old girl.

Police said a majority of the crowd in the field near Haswell had travelled from outside the County Durham area, bringing with them a number of vehicles.

Officers were called to the area shortly after 17:30 BST, the force said.

No-one was injured and no arrests were made.

However, a police operation, including investigation work and visible uniformed patrols, would continue in the area over the coming days, Durham Police added.

News.title: NHS bosses warn of chaos in ADHD and autism care
News.content:
Autism and ADHD care is at risk of descending into chaos, NHS bosses are warning, as costs spiral out of control and unregulated private providers capitalise on the huge demand for help.

The NHS Alliance, which represents health managers, says the current system in England represents a "bad deal" for patients and taxpayers alike.

It points to big variations in what the NHS is being charged for assessments and care - in one case, a local health board was paying Â£300 to Â£3,000 for similar services.

The group says there has been a rapid expansion in new providers â both private firms and charities are involved - and NHS managers are struggling to ensure the quality and safety of care being provided.

The government said an independent review into services and what is behind the rising demand, including whether there is over-diagnosis of these conditions, would be published soon.

It said it would act on the findings of that, promising a ânew national approachâ for autism, ADHD and mental health.

Ahead of that, the NHS Alliance has been gathering information from integrated care boards, which hold the budgets for local services, about the current state of care.

News.title: Watch: Stargazers around the world glimpse 'Blood Moon' lunar eclipse
News.content:
Stargazers across the globe gathered to witness a near-total lunar eclipse on Thursday night and early Friday morning.

Some parts of the world had a chance to see a rare 'Blood Moon', when the Sun, Earth and Moon line up in the night sky.

It comes just weeks after millions of people witnessed the most significant solar eclipse in nearly 30 years.

News.title: Serial rapist police officer passed vetting despite warnings, BBC reveals
News.content:
A police officer - who was later exposed as a violent serial rapist - passed vetting checks to join the force despite having two reports of criminal behaviour against women on his record, BBC Disclosure can reveal.

Alan Greer was investigated by police in 2002 and 2005 for making inappropriate phone calls to women, with one case resulting in a formal police caution.

He was accepted into Strathclyde Police in 2009, despite vetting staff being aware of his previous offending.

The revelation comes a month after Police Scotland told the BBC there had been no "missed opportunities over the years" to identify Greer's offending sooner.

In response to further questions from the BBC, Police Scotland moved to clarify its earlier comments.

It said it had "provided answers to questions relating to Alan Greer's offending during the course of his police career" and did not believe it had been answering questions about his police vetting record.

News.title: Celtic and Rangers ordered to play Scottish Cup ties behind closed doors after fan disorder
News.content:
Celtic and Rangers have both been ordered to play their next home Scottish Cup matches behind closed doors after last season's quarter-final was marred by fan disorder.

Both clubs will also have to pay Â£100,000 to the team they are drawn against in that fixture.

The two clubs could also face a second home match without fans if there is a further incident of either side's supporters engaging in "unacceptable conduct" in a Scottish Cup fixture.

Celtic progressed to last season's semi-finals by beating Rangers on penalties at Ibrox, after which fans of both teams spilled on to the pitch.

The sanctions are likely to come into force when both sides enter this season's Scottish Cup in January.

News.title: Greens call for temporary ban on new data centres
News.content:
Zack Polanski has called for a freeze on the approval of new data centres in England because of concerns about the amount of water and energy they use.

The Green Party leader said the government should introduce stricter environmental rules and give communities more say on whether the centres are built in their area.

Data centres can use significant amounts of water to cool their systems, although there are no official figures on how much water they consume in the UK.

The government said a pause would lead to the UK losing investment and being dependent on overseas computing for sensitive data processing.

A spokesman said: "It would be a disaster for jobs and national security."

There are hundreds of data centres in the UK â with plans for many more.

Exact numbers are hard to find, but the BBC reported last year there were around 477.

Many are clustered around London and the south of England â areas which are officially in drought at the moment.

The amount of water data centres consume can change based on size, design and local climate - the hotter the area the more water needed to cool the equipment.

News.title: What we know after the big Grand Theft Auto 6 preview
News.content:
After more than 18 months since the last official glimpse of Grand Theft Auto 6, developer Rockstar has shown fans a 26-minute preview of the upcoming blockbuster video game.

Its "extended look" debuted on Netflix, six hours before going live on YouTube, and was the first chance players have had to see detailed footage of the title in action.

The montage, with no commentary or explanatory captions, showed off improved graphics, detailed environments and a selection of car-chases and shoot-outs from the sequel.

The broadcast followed a week of unauthorised gameplay leaks, which the developer said it had been "heartbreaking" to see shared online.

After it got its chance to show the version of GTA 6 it wanted the world to see, here are some things we learned, and some things we still don't know.

News.title: Celebrity Hunted showed I can achieve anything after cancer, Amy Dowden says
News.content:
Spoiler warning: This story contains details of the winner(s) of Celebrity Hunted

Strictly Come Dancing star Amy Dowden has said winning Celebrity Hunted has helped her believe she can "achieve anything" following her battle with cancer.

The 36-year-old professional dancer won the latest series of the Channel 4 challenge show alongside Strictly's Carlos Gu, claiming a joint victory with actor Brian Conley and his daughter, comedian Lucy Conley.

The programme sees celebrities go on the run while an elite team of hunters tries to track them down, in aid of Stand Up To Cancer.

The joint victory marked the first time in the show's history that two pairs have managed to stay on the run without being caught.

It also marked a reunion for Dowden and Brian Conley, who were paired together on the BBC One dance programme in 2017.

The nail-biting finale saw the two pairs jumping on an extraction plane from a beach in north Wales, narrowly escaping the hunters.

Dowden was just 32 when she was diagnosed with grade three breast cancer in May 2023, after finding a lump in her breast the day before her honeymoon.

She said: "Cancer took a lot away from me in the last two years but I truly feel I've got my confidence back and this has given me the belief I can go on to achieve anything.

"We got on to that plane, I was just like, 'celebrate!' I grabbed the champagne!"

The Welsh dancer made a return to the ballroom floor in 2025, and has been candid about her experiences of the disease, including having a mastectomy, chemotherapy and fertility treatment.

She was put into an early menopause as a result of the treatment, which she opened up about in her BBC documentary Strictly Amy: Cancer And Me.

News.title: 'Please help us find her': Families fly to Nepal in search for 33 missing British nationals
News.content:
Essex nurse Rajendra Pudasaini said his relatives were "swept away" by the floods.

"My wife's auntie and uncle, and their granddaughter and her husband are missing, and my godson as well," he said.

"They're gone. The speed the water came, they couldn't be saved, they were just swept away."

Sarada Simkhada, a senior nurse at Darent Valley Hospital in Kent, is also among the missing, according to a local councillor.

The Times said Simkhada was "following in the footsteps of thousands of Hindus this month in making the spiritual journey to Mount Kailash".

A family of four, including an 18-year-old A-Level student and a 13-year-old girl, from Surrey are also among the missing.

Spandan Sahu, 18, was in Nepal with his father Santosh Sahu, 46, his mother Surabhi Manmath Padhy, 44, and sister Syna Kumari Sahu, 13.

Spandan had just finished his A-levels at Royal Grammar School Guildford.

In a statement, a spokesperson for the school said: "It is with great concern that we have been informed that a former student, along with members of his family, have been reported missing in Nepal.

"Whilst we are hoping for positive news, we do not have any further information at this time.

"Our thoughts, love and deepest sympathies are with all of the families and loved ones of anyone affected by this tragedy in Nepal at this incredibly difficult time."

Vikram Kolagatla, from London, told the BBC he has not heard from his wife, Geetha Reddy, since the flooding hit.

Reddy, who has two daughters aged 12 and 14, had been in Hotel Kailash in Rasuwagadh when the flooding hit.

"We're not sure what to do. I have two little girls, and their schools are starting next week," Kolagatla added.

"The kids still don't believe it. They think she's stuck in the flood and that she'll come back. They think she's stuck somewhere and there's no mobile network."

News.title: UK soldiers could get paragliders to drop behind enemy lines
News.content:
British soldiers could soon be given powered paragliders to enable them to fly up to 200 miles behind enemy lines.

The backpack-sized gliders mean Royal Marine and Parachute Regiment troops could fly into hostile areas during the night without the need to drop from aircraft.

Manufacturer Blakcro, which is based in Wiltshire, say the machines can be assembled in eight minutes and launched on foot.

The Ministry of Defence is spending Â£6m on the system, with trials set to begin "in the coming months".

Defence Minister Luke Pollard said the government was building a "more resilient, homegrown defence supply chain and ensuring our armed forces receive the pioneering equipment that can give them the edge on the battlefield".

The paragliders, which have a range of up to 200 miles, can carry body armour, night vision equipment and weapon mounts.

The manufacturers say the titanium-framed machines can be used to enter hostile territory covertly as they are more difficult to detect by radar or sound than traditional aircraft.

The gliders will be powered by a fan but pilots will be expected to launch them on foot.

The technology is currently being used by other Nato member countries.

Blakcro, which employs 11 people, was founded in 2023 and has received government support for two other projects.

The company also works with the US Department of Defense.

The government has said it wants to spend more on UK-made defence equipment and bring smaller companies into the supply chain.

Chancellor John Healey is under pressure to increase defence spending after he resigned from Sir Keir Starmer's government in protest at its investment plans.

As defence secretary, he accused Starmer's government of having no clear timetable to reach the target of spending 3% of the UK's national income on defence.

He is expected to increase spending further - but will not be setting out any plans in his first Budget in October.

Instead, a revised defence plan will be set out as part of a wider government spending review in the spring.

A government spokesperson said: "The first duty of government is to keep its citizens safe.

"The prime minister and chancellor are committed to fully funding the defence investment plan.

"At the spending review we will set out a pathway to meet our NATO commitment of 3.5% of GDP on defence by 2035 and will set a target date to hit 3% on that path."

News.title: Clean-up of illegal waste supersite costs taxpayers £6m
News.content:
The clear-up of one of England's largest illegal waste tips has been completed - landing taxpayers with a Â£6m bill.

The government has vowed to recoup the clearance costs for the Kidlington dump in Oxfordshire - and seven other sites - from the criminals responsible.

In 2025, around 22,000 tonnes of domestic and commercial rubbish was dumped at the spot, between the River Cherwell and the A34. It is one of nearly 30 so-called "supersites" first uncovered by a BBC investigation.

The government, which launched a crackdown on waste crime last week, said it would do more to force criminals to pay for clean-up operations by confiscating their money and assets.

But figures obtained by the BBC show that, in the past five years, the Environment Agency has so far managed to claw back just over Â£7m from waste criminals using Proceeds of Crime Act (Poca) confiscation orders.

At the same time, the agency says waste crime costs the economy Â£1bn a year., external

Campaigners have labelled the amount taken from convicted criminals as "derisory" while the Country Land and Business Association (CLA), which represents rural landowners, asked: "Where is the deterrent?"

The amount paid by criminals so far was revealed by an Environmental Information Regulations (EIR) request to the Environment Agency by the BBC.

It shows there have been 66 confiscation orders between January 2021 and March 2026, totalling Â£7.3m.

Fourteen orders have yet to be fully paid, leaving around Â£1.4m still to be recovered.

The figures cover those larger illegal sites for which the Environment Agency is responsible, and do not include confiscation orders for smaller fly-tipping offences, which fall under the remit of local authorities.

News.title: Baby died after hospital monitor volume was too low
News.content:
A coroner has raised concerns after a boy died following a medical emergency that went unnoticed because a hospital monitor alarm was set too low.

Ismaeel Islam, who was under six months old, died at the Royal London Hospital's special care baby unit on 7 March 2025.

Coroner Mary Hassell said he suffered a desaturation and respiratory arrest on 3 November 2024 which went unnoticed for about 30 minutes because the alarm's volume had been turned "too low to be usefully audible".

The coroner found this medical emergency led to his death. She issued a Prevention of Future Deaths report to Masimo UK, the maker of the monitoring alarms used at the hospital. Masimo UK has 56 days to respond.

Hassell, who led an inquest into the death at North London Coroner's Court, said the nurse caring for Ismaeel, who had health problems linked to Down's syndrome, growth restriction and prematurity, was attending to another baby at the time and he was not in her line of sight.

The coroner acknowledged that Barts Health NHS Trust, which runs the hospital, had since introduced measures to improve the audibility of alarms and lines of sight to cots on the unit.

However, she raised concerns that the alarms could be set at a volume too low to be heard and said there was a risk of future deaths unless action was taken.

She has called for baby monitors to be locked at a maximum volume or set to maximum.

"If Ismaeel's deterioration had been recognised immediately and treated appropriately, his life would have been saved," she said in her report.

News.title: Sunderland and Bournemouth draw AC Milan in Europa League
News.content:
Sunderland will mark their first European campaign since 1973 with a trip to the San Siro after drawing AC Milan in the Europa League.

The Black Cats, who finished seventh in the Premier League last season, will face the seven-time European champions in one of their eight league-phase matches.

Bournemouth have also been handed a tie against the Italians, although theirs will be on home soil.

The Cherries, who have qualified for European football for the first time, will also face Real Sociedad among their eight games.

Last season's Conference League winners Crystal Palace have been handed arguably the toughest draw out of the three Premier League teams, with Pierre Sage's side set up for meetings with Lyon, Real Sociedad and Besiktas.

It will be the first time Palace have competed in the Europa League, having been demoted from the competition last July for breaching multi-club ownership rules.

Scottish Premiership champions Celtic, who fell into the Europa League after surrendering a four-goal lead against LASK in the Champions League play-off tie earlier this week, will take on Marseille, Benfica and Besiktas.

In the Conference League, Brighton's draw includes fixtures against AS Monaco and Spanish side Getafe.

Hearts have also been drawn against Monaco and will also face a trip to Mohamed Salah's Trabzonspor.

The Europa League final will take place in Frankfurt on 26 May, with the Conference League equivalent taking place six days later in Istanbul.

News.title: Artist defends 'unfinished' Ronnie O'Sullivan mural
News.content:
A Sheffield street artist has defended his mural of snooker player Ronnie O'Sullivan after the design received criticism - saying that the project is "unfinished".

Chris Ashmore was commissioned to produce the artwork featuring seven-time world champion O'Sullivan for the back wall of the Spot On Snooker Club on Langsett Road.

Although many residents said they liked the mural, others described it as "zombie-like", "shocking" and O'Sullivan's face as "skeletal".

Ashmore said he was surprised by the viral response online, but confirmed that he had only completed two weeks out of the five assigned to the job, and "touch-ups" were still needed.

The local artist said part of the problem was that he had been working from a scaffolding platform which obstructed his view, meaning he didn't get the "full perspective".

"I usually use a scissor lift, where you can stand back and see things as a whole, but I couldn't use it as the land is too uneven," he explained.

"When the scaffolding came down, I came away and boom - it's gone viral.

"I saw people saying it looks like Michael Jackson or a zombie. I've got thick skin, I'll be OK, but it didn't feel fair."

News.title: Huge waste facility fire shuts Tube and train lines
News.content:
A large fire has broken out at a waste facility close to Wembley Stadium in north-west London, shutting Tube and train lines in the area.

The London Fire Brigade (LFB) said 125 firefighters were tackling the blaze at an industrial estate on Hannah Close in Neasden, with the smoke plumes visible from miles away in central London.

The LFB was alerted just after 11:30 BST and has deployed 20 fire engines to the scene. Residents have been warned to keep their windows and doors shut because of the huge amount of smoke.

Transport for London (TfL) said the entire Metropolitan line has been suspended as a result, while the Jubilee line has been part shut between Willesden Green and Wembley Park.

Rail services to and from London Marylebone are also being delayed or cancelled due to train lines to Aylesbury being blocked, National Rail said.

News.title: Nicola Coughlan and Hugh Bonneville among actors calling for law on AI voice cloning
News.content:
More than 80 performers have signed the letter, with Derry Girls actress SiobhÃ¡n McSweeney saying she was "deeply worried" that the government was lagging behind.

"There is a way to work alongside AI and to use it as a tool that benefits us rather than rendering us obsolete," she said.

"Our audiences want that human connection. Not AI."

As well as actors, other signatories include those working in other performing industries.

That includes Scottish singer Sandi Thom, known for her 2006 hit I Wish I Was a Punk Rocker (With Flowers in My Hair).

She said she was signing the letter because her voice was "unique to me and was handed to me at birth".

"Behind that voice is the emotion, the life, the pain, the tears and joy that I've felt along the way," she said.

"Without creativity, we are nothing."

It comes a few months after lawyers warned UK legislation has become "unfit for purpose" because of the advancements of AI tech.

"The law comes close, but it doesn't fully protect your voice, your face or your identity," Dr Mathilde Pavis said in June.

However, some people - for example those who are unable so speak properly because of illness - have welcomed technology that can replicate a person's voice.

Yvonne Johnson, who lost her voice due to motor neurone disease, told the BBC's Tech Life programme in February how having it cloned by AI had "totally blown her mind", and brought her closer to her family, who had forgotten what she sounded like.

Others have gone a step further and used AI not only to replicate a person's voice, but to create a holographic representation of them.

Pam Cronrath, from Washington state, used the tech to surprise mourners at her husband's funeral, where a digital version of her deceased partner addressed those who attended his wake.

"I was completely impressed," she told BBC News. "It stayed with me."

News.title: Police condemn ‘anyone using tragedy as excuse for disorder’ after five cars torched at A66 crash vigil
News.content:

Read our Privacy notice

Police have condemned the behaviour of a crowd after cars were torched and flares set off at a gathering for one of the men killed in a head-on collision with police on the A66.

Footage on social media showed several vehicles on fire at the event, which was reportedly a vigil to remember 23-year-old Michael Cahill, in a field in Haswell, County Durham.

Durham Constabulary said that officers and fire crews were called to a privately-owned field at 5:30pm, and said that the majority of the crowd had travelled from outside the area.

Blue balloons and flares were also released, with one attendee captioning the videos “Rest in Peace Mickey”.

open image in gallery Cars are torched at a vigil for one of the young men killed in Middlesbrough ( Instagram )

Cars could also be seen skidding around the area with a number of people on motorbikes and quad bikes.

Later on Thursday, more videos shared online appeared to show burnt-out cars being moved from the field by a tractor.

Assistant Chief Constable Jon McAdam, of Durham Constabulary, said: “The behaviour we saw at last night’s gathering was completely unacceptable.

“Our officers and the communities of County Durham and Darlington were understandably horrified by the tragedy which unfolded on the A66 last week which resulted in multiple deaths, including two serving police officers.

“We utterly condemn anyone who would use that tragedy as an excuse for disorder and expect the overwhelming majority of the public would join us in doing so”.

Anna Turley, MP for Redcar, said the scenes of vehicles being driven dangerously across fields were “completely unacceptable”.

In a post on Facebook, Home Office minister Ms Turley said: “It puts lives at risk, places even more pressure on our already stretched emergency services and leaves residents frightened and angry in their own communities.

open image in gallery Blue flares and balloons were released for Michael Cahill ( Instagram )

“After everything our area has endured over the past week, I will not accept this kind of behaviour becoming normalised.”

The footage comes after hundreds of police officers were drafted in after a spate of violent incidents in the Teesside town of Middlesbrough, which a local MP said has left people “not feeling safe” going to the shops.

Alec Brown, leader of Redcar and Cleveland Council, said more than 200 extra police officers have been, or will be, deployed from around the country to support Cleveland Police, and that he would be asking the prime minister for more support.

He said officers were “working 20-hour days to ensure the ongoing safety of innocent residents”.

The violent incidents began with the head-on crash on the A66, which killed seven people, including two police officers, on Saturday.

On Wednesday, a fatal house fire a mile away from the crash site took the lives of a seven-year-old girl and her 34-year-old aunt.

open image in gallery Cars were torched at a memorial event for Michael Cahill in a field in Haswell, County Durham ( PA )

A further two incidents on Thursday prompted concerns of further violence, after a vehicle crashed into a wall outside a house in Steele Crescent, South Bank, just minutes away from the other two scenes in the early hours.

At around midday, a 39-year-old was stabbed in nearby Sedgemoor Road, Eston.

A man who lives near the scene of the stabbing said people in the area were “trying to keep our heads down”.

Referring to the postcode that covers Eston and Grangetown and South Bank, among other areas, he said: “TS6 has gone mad, it’s brutal.”

open image in gallery Michael Cahill was one of the five men killed in the A66 collision alongside two police officers ( Facebook )

Police have arrested 17 people following the A66 crash, which followed a police pursuit, charging two of them and bailing the others, as part of investigations into alleged organised crime.

PC Matthew Blades, 37, and PC Tom Clough, 38, died in the head-on collision with a Volkswagen Passat on Saturday.

Cole Worthy, 17, Theo Rae, 17, Makai Saddington, 18, and 23-year-olds Cahill and Jakub Matusiak were also killed in the incident.

Meanwhile, two men have been arrested on suspicion of murder in connection with the fire that killed Natalie McDonald and her niece, Valentina Foster, and injured four others.

President Trump did not brief some senior White House officials ahead of the director of the CIA’s visit to Russia earlier this week, it has been reported.

​John Ratcliffe, the chief of the Central Intelligence Agency, flew to Moscow from Latvia on Tuesday in a visit that had not been publicly announced. Reports, though, of an unmarked U.S. C-17 military cargo plane flying into Russia that day quickly sparked rampant international speculation about the visit.

​U.S. officials told The Wall Street Journal that Trump had sent Ratcliffe personally. The message being given to the Kremlin by Ratcliffe was also not shared with military figures and aides who normally would have been briefed on such a trip.

open image in gallery CIA Director John Ratcliffe's (pictured) visit to Russia was concealed from some senior White House officials by President Trump, according to reports ( AFP/Getty )

​European officials told the publication that Ratcliffe had reiterated that the United States remained committed to NATO’s Article 5.

Article 5 of the North Atlantic Treaty states that an attack on one NATO country would be considered to be an attack on all of its member states.

​On Wednesday, Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov confirmed to reporters in Moscow that Ratcliffe had spoken with Russian intelligence officials during his visit. Russian President Vladimir Putin was briefed on the talks but did not attend a meeting with Ratcliffe.

​Sources told The New York Times that Ratcliffe had visited the Russian capital to warn the country to agree to a deal ending its war with Ukraine before the former country’s economic and military position worsens.

The sources added that Ratcliffe had spoken with Ukrainian officials before meeting Aleksandr V. Bortnikov, the director of Russia’s intelligence service, the FSB.

open image in gallery Alexander Bortnikov (right), the director of the FSB, met with Ratcliffe. President Putin (left) was briefed on the talks but did not attend ( AFP/Getty )

​Ratcliffe also urged Moscow against “overreacting” if it is impacted by sanctions imposed by the U.S. on countries that do not cut economic ties with Iran, sources told Politico. He also pressed officials to stop sharing technology with Iran amid its war with the U.S.

​However, his meeting was "primarily" to warn Russia against attacking a Baltic state specifically, a source said.

​Speaking in the Oval Office on Thursday, the commander-in-chief dismissed concerns that Putin could launch an attack on a NATO country.

open image in gallery Trump said that Putin is ‘not going to attack a NATO territory’ ( AFP/Getty )

​“He’s not going to attack a NATO territory,” Trump said.

​Speaking on The Glenn Beck Program, Trump described Ratcliffe’s visit as “semi-routine.”

​“He’s there, you know, very sort of semi-routine,” the president said. “I hate to disappoint people. We would like to see the war with Ukraine end.”

​Asked if Ratcliffe had visited Russia over concerns that Putin planned to “test NATO resolve,” or gain cooperation with sanctions on Iran, Trump replied: “None of the above.”

The Independent has contacted the White House for comment

Huge amounts of smoke can be seen near Wembley Stadium after a large fire broke out on an industrial estate, forcing a nearby Amazon warehouse to evacuate.

London Fire Brigade (LFB) said 20 fire engines and around 125 firefighters are on the scene in Hannah Close in Neasden.

Residents in the immediate area are told to close doors and windows and stay inside where possible, due to the large amount of smoke. People have also been urged to avoid the area as crews respond to the blaze.

Tube services on the Metropolitan line are fully suspended, and there are “severe delays” on the Jubilee line between Willesden Green and Wembley Park. Rail services into London Marylebone have also been disrupted.

The cause of the fire is not yet known.

Dramatic pictures show huge columns of smoke billowing into the sky over west London.

TfL said tickets will be accepted on London Buses, DLR, Elizabeth line, Mildmay line, c2c and Thameslink services.

Fancy sleeping under the stars this weekend? In my new book, Under the Stars, I’ve explored some of Britain’s wildest, weirdest and most wonderful campsites, from ancient woodlands to secret islands, and from rewilding projects to swimming lakes.

Whether you want to pitch your tent with a view of a beach, park your campervan in the mountains or stay in a remote cabin, I’ve found the perfect spots to sleep wild across England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland.

A great campsite is about more than a nice view and decent loos (although creature comforts are important, too). I’ve picked pitches with a real sense of place, whether there’s amazing wildlife to spot, walks straight from your tent door or centuries of history. These are 10 of the very best British campsites I’d happily return to summer after summer.

open image in gallery The Knepp Estate’s 3,500 acres have been transformed by a rewinding project ( NT/John Miller )

1. Knepp Estate, West Sussex

Few places have changed Britain’s relationship with nature like the Knepp Estate. Once intensively farmed, its 3,500 acres have been transformed into one of the country’s best-known rewilding projects. Camping here means sleeping in a flower meadow surrounded by birdsong rather than traffic, with wildlife safaris and beautiful walks on your doorstep. The campsite is adult-only, so it’s wonderfully peaceful. Creature comforts haven’t been forgotten either, with great showers, outdoor hot baths and even a wild swimming pond on site.

Price per night: £25

2. Pool Bridge Farm, York

If your perfect camping trip revolves around swimming, Pool Bridge Farm is hard to beat. Four freshwater lakes sit at the heart of this campsite, each with its own character, from family-friendly paddling to a 300-metre circuit for serious open-water swimmers. Wood-fired saunas line the shore, while six acres of meadow provide plenty of room to pitch your tent.

Price per night: £20

open image in gallery Robert Baden-Powell held the very first Scout camp on Brownsea Island ( National Trust/Annapurna Mellor )

3. Brownsea Island, Dorset

Ready your neckerchief and three-fingered salute: the island where Robert Baden-Powell held the very first Scout camp in 1907 still feels wonderfully adventurous today. Brownsea Island, in the sheltered waters of Poole Harbour in Dorset, is a patchwork of woodland, heath and lagoons, and one of southern England’s richest wildlife havens. Catch the ferry from Poole and spend the night at Brownsea Island Campsite, with hot showers, a dining shelter and a shop making life under canvas surprisingly comfortable.

Price per night: £39

open image in gallery The path to Scafell Pike can be picked up from Wasdale Campsite ( Harper Collins/Robin Kitchin )

4. Wasdale Campsite, Cumbria

How’s this for a perfect camping day? Wake up in your tent, climb England’s highest mountain, cool off with a swim in its deepest lake and finish with a pint in one of the country’s most remote pubs. Wasdale Campsite sits at the head of one of the Lake District’s most spectacular valleys, with the path up Scafell Pike beginning from your tent door. Afterwards, the famously cold waters of Wast Water are waiting below before you warm up back at the campsite.

Price per night: £24

open image in gallery Bert’s is one of ‘Britain’s most memorable places to camp and eat’ ( Bert’s Kitchen Garden )

5. Bert’s Kitchen Garden, Llŷn Peninsula

Love good grub as much as you love fresh air? This eco-friendly, car-free site in north west Wales is perfect for foodie families. There’s no wifi or electric hook-ups at Bert’s – expect acres of wildflower meadows, composting toilets, excellent showers and a communal kitchen. At the campsite’s heart sits a beautiful restaurant surrounded by the kitchen garden that supplies much of its menu, making this one of Britain’s most memorable places to camp and eat.

Price per night: £46

open image in gallery Llanthony Court Camping is home to a beautifully restored railway carriage ( NT/James Beck )

6. Llanthony Court Camping, Monmouthshire

The soaring ruins of Llanthony Priory rise from the floor of the Welsh Black Mountains like the setting of a Gothic novel. Camping next door at Llanthony Court Camping, in Bannau Brycheiniog National Park (the Brecon Beacons), is pleasingly old-fashioned and affordable. And if tents aren’t your thing, there’s also a beautifully restored railway carriage complete with a wood-burning stove, or an off-grid dome perfect for two on site.

Price per night: £7

open image in gallery Comrie Croft is surf over 231 acres of woodland and meadows ( Comrie Croft )

7. Comrie Croft, Perthshire

Choosing where to pitch is half the fun at Comrie Croft. Spread across 231 acres of woodland and meadows in the heart of Scotland, every corner of this campsite feels different. Families gravitate towards the easy-going Low Meadow, while those after a wilder feel can tuck themselves into the Birch Woods or the car-free Far Away Meadow. Once you’ve settled in, there are miles of walking trails and mountain bike routes on the doorstep, plus the Nowhere Sauna for easing tired legs after a day outdoors.

Price per night: £16

open image in gallery Glenbrittle Campsite is one of the nation’s most spectacular camping spots ( NT/Annapurna Mellor )

8. Glenbrittle Campsite, Isle of Skye

It’s a journey to reach Glenbrittle Campsite – but it’s worth it. After crossing to the Isle of Skye, follow a single track beneath the jagged peaks of the Cuillin Ridge to reach the shores of Loch Brittle. The reward is one of Britain’s most spectacular camping locations. Glenbrittle is super spacious and feels akin to wild camping with its mountain backdrop, albeit with the luxury of hot showers and barista coffee from the campsite cafe.

Price per night: £14

open image in gallery Wild Orcardian is half campsite, half organic farm ( NT/Annapurna Mellor )

9. Wild Orcadian at Wheems Organic Farm, Orkney

You can’t travel much further north in Britain than Orkney – this archipelago of 72 green islands off the north coast of Scotland is closer to the Arctic Circle than it is to London. Catch a ferry or cross a causeway to reach South Ronaldsay, and pitch up at Wild Orcadian. Half campsite, half organic farm, these friendly camping fields come complete with big views of sea and sky – just peg in your tent or park up a campervan on one of their grassy terraces.

Price per night: £25

open image in gallery Castle Ward Caravan Park looks out over the tidal waters of Strangford Lough ( NT/Rob Stothard )

10. Castle Ward Caravan Park, County Down

Castle Ward in Northern Ireland will be instantly recognisable to fans of Game of Thrones as Winterfell, the ancestral seat of House Stark, as the estate provided the backdrop for some of the show’s most iconic scenes. If you want to stay the night in Stark country, set up your own tented castle at Castle Ward Caravan Park, looking out over the tidal waters of Strangford Lough. The campsite has 35 pitches in total, with hard-standing spots for caravans and weatherproof timber pods.

Price per night: £28

Under The Stars: Wonderful Places to Camp and Explore by Sian Anna Lewis (National Trust Books, £16.99) is out now

President Donald Trump’s upcoming Republican midterm convention has been described as a trainwreck by political insiders, with concerns ranging from the exorbitant ticket prices to poor optics, according to a new report.

The convention, the first of its kind, is set to be held at the American Airlines Center in Dallas on September 9 and 10 — just months before the November midterm elections, which are historically viewed as a referendum on the president’s performance in office.

“We are going to celebrate the GREAT AMERICAN COMEBACK, and the incredible successes of the American People who transformed our Country through the America First Agenda,” the president wrote on Truth Social in June when announcing the event. “It will be a RALLY like none other!”

But the upcoming GOP extravaganza, hosted by the Republican National Committee, has been derided as a disaster by some Republican operatives, Puck News reported. One GOP strategist, putting it bluntly, described the event as a “s*** show.”

The ticket prices are one source of discontent. The National Republican Campaign Committee is asking House members to pay $25,000 for themselves and a plus one to attend, according to three sources who spoke to the outlet. The top price is even steeper, with some lawmakers being asked to contribute $100,000 — and few appear eager to attend.

open image in gallery President Donald Trump’s upcoming midterm convention has been criticized for its steep ticket prices and poor optics, according to a new report ( AFP/Getty )

Concerns have also been raised over the fact that corporate donors have been invited to sponsor the event, particularly because no official party business is scheduled to take place. “It’s yet another opportunity to shake down corporate America,” a GOP strategist told Puck News.

The event’s timing has also raised eyebrows, given it is scheduled for the day before the 25th anniversary of the September 11, 2001, terrorist attacks. Trump, whose approval rating remains at historic lows in recent polls, could also prove to be a liability for Republicans running in swing districts.

“Nobody understands why we’re doing a midterm convention,” a campaign strategist said. “It’s just another show that Trump is going to put on to remind the voters that he is sitting there, and maybe they don’t want to be reminded of that.”

open image in gallery The convention is scheduled for September 9 and 10 at the American Airlines Center in Dallas, Texas ( Getty Images )

On top of everything else, the event will compete with the opening game of the NFL regular season, when the Seattle Seahawks are scheduled to face the New England Patriots on September 9. The game is expected to draw a substantial television audience, potentially diverting viewers from the GOP event. NFL games are typically among the top-viewed programs in the U.S. every year and few programs top even regular season games.

On the second day of the convention, the San Francisco 49ers will play the Los Angeles Rams.

Still, organizers, who plan to highlight Trump’s immigration policies and tax cuts, hope the event will help energize GOP voters.

“President Trump turns out voters like no other candidate, and this convention will provide the momentum needed to expand our majorities in November,” RNC spokesperson Natalie Baldassarre told Reuters.

The Independent has contacted the White House for comment.

Michael Carrick has confirmed that new £70 million signing Carlos Baleba will be unable to make his Manchester United debut for around three weeks due to an ankle injury.

Following the summer arrivals of Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans, the 22-year-old completed his move from Brighton on Tuesday to further bolster the midfield.

United director of football Jason Wilcox praised Baleba as "an elite midfielder with immense potential to develop further", but fans face a wait to see him play.

The Cameroon international arrived with an ankle problem, ruling him out of Sunday’s Premier League home fixture against promoted Ipswich and beyond.

"He’s got a little ankle issue, so maybe a couple of weeks or so, maybe three weeks," Carrick said.

open image in gallery Carrick confirmed Baleba is not ready to play yet ( PA Wire )

"We’ll see but we knew that before, so it’s no major issue but it’ll be great to have him back when we can."

Asked if Baleba and Amad Diallo could return before the three-week international break, the United boss said: "It’s obviously new, the break to deal with, but we’ll wait and see.

"We’re hopeful but I don’t want to put any deadlines on it just yet.

"Amad won’t be involved this week. He’ll be out for a little bit longer. Mase (Mason Mount) is back around the group, which was great. Trained this week, so that’s a big positive for us."

Baleba’s injury ruled him out of Brighton’s Conference League fixtures and Premier League opener, with Carrick's timeline pointing to a potential debut against his former club.

United host Albion in the Carabao Cup before travelling to Fulham on September 20 – their final game before hosting Tottenham after the international break on October 10.

Despite the delay, there is strong excitement about what the 22-year-old can achieve at Old Trafford.

"We’re delighted to have Carlos," Carrick said. "I think huge potential, massive potential. I think he’s a really exciting signing for us.

"I think the quality that he has, the attributes that he has that offsets a little bit of the balance of the group that we’ve got. Different strengths, different combinations.

"So, for us to have that, absolutely delighted to have him. I think there’s so much more to come from him as well, which with the player that he already is with that little bit more to come is exciting for us."

open image in gallery United are looking to bounce back after losing to Hull last weekend ( PA Wire )

United are looking for a response after last weekend’s 2-0 loss at play-off winners Hull marked a nightmare start to the season.

Marcus Rashford was introduced at half-time having been granted additional rest after the World Cup, alongside fellow substitutes Lisandro Martinez and Kobbie Mainoo.

"We’ve got a squad to choose from. We’ve got a good squad and we could pick we could pick a variety kind of combinations within the team," Carrick added.

"We’ll pick a team for the weekend but, yeah, certainly the boys are massively in contention."

News.content:

Reform UK plans to bring in draconian new laws which could exclude millions from voting and would make it hard for non-English speakers to take part in elections.

Nigel Farage’s party has published its “Election Integrity Bill” and has demanded that the government take its proposals as amendments to existing legislation going through parliament, but it is almost certain they won’t be.

The Reform UK proposals include removing the historic right to vote of Commonwealth citizens, ensure that election material is only published in languages native to the British Isles, such as English, Welsh or Gaelic, or accessible communication formats such as Braille or BSL.

There is also a proposal to force staff at polling stations to police whether people would have sufficient English to vote.

He also wants to introduce limits on postal voting, and enforce new protections against voter coercion and control – so-called “family voting”.

The purpose of the bill appears to be aimed at excluding people with low levels of English to take part in UK elections.

Farage wants election reform ( Copyright 2026 The Associated Press. All rights reserved )

The double effect of banning non-native British languages from election literature and ending postal voting would make it hard for many to take part in the democratic process.

The proposals are the latest in a raft of nationalist policies, which also include proposals for mass deportations and banning non-British citizens from receiving council housing.

Head of Reform UK’s Department for Preparing for Government Danny Kruger said: “With every election, our democracy is being systematically eroded. Britain’s electoral system - once the envy of the world - now buckles under the strain of uncontrolled immigration. In too many parts of the country, elections have been captured by foreign conflicts and sectarian interests, not by what is best for Britain.

“Reform UK will not stand by while our political system is undermined. Britain should be run in the interests of the British people. That’s why we are introducing these changes to save our democracy.”

Mr Farage, and his allies when he was leader of UKIP, the Brexit Party and now Reform UK, have long had concerns with postal voting, where they have consistently lost out to more established parties, particularly Labour, in by-elections.

In 2019, they claimed that Labour beat the Brexit Party in Peterborough because of election fraud and demanded an investigation by the police.

Critics have argued that the failure of parties led by Mr Farage to have properly organised ground campaigns is the real reason they lose out, rather than their allegations that it is harvesting of ethnic minority groups.

But if postal voting was to be restricted it could exclude millions from taking part in the democratic process. In the 2024 general election almost 10 million people used postal votes.

Reform also alleges that other forms of cheating are being used by their opponents.

Earlier this year they highlighted allegations of so-called “family voting” in the Gorton and Denton by-election won by the Green Party’s Hannah Spencer.

Reform has also opposed lowering the age of voting to 16 in the current legislations Labour is taking through parliament.

Mr Kruger pointed to a House of Commons report in 2012 which stated that Britain’s electoral system made it “childishly simple” to commit fraud as a result of Tony Blair’s reforms which liberalised postal voting.

Reform stated: “These concerns have yet to be addressed, with the arrival of the Boriswave accelerating the undermining of British democracy through massive numbers of non-citizens voting, foreign language-based campaigning, and coercive voting.”

A Labour Party spokesperson said: “This is yet another desperate attempt by Reform to deflect attention from the scandals Nigel Farage and his top team are drowning in. It’s time he came clean with the public over his secret £5 million “gift” and rid his Party of the enormous amount of sleaze and scandals that have come to light.

“The integrity of our democratic system is something Labour will always protect. That’s why we’re taking tough action to safeguard our democracy through the Representation of the People Bill. Meanwhile Reform wants to stop people voting if they go on holiday, despite Nigel Farage having voted by post himself. As ever, it’s one rule for him and another for everyone else.”
