New Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh has sought a lower profile than his predecessors, yet his speech Friday at the central bank's annual conclave in Jackson Hole will be one of the most closely watched in years.

When Warsh last spoke, in a press conference in late July, he sowed confusion about his willingness to lift interest rates to combat stubbornly high inflation. Longer-term borrowing costs rose on fears that inflation could worsen.

What many economists and Wall Street analysts are hoping for is a clear signal on how he thinks the Fed should respond to the ongoing price increases that have caused pervasive gloom for many Americans.

Warsh has said he doesn’t want to provide what analysts call “forward guidance” about whether the Fed will hike or cut rates or stay on hold at upcoming meetings. He argues that it limits the Fed’s flexibility by committing it to a specific policy. He also thinks financial markets have become too dependent on such guidance.

Yet some economists argue that he could say more about his views on Fed policy without tipping his hand about future actions. The stakes are high for Warsh, who took over the Fed chairmanship May 22 after his predecessor, Jerome Powell, completed his term.

Previous Fed chairs have often used speeches at Jackson Hole to address broad questions about interest-rate policy and the economy, or to signal upcoming changes in their approach. In his first Jackson Hole speech in 2018, former chair Jerome Powell discussed the shortcomings behind central banking concepts such as “neutral” interest rates, that neither support nor hinder growth, or maximum employment.

By 2022, with pandemic-era inflation having soared to 9.1%, Powell signaled the Fed would continue to sharply raise interest rates in a fight against runaway prices, and he acknowledged that such maneuvers would bring “pain” to consumers and businesses.

Most analysts expect the Fed will keep rates unchanged when it meets next in mid-September. Wall Street investors, however, are betting the central bank will hike rates by December, according to futures pricing tracked by CME Fedwatch.

Inflation cooled in June and July after spiking in May from soaring gas prices, yet it remains above the central bank’s 2% target. According to the Fed’s preferred measure, it was 3.7% in July.

Questions swirling around Warsh have also been intensified by President Donald Trump’s continued calls for lower interest rates. While Trump has continued to defend Warsh, whom he appointed and who took office May 22, the president has criticized other Fed officials for supporting higher rates.

Trump has also renewed his efforts to remove Fed governor Lisa Cook, who was appointed by former President Joe Biden. Replacing Cook would enable Trump to appoint a majority of the seven-member board. Trump tried to fire her last year but was temporarily blocked by the Supreme Court.

If Warsh does assuage some of these concerns, longer-term interest rates could decline slightly. Those rates have steadily risen in recent weeks because of a range of factors, including burgeoning U.S. government deficits and outsize borrowing by tech firms building AI infrastructure.

The rate on the 30-year Treasury bond reached the highest level in 19 years last week, prompting an unusual effort by Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent to buy back bonds and push the yields lower.

News.title: Champions League draw: Arsenal to renew Mourinho rivalry with Real Madrid tie
News.content:
Hello and welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of the Champions League draw in Monaco, with the 36 teams in this season’s competition finding out their eight league phase fixtures.

The teams will be split into four pots of nine, based on “club coefficient rankings”, with defending champions Paris St-Germain automatically named as the top seed.

Liverpool, Manchester City and Arsenal will be among the teams joining the Parisians in pot one, while the two remaining English teams, Manchester United and Aston Villa, will be in pot two.

Proceedings will begin with a team from pot one being drawn at random, and they will be allocated eight fixtures – four at home and four away – by an automated software. They will face two teams from each pot, with one home game and one away game per pot, while they cannot play a team from their country.

This will be done for all nine teams from pot one, before the same process takes place for pot two teams, though they will already know their pot one opponents. Pot three teams will then find out their pot three and four opponents, before the pot four sides are allocated their fixtures against each other.

This season is the third under the new format, with a league phase instead of a group stage, and Uefa has confirmed that fixtures that have taken place in the league phase of the two previous seasons cannot be repeated this time around.

For example, Liverpool cannot host Real Madrid in the league phase this term after welcoming the 15-time European champions to Anfield at this stage of the previous two campaigns. Andoni Iraola’s side could, however, travel to the Bernabeu for an away meeting with Madrid.

The league phase will kick off on 8 September and will be wrapped up after all teams play at the same time on 27 January. The top eight teams of the league phase progress to the last 16 automatically, while teams that finish between ninth and 24th will be forced to navigate a play-off tie to reach the knockout stages.

The draw is expected to get underway at 5pm.

News.title: England return to proper Test cricket with gritty batting performance
News.content:
Cox unfurled some fine drives and assessed conditions like a veteran, scoring quickly to a run-a-ball 38 but only six more from his next 48 as Pakistan knocked over partners at the other end. It was vital Cox stayed in to stabilise the innings. It is the job of a No 3 to attack or defend; calibrate their game to what is required at the time. Cox, when he played briefly for England in New Zealand two winters ago and before injury cut short his tour, looked to be a player drunk on the Bazball fumes. He was out in a warm-up match against a New Zealand XI in Queenstown hooking and flailing at the ball. This was his second mature performance in a row, an innings of 55 to follow his 73 at Leeds and this was made in much harder circumstances.

Pakistan were better after their Headingley horror show. Mohammad Abbas must feel more at home on a dank London day than he does in Sialkot, and can earn a place on the honours board if he nicks the last England wicket after taking four for 56. Mohammad Ali bowled some jaffas, and some rubbish, for three for 67 and spinner Usman Ali kept it tight and found some turn before losing control as Smith went after him. England still scored at 4.4 an over a reflection of some of the wasted deliveries by Pakistan and 10 no-balls.

Inevitably they were a mixed bag in the field. Three dropped catches were redeemed by a run out and a world-class grab at slip by Salman Ali Agha – captain last week, left out here – to dismiss Cox when he lost his shape trying to hit the ball too hard.

News.title: Ebola response shifts to Congo’s river network
News.content:
Stacked with logs and crammed with hundreds of passengers, the giant barges are nudged day after day along one of Africa’s greatest waterways.

The weeks-long voyage looks sedate, but the tugs are pushing their heavily-laden charges along an unstoppable aquatic superhighway.

Sharing the Congo river with these trade behemoths are canoes, fishing boats and smaller wooden cargo ships.

The river connects the wild east of Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) to the capital Kinshasa, in a vital economic artery and transport corridor nearly 1,100 miles long.

The waterway is a lifeline for passengers, timber, produce and goods. Roads are rare and unreliable, and airfares are far too expensive for most.

Now there are concerns the river risks becoming a conduit for something else heading to the capital of nearly 18 million people: the deadly Ebola virus.

News.title: Great British fry-up implicated in Salmonella outbreak
News.content:
The outbreak, which involved packets of chicken-flavoured instant dried noodles, was traced back to a manufacturing plant near Kyiv, according to an assessment issued by the European Centre for Disease Control (ECDC) in June.

“Epidemiological investigations have found that cases in Denmark, Estonia, Germany, Latvia and Lithuania had consumed flavoured noodle products from the same brand. Investigations have linked the products, which were distributed in several countries, to the same producer in Ukraine,” the ECDC said in a statement at the time.

Another outbreak, which lasted from 2021 to 2024, sickened 174 people in the UK and killed one. It was linked to frozen, steam-cooked chicken breast fillets produced in Ukraine.

Although it is not known if the latest outbreak is linked to Ukraine (the UK also imports eggs from countries including Poland, Spain, and Belgium ), Ukraine sits outside of the EU and Salmonella contamination is common in many of the country’s poultry farms.

A senior figure investigating a connected outbreak of Salmonella in the Netherlands told The Telegraph that the “working hypothesis” among British health officials is that the contaminated products have come from Ukraine.

“In Ukraine, thousands of salmonellosis cases are reported each year. The highest incidence is observed among children,” said a study published in the academic journal Advances in Animal and Veterinary Sciences earlier this year.

“The main sources of the pathogen are eggs, chicken meat, and meat and dairy products. Analysis shows that frequent outbreaks are associated with poor food storage conditions [...] predominantly in the southeastern regions of Ukraine,” added the authors from the Institute of Laboratory Diagnostics and Veterinary-Sanitary Expertise in Kyiv.

Britain’s egg consumption has boomed over the last two decades, with 209 eaten per person on average every year compared to roughly 163 per person in 2000.

The rise is thought to have been driven by a spike in baking during the pandemic, the rise of brunch culture and the rise of a focus on diets rich in protein among the young, according to experts.

News.title: Heading to a festival this weekend? Here’s how to fold down a pop-up tent in 60 seconds
News.content:
A pop-up tent can be pitched in seconds and, theoretically, taken down in less, making them perfect for music festivals, casual camping or even waiting in the queue at Wimbledon overnight.

Their problem is that they’re not actually as easy to put away as they should be. Angle it right, and the tent folds away as easily as it popped up. Approach without a plan, and you’ll find yourself wrangling with a seemingly live tent that refuses to fold back into its circular bag.

Here’s my step-by-step guide on how to put away a pop-up tent in less than 60 seconds, to help you avoid that problem. Watch the video to see exactly how I do it.

1. Unzip the doors

This is to let any air escape. Otherwise, you’ll find it balloons out as you try to fold it.

2. Gather the poles

Find the highest arch on both sides, then pull them together into the middle.

News.title: Savio scores on debut as Spurs cruise past Charlton in Carabao Cup
News.content:
It looked like this was going to be a night for “one of their own”, but Tottenham Hotspur’s latest big-money arrival, Sávio, stole the headlines to crank up the excitement at his new club.

Mikey Moore had set Spurs on their way to what proved a comfortable Carabao Cup success over Championship club Charlton Athletic and heard his name sung by the home fans.

But Sávio stepped off the substitutes’ bench to take the limelight with a late goal just a few days after completing his expensive switch from Manchester City, and head coach Roberto De Zerbi is demanding many more to come.

“A perfect day for him,” said De Zerbi. “His biggest improvement is to increase the number of goals. He is one of the best wingers, but the best wingers score many goals and I spoke with him two days ago, and we put the goal at 10-12 goals.

“We need 10-12 goals from the wingers. Last season, we suffered too much because the number of goals were not enough.”

News.title: German airport worker dies of malaria after mosquito imported on plane
News.content:
Five airport workers in Frankfurt have been infected with malaria and one has died after being bitten by a stowaway mosquito, health officials have said.

The employees are thought to have been infected in early July, but their diagnosis was delayed due to a lack of travel history to malaria-endemic regions, according to the Robert Koch Institute, Germany’s federal agency responsible for disease control.

It is believed that they were bitten by mosquitoes which arrived at the airport on a plane, most likely from Africa, where 95 per cent of global malaria cases are found.

The five surviving airport workers – who are all male and are said to work in different parts of the facility and in different jobs – are undergoing medical care.

Traps have now been installed across the airport in an attempt to catch any remaining mosquitoes and analyse their origin, according to an airport spokesperson.

It is not the first time that Frankfurt Airport, Germany’s busiest travel hub, has recorded a case of malaria, according to the Robert Koch Institute, which added that there was another incidence in 2023.

More than 610,000 people die of malaria every year, the overwhelming majority children under five in Africa who are unable to quickly access treatment.

The disease, which is caused by a parasite carried by infected mosquitoes, is largely curable if treated early with antimalarials.

In Britain and Europe, there are thousands of imported cases of malaria every year reported in returning travellers from Africa and Asia – but local transmission is exceedingly rare.

Of the 5,000 or so cases recorded in Europe every year, typically just five are caught locally – either from an airport or from a non-infected European mosquito picking up the disease from a sickened person and spreading it to others.

Early symptoms include fever, headaches, and chills, which can quickly develop into multi-organ failure.

Vaccines were made available for the first time in 2024 and are licenced for use in young children in Africa, although they are thought to be only between 30 and 50 per cent effective at preventing the disease.

Protect yourself and your family by learning more about Global Health Security

Sports.title: Xabi Alonso gives Chelsea transfer update after relying on shock star in defence
Sports.content:
XABI ALONSO’s Chelsea squad construction masterplan is almost complete.

The Blues finally seem to have struck a fine balance between talented youth and level-headed experience going into this season, with Alonso, 44, admitting Chelsea are “quite close to the plan we had”.



Alonso has bought in experienced heads in the likes of Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson, as well as adding top quality Premier League experience in Morgan Rogers and Maxence Lacroix, who seem to be taking no time at all to adapt to life at Stamford Bridge.

But Chelsea have also had another good window in terms of raking in profitable fees for their unwanted stars, with Nicolas Jackson and Liam Delap gone, and wantaway Enzo Fernandez’s exit seemingly looming.



Dream Team is back, free, and there’s £100,000 up for grabs!

Ahead of facing Brighton on Sunday, Alonso said: “We are quite close to the plan we had. We will see where we finish, if it’s fully executed or there are things still to be done or things we couldn’t do.

“But for sure I think overall the balance of what we have is going to be good. We have to see how the last few days develop. But so far the team is coming together. It is a process that will take time. We are in a good position, with a few more days to see.”

Welbeck, who scored the opener against Luton Town in the Carabao Cup on Thursday night, is unlikely to start against his former club on Sunday.

But even if he doesn’t play at all, Alonso will be relieved that he’s not playing against Welbeck, and is aware of his scoring record against the Blues – with five goals and two assists in eight games for Brighton against them.

When asked about Welbeck, Alonso laughed: “I am aware (of his record) and I am happy he is with us.

“He has many qualities. As a player you see how intelligent he is. He links well. Outside the box he is able to combine, inside the box he is very intelligent to be in the right place. We have seen it tonight.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

“On a daily basis he is a great influence for the rest of the players. He trains really hard. He is raising all the standards in training and that is something we think is very important.”

But it’s not just experience that Alonso has bought in, it seems he is the first Chelsea manager who is going to put faith in academy graduate Josh Acheampong at the back, who started against both Fulham and Luton in different systems.

He has been arguably Chelsea’s best central defender in both games, having been constantly linked with a move away on loan, and now looks set for a breakthrough season under the Spanish boss.

Alonso added: “For me when Josh plays with confidence, with aggression, he has a lot of good attributes for a modern defender.



“He can play in different positions, he is good with the ball, he understands the game. I have seen progression in these few weeks that we have been together and he has played very solid games against Fulham and tonight. We are very happy he is felling this way.

“We need to help him. There will be different moments in the season for sure because we are going to have competition in all positions.”

Sports.title: Chelsea to have TWO of Premier League’s most calamitous goalkeepers in last three seasons on their books
Sports.content:
ROBERT SANCHEZ’s horror show at Craven Cottage appears to have ended his tenure as the Chelsea No1.

The Spaniard, 28, was caught out at his near post when Josh King equalised in the 23rd minute, and palmed an effort straight into the path of Gonzalo Garcia when Fulham netted in the second half.



Thankfully for Chelsea, they still got away with a 3-2 win in Xabi Alonso‘s first competitive game.

But by turning to Emi Martinez, the Stamford Bridge hierarchy may just be subbing out one calamitous keeper for another.



At least that is what the stats suggest.

Because Martinez is far from a flawless, error-free stopper.

In fact, he is only just behind Sanchez on the list of Premier League goalkeepers with the most errors leading to goals in the last three seasons.

And his prospective £7.5million signing from Aston Villa would mean that, if Chelsea keep Sanchez, they will have two of the top-four on their books.

Brighton’s Bart Verbruggen takes the unwanted pole position with a whopping 11 errors leading to goals since the start of the 2023/24 campaign.

He is the only man into double figures, with Sanchez next on eight.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Third-place Aro Muric somehow managed his seven mistakes across just 28 Prem appearances for Burnley and Ipswich.

And then comes Martinez – alongside exiled Newcastle goalie Nick Pope – on six apiece.

Although the error stats do not reflect well on Martinez, he would head to Stamford Bridge with a strong CV.

He won the World Cup with Argentina in 2022 and the Europa League with Villa last season, establishing himself as one of the world’s top keepers.



If the 33-year-old completes his move as expected, attention will turn to how Chelsea reorganise their goalkeeper department.

Sanchez and Blues prospect Mike Penders were expected to battle for the No1 spot this season, and it seems unlikely that either would settle for being third-choice.

Sports.title: Stamford Bridge away allocation announced for Shakhtar Donetsk Champions League matches played at Chelsea’s stadium
Sports.content:
SHAKHTAR Donetsk will cap the number of away fans for their Champions League games in London – in a bid to make them feel like home matches.

The Ukrainians, who have been unable to play on their own soil since the 2022 invasion by Russia, agreed a deal with Chelsea to use Stamford Bridge for their four home games.



While they missed out on hosting any of the Prem’s five representatives, Shakhtar pulled out a plum tie with a home game against Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid, alongside matches with Sporting Lisbon, Fenerbahce and AEK Athens.

That raised the prospect of 35,000-plus Madrid fans swarming into London to see their side in action.



Uefa rules only mandate that clubs sell a minimum of five per cent of tickets to away supporters, with no limit on the maximum number.

But with an estimated 200,000 Ukrainians now living in London, the majority of whom are refugees from the ongoing war, Donetsk have prioritised those supporters rather than seeking to cash in on Spanish interest.

Final ticket details, including prices, are expected to be published early next week but Donetsk will sell only 10 per cent of available seats – adding up to just under 4,500, to visiting supporters.

That should ensure a “home” atmosphere, with Donetsk sporting director, former Croatia wing-back Darijo Srna, explaining: “We want this to be a game for all our fans who now live in the UK.

“We think we will get a full stadium for Real Madrid, hopefully for Fenerbahce too, and good crowds for the other matches as well.

“This is a historical moment for us and there will be a four-match package of tickets for the whole set of games.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“We are looking forward to seeing the Ukrainian flags all over Stamford Bridge.”

Chelsea confirmed Shakhtar would be playing Champions League games at the Bridge in an announcement last week.

The club said: “FC Shakhtar have played in countries across Europe and we look forward to welcoming them to London for their Champions League campaign this year.

“We will be working with the Shakhtar team closely over the coming weeks to ensure that matchdays run safely and smoothly for their team and supporters.”

Shakhtar added: “Playing our Champions League home matches at Stamford Bridge is a special opportunity for Shakhtar.



“We are grateful to Chelsea Football Club for the opportunity to host our games at this special venue.

“Stamford Bridge is one of the most famous stadiums in world football, with an incredible history and atmosphere.

“We are convinced that Shakhtar’s matches in London will provide unforgettable emotions for Ukrainian and English fans.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Talks between the clubs began in July, as the Ukrainians were forced to abandon the Donbas Arena when Russian troops invaded Crimea and a war broke out in the region in 2014.

They have brokered deals with German sides Hamburg and Schalke, and Poland’s Wisla Krakow, in each of the last three seasons.

Sports.title: Como issue update on stunning stadium amid Man Utd fan fears that Champions League tie could be held 150 miles away
Sports.content:
CHAMPIONS LEAGUE rookies Como are confident they will get the green light to host Manchester United at their own home.

But that will lead to a scramble for United fans to get their hands on one of just a handful of available tickets.



Como, coached by former Arsenal and Chelsea midfielder Cesc Fabregas, qualified to join Europe’s elite for the first time as they edged Juventus out of the Serie A top four.

But the northern Italian club completed their greatest achievement while undertaking a major £50million refurb of their 13,000-capacity Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia.



Uefa chiefs have to give the okay for the club to play at home, with the alternative being to move 150 miles to stage matches at Sassuolo’s 21,525-capacity Mapei Stadium.

Playing in Como would mean just a maximum of barely 600 United fans being sold tickets from the official allocation, compared to nealy 1,100 if the game was played in Sassuolo.



Como also host holders Paris Saint-Germain, RB Leipzig and AEK Athens in the league phase.

And president Mirwan Suwarso said: “We’ve put in a lot of work to match Uefa’s standards, so we hope it all goes well.

“This is a surreal experience for us. We were in Serie D just seven years ago – now we’re in Serie A and in the Champions League.

“We can’t believe it. For us, it’s very important just to be here. We think day by day. We’ll try our best and enjoy the moment.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

“So we can only do our best – results will say the rest. The most important thing for us is to enjoy the moment.

“For as much as we would like to say we’d like to experience it again, we must not take it for granted. Perhaps tomorrow we won’t be here.”

It is likely that Como will play their first game away when the fixtures are confirmed on Saturday morning.

That would result in their opening home match not coming until mid-October, allowing more time to complete building works.

Sports.title: Chelsea finally land front-of-shirt sponsor as they agree lucrative deal with US digital currency company
Sports.content:
CHELSEA have ended their search for a front-of-shirt sponsor after striking a big-money deal.

The Blues, who booked their place in the third round of the Carabao Cup with a routine win over Luton Town last night, have announced a lucrative agreement with Circle Internet Group Inc.



And Chelsea’s biggest names, including record signing Morgan Rogers, will now have a fresh look just days into the new season.

Circle and USDC brands are set to appear on the front of the West Londoners’ men’s, women’s and academy shirts.



Chelsea president Jason Gannon has hailed the money-spinning partnership with the American digital currency company.

He said: “This partnership with Circle positions Chelsea at the forefront of football’s digital evolution.



“We are two organisations fixated by the future and are relentlessly innovating to be in the best position possible for the long-term.

“We look forward to beginning our journey with Circle – to introduce Circle to the Chelsea family and continue enhancing how we operate.”

Circle co-founder and chief executive officer Jeremy Allaire added: “We built USDC on the belief that money should work seamlessly for everyone everywhere, the way the internet does.

“Partnering with Chelsea connects us with a global sports community built on that exact same borderless vision.”



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

The Circle and USDC logos will be seen on the front of Chelsea’s strip for the first time against Brighton on Sunday.

The Blues had Swedish artificial intelligence firm IFS emblazoned across their jersey as part of a multi-million-pound agreement in the final months of last season.

But Chelsea did not manage to find a replacement before the new campaign got underway.

Club chiefs had been looking for a long-term front-of-shirt partner since the £40million-per-year deal with mobile phone firm Three ended in 2023.



Chelsea Women chief executive Aki Mandhar said: “We are excited to introduce Circle and USDC to the Chelsea Women family for our inaugural season at Stamford Bridge.

“Forging and facilitating connections between people is what Chelsea Women and Circle do best and we look forward to bringing USDC to the Chelsea Women fanbase and beyond.”

Sports.title: Arsenal ‘in talks with Real Madrid over shock Endrick transfer after missing out on Vinicius Jr’
Sports.content:
ARSENAL have reportedly entered talks with Real Madrid over a shock move for Endrick.

The Gunners are intent on recruiting a forward this summer but top target Vinicius Junior chose to extend his contract at the Bernabeu.



Emirates chiefs suffered a setback earlier in the window when Morgan Rogers signed for Chelsea.

And they are currently having difficulty convincing Atletico Madrid star Julian Alvarez to pick North London over Barcelona.



Endrick, 20, had struggled to build momentum during his first season and a half at the Bernabeu.

But a successful loan spell at Lyon during the second half of last season, where he scored eight goals in 21 games, has put him back on the map.



According to talkSPORT, Arsenal have made an official approach for the youngster and are planning to test Real’s resolve.

Madrid boss Jose Mourinho is a big fan of Endrick and does not want to lose him before the deadline.

The Portuguese said: “He’s a player I like a lot and who has had many contacts from clubs that wanted him on loan or transferred.

“I didn’t want to loan or sell him because I like the player, and I’d like to work with this young player who has important talents.”



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Aston Villa, Liverpool and Roma have also been linked with Endrick.

The Brazilian international, who already has 21 caps for his country, was hailed as the next mega South American talent when Real Madrid agreed a £60million deal to sign him in 2022.

By that point, at 16 years old, he had begun playing regularly for the Palmeiras first-team.

And he had notched 21 goals in 82 games for the club when he left to finally join up with Real in 2024.

CRYSTAL PALACE could play their first Europa League game against the club whose owner prevented them playing in the competition LAST season.

And Euro rookies Bournemouth and Sunderland will BOTH play Italian giants AC Milan in a series of tough-looking fixtures.



The Rossoneri will visit the South Coast with the Wearsiders making the trip to the San Siro.

The Selhurst Park side had qualified for Europe’s second competition by winning the FA Cup in 2025.



But then-Lyon owner John Textor’s “decisive influence” through his shareholding in Palace saw Uefa, pushed by Nottingham Forest, demote the Eagles to the Conference League.

They subsequently won this competition in May to earn their place in this term’s Europa League.

In a twist of fate, the computerised draw in Monaco then sent Palace on a trip to the French side, who missed out on Champions League football with a home defeat to Fenerbahce.

Palace’s other fixtures see home ties with Spaniards Real Sociedad, Sparta Prague, Poland’s Lech Poznan and Germany’s Hoffenheim.

Bournemouth, in Europe for the first time but now under new management with Marco Rose at the helm, will also welcome Viktoria Plzen from the Czech Republic, Sturm Graz and Israel’s Hapoel Beer-Sheva.

Sunderland also meet Milan, but in the San Siro, with home matches against AZ Alkmaar, Dinamo Zagreb, Jagiellonia – the Black Cats also face Poznan, in Poland – and Levski Sofia.

Sports.title: Who is Michael Owen’s son James?
Sports.content:
FORMER England and Premier League star Michael Owen is opening the doors to his private life in the Amazon Prime Video docuseries Meet the Owens.

The six-part show offers viewers an intimate, unvarnished look at family life alongside his wife Louise and their four children.



Michael considers raising their four children – including his only son, James- to be one of his greatest achievements.

Who is Michael Owen’s son James and how old is he?

Michael Owen and his wife Louise welcomed their only son James on February 6, 2006.



He is one of four children – and has siblings Gemma, Emily May, and Jessica.

His mum and dad met in primary school in 1984 and became childhood sweethearts while at Hawarden High School in Flintshire, Wales.

They became engaged on Valentine’s Day in 2004 – which is also Louise’s birthday – when he proposed at their home, and they married the following year.

What is James’ condition, Stargardt?

In 2019, Michael revealed his son James is “clinically blind”.

The retired England striker confirmed his second eldest was diagnosed with Stargardt disease – a degeneration of his retina.

Stargardt typically causes a loss of vision during childhood or adolescence and although there is no cure for it yet, it is rare for people with the disease to lose complete sight.



Speaking to The Times, he said: “He will never be a footballer. My son’s got an eye condition.

“I’ve never said this. I don’t want a big headline.

“Clinically, he’s blind. He’s got Stargardt disease, a degeneration of his retina. I used to go and watch him and bollock him about his positioning.

“He can’t see the ball until it’s five yards away. As much as every father wants their son to play, it is almost a relief to me.

“Everyone always asks, ‘Is he going to be a footballer?’ and then I stand on the side of the pitch and hear, ‘He’s not as good as his dad.'”



What does James Owen do for a living?

Now 20, James works alongside his father at Manor House Stables, the family’s large horse racing and breeding yard near Chester.

He previously co-starred with Michael in the TNT Sports documentary Football is for Everyone, which explored sight loss in sport and highlighted England’s partially sighted futsal team.

He has a large following on Instagram, on his very popular handle @_james_owen10.

Who is James’ sister Gemma?

James’ eldest sister Gemma is an equestrian and was a contestant on 2022’s Love Island.

Since then she has her own fashion line, and is also an Influencer.



In May 2023, Gemma shared an emotional post about her brother James’ eye condition.

The reality star shared a photo of herself smiling alongside her brother and announced that she was the new ambassador for UK charity Fight For Sight, which helps fund research into the prevention and treatment of blindness and eye disease.

“When my brother James was around 8yo he was diagnosed with a rare genetic disease called Stargardt Disease,” she said.

“This condition progressively deteriorates vision from the macula and currently there is no cure or treatment.

“Having closely witnessed how sight loss has affected him personally, I am honoured to announce that I am now an ambassador for Fight For Sight.”



Gemma admitted the charity is very important to her and her family as she prepares to undertake her new job.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“This UK charity is funding research into the prevention and treatment of blindness and eye disease and has a special place in all of my family’s heart,” Gemma continued.

“I’m looking forward to working with them to help raise funds and awareness for research and developments in treatments for people with Stargardt Disease and other conditions causing blindness.”

Sports.title: Mercedes confirm Russell grid penalty - but where will he take it?
Sports.content:
Mercedes have confirmed George Russell will take a grid penalty for exceeding his engine allocation, but are yet to decide which race to serve it at.

Championship leader Kimi Antonelli will start at the back of the field at the next Formula 1 race in Italy next weekend, but Russell will also face the same repercussions at a race later this season.

Despite having the best car for the majority of this year, both Mercedes drivers have suffered from engine unreliability and will need more than the four allotted power units for this season, thus incurring grid penalties.

"We have not finalised where George will take his penalty, but both drivers will be affected," said Mercedes deputy team principal Bradley Lord on the team's Nu Silver Arrows Radio Show.

"George retired in Canada, Kimi retired in Barcelona, and George also stopped at the end of qualifying in Hungary. Had that happened in the race, the impact could have been much greater.

"We must manage the remaining events so that both cars reach the end of the season with the freshest and best-performing hardware possible. It is a constant trade-off between the risk of running high-mileage components and the points cost of taking a grid penalty and recovering through the field."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player An unfortunate power unit failure for George Russell sees him out of the Canadian Grand Prix

Antonelli leads Russell and Lewis Hamilton by 59 points in the Drivers' Championship with 11 scheduled events remaining, although there is uncertainty about the final races on the calendar in Qatar and Abu Dhabi.

Lando Norris, the winner of the last two races, is 83 points behind Antonelli and could make further inroads at the Italian Grand Prix next Sunday.

Mercedes trackside engineering director Andrew Shovlin says the team will continue to assess where Russell takes his grid penalty.

"Every race adds mileage and learning across Mercedes and the customer teams. Components are checked continually, and we assess whether previous containment measures have solved the underlying issues," he said.

"Our confidence in running a power unit to a sixth or seventh event may be higher in a few races than it is today, so the plans are reviewed after every weekend."

Image: The F1 Drivers' Championship ahead of the Italian Grand Prix

Are F1 budget cap rules the reason for Mercedes' lack of development?

Following their double podium at Zandvoort, Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff revealed the Silver Arrows do not have the money to respond to the growing threat from McLaren and Ferrari.

Mercedes have lost their early-season pace advantage and have brought the fewest developments of the front-running teams this season.

On the FIA's upgrades declaration sheet, Mercedes have fitted 24 new parts to their car compared to 37 for Red Bull, 38 for McLaren and 40 for Ferrari.

Since 2021, F1 has had financial regulations which limit the teams' budget they can spend each year to ensure costs do not get out of hand.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mercedes team-mates Kimi Antonelli and George Russell reflect on their Dutch Grand Prix race

Lord suggested the budget cap regulations and Mercedes putting more money into the car at the start of this year means they have less resource for in-season development.

"It is the reality every team faces under the cost cap. Formula 1 organisations must balance headcount and salary costs against the money available for hardware," he explained.

"They must consider how much of the current car was produced this year rather than last, how many spare parts to manufacture and how much stock to carry at the factory and with the race team.

"Every team is trying to find the optimum balance. We continue to find performance in the wind tunnel, but the challenge is deciding when to convert that virtual gain into real parts. With a floor, for example, do you manufacture a new one as soon as performance is found, or align the upgrade with the point at which a fresh floor is required simply to complete the season? Finding those efficiencies is the art within the science.

"A team in catch-up mode may make different choices from one that is leading. By the time we race in Mexico, Brazil and Las Vegas [in November], it does not necessarily follow that another team will have introduced more total performance. It may simply have released it in smaller, more frequent steps."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mercedes team-mates Kimi Antonelli and George Russell reflect on their Dutch Grand Prix race

Shovlin also hinted Mercedes could already be looking at next year's car concept, which is another reason behind their development plan.

"If we believed these [2026] championships depended on having an update at Zandvoort, we would probably have found a way to achieve it," he said.

"We are in the enviable position of leading, so it is logical not to throw as many parts at the current car as competitors who are chasing. We must remain competitive this year while also thinking about the next championship.

"Being in front allows a little more long-term thinking. We have made calculated decisions about the most cost-efficient route to the end of the year. After every race, however, we reassess whether we are doing enough, bringing enough and whether anything can be pulled forward."

Sports.content:
With the flat season building to an exciting crescendo, the Weekend Winners team have taken a look at some ante-post fancies for the Prix de l’Arc de Triomphe, the Leger and the Ayr Gold Cup.

The long-awaited arrival of rain should add plenty of intrigue for form studiers as attention turns to Doncaster's Classic in September and then to Paris for the Arc in early October.

Host Kate Tracey was joined by regular sidekicks Declan Rix and Sam Boswell as they looked for some long-range fancies.

Sports.title: Italian GP: Schedule and how to watch on Sky Sports
Sports.content:
The 2026 Formula 1 title race is set to heat up at the Italian Grand Prix as championship leader Kimi Antonelli will start at the back of the grid due to a power unit change.

Antonelli leads George Russell and Lewis Hamilton by 59 points in the Drivers' Championship but his biggest threat may now come from Lando Norris, who is 83 points behind, but has won the last two races.

Given Antonelli is highly unlikely to win at Monza, it provides a big opportunity for his title rivals to make inroads into their championship deficits.

Ferrari will have huge support from their home crowd, the Tifosi, and are also expected to run new engines in Hamilton and Charles Leclerc's cars - but will not suffer grid penalties.

They hope the extra power will get them back to winning ways after disappointment in Hungary and the Netherlands, tracks Ferrari were predicted to be strong at.

Max Verstappen won last year's Italian Grand Prix and Red Bull could be back towards the front this weekend due to their strong engine.

Image: The F1 Drivers' Championship ahead of the Italian Grand Prix

Italian GP track - Monza

Monza is one of the four current tracks that feature on the original 1950 F1 World Championship calendar - Monaco, Silverstone and Spa-Francorchamps being the others - and is known as the Temple of Speed thanks to its long straights.

The prime overtaking spot is into the Turn 1 chicane but the battle often continues through the Curve Grande and into Turn 4.

After that comes two 90-degree right handers, known as the Lesmos, before another long straight towards the Ascari Chicane, then the final corner, commonly called Parabolica.

Italian GP weather in Monza

The current weather forecast suggests rain will not affect the on-track action at Monza with sunny skies across all three days of running with air temperatures at around 30C.

Sports.title: Chelsea prepared to sell Fernandez to Man City for right price
Sports.content:
Chelsea are prepared to sell Enzo Fernandez to Manchester City for the right price - and if they can improve their squad before the window closes.

There are not believed to have been any club-to-club talks between City and Chelsea yet, but Fernandez was left out of Thursday night's Carabao Cup win over Luton.

Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso said after the game that Fernandez is a "good professional" who has been training well, and a decision on whether he will be available for Sunday's clash with Brighton will be taken nearer the time.

Man City's interest continues despite missing Chelsea's August 14 deadline to bid for Fernandez.

Image: Fernandez ranked highly in a number of attacking metrics last season

Chelsea had agreed with Fernandez's representatives that he could be sold for £120m by that deadline but an offer never arrived.

Alonso also said ahead of the Luton game they are "prepared for whatever" happens with any players who could leave before the deadline.

Among the players Chelsea are considering to bring in midfield are Bournemouth's Alex Scott and Crystal Palace's Adam Wharton. Both clubs consider those players unsellable, however.

City also have Scott as a midfield target as well as Roma's Manu Kone.

Reinforcing central midfield has become an even bigger priority for City following Rodri's departure to Barcelona earlier this month.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the La Liga match between Barcelona and Athletic Club

Nico Gonzalez has just left to join Newcastle in a transfer worth up to £50m, with Tijjani Reijnders recently departing for Al Qadsiah for £51m. Bernardo Silva also left City following the expiry of his contract and has since joined Real Madrid.

City this week completed the signing of Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille with the midfielder moving to the Etihad Stadium for £86m in a world-record deal for a teenager.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Enzo Maresca praised the signing of Ayyoub Bouaddi and believes the player will be a valued asset at Manchester City.

England international Elliot Anderson joined City in a £116m deal from Nottingham Forest last month.

Why Alonso left Fernandez out against Luton

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso refused to be drawn on whether star midfielder Enzo Fernandez will be moving to Premier League rivals Manchester City

Alonso confirmed in his post-match press conference that he took the decision to leave Fernandez out of the matchday squad for Thursday night's Carabao Cup second-round win over Luton.

"It was just because of the game," Alonso said in his press conference after the win.

Image: Enzo Fernadez's positional performance last season

"We have other players who need minutes."

Asked when he decided Fernandez would not play against Luton, Alonso replied: "In the afternoon. It's a decision that I took.

"Enzo is a good professional. He's training well and I have nothing to say about this. It was just decisions that we have to take thinking about the game that we were playing tonight. We will see for Sunday."

Chelsea have agreed a deal worth £7.5m with Aston Villa to sign Emi Martinez.

Sky Sports News reported Chelsea were considering a late move for Martinez after current No 1 Robert Sanchez came under criticism after his error in Monday's win at Fulham.

Martinez has needed to find a new club after Villa signed Zion Suzuki from Parma for nearly £30m.

He was the subject of interest from Juventus but they chose to sign Guglielmo Vicario from Spurs.

Question marks will now be raised over whether both Sanchez and Mike Penders will remain at Stamford Bridge for the season.

Penders started Chelsea's Carabao Cup tie with Luton on Thursday night, after Sanchez started v Fulham.

Sports.title: 'I fought Serrano on 15 days' notice - I'm even better now!'
Sports.content:
Fortune can favour the bold in boxing and Reina Tellez is riding the momentum of her own valour as she steps onto the world stage once more.

The 23-year-old made a name for herself back in January when she agreed to fight seven-division champion Amanda Serrano on just 15 days' notice, going the distance in a points defeat to the Puerto Rican icon.

Now Tellez, hailed as a 'warrior' by Serrano for her performance, is preparing to face Jessica Barry on the undercard of Mikaela Mayer and Chantelle Cameron's main event at MVPW-06 in Birmingham this Saturday.

"I believe in myself and I have a lot of heart. This is something I've always wanted to do, ever since I was a child," Tellez told Sky Sports.

"Having somebody that I watched growing up (Serrano) and then having the opportunity to fight her, it meant so much to me. And to make my family proud and to prove something to myself. So I took it considering the short time.

"I had a great outcome, even though it wasn't a win. I got a lot of things from that fight. Like I said, I'm grateful."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Alycia Baumgardner took everyone by surprise including Mikaela Mayer as she grabbed the mic and asked her former rival a question at the press conference

Tellez, who is 13-1-1 (5 KOs) as a professional, had previously been scheduled to face Juliana Vanesa Basualdo on the Stephanie Han vs Holly Holm 2 card in May, however the fight did not go ahead.

She now features on a landmark bill as MVP celebrate their fifth anniversary this weekend, Tellez crediting her decision to fight Serrano at last-minute notice as a catalyst for her latest opportunity to shine.

"The Serrano fight got me on a platform like I am today. For that, I'm extremely grateful," she continued.

"I feel like without that fight, I wouldn't be able to see the things that I need in my life and in my career to keep being successful and keep being Reina. It taught me a lot as a boxer and as a person.

"It means a lot to me. I'm not the same fighter that I was when I fought Amanda Serrano, and even my fights before that, I feel like I've really evolved.

"So to see how much better I've got over the past couple of months and the changes that I've made that I can showcase in the ring, it means a lot to me. This fight means so much to me, my family and my team. So I'm grateful for it."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Caroline Dubois was not shy about talking to Amelia Moore at their head to head and the American didn't appear to be enjoying the long conversation!

Serrano recently clinched the 50th win of her professional career with a majority decision victory over Lucrecia Manzur to retain her WBA and WBO featherweight titles.

The fight had been broadcast live on TikTok and drew a total of 3.4m views across the night.

"You look at everything she (Serrano) has done, she's done a lot for the sport," said Tellez. "She's a world champion for a reason. So you have to always give respect to her too."

Tellez fell into boxing as a child growing up in Vero Beach, Florida having regularly watched the sport on television while also seeing her uncle train at the local gym. It would later prompt her to relocate in order to further her career inside the ring.

"I told them I wanted to box, and at first they didn't want to because I'm the only girl in the family," she said.

"And then they took their chance on it, they took me to the gym and since then I've just been boxing."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Chantelle Cameron says Mikaela Mayer's pre-fight talk is a sign of lacking confidence and she's certain of winning a close contest in Birmingham

These days she operates out of San Antonio, Texas as one of two fighters alongside Miranda Reyes to represent a state boasting its fair share of boxing greats this weekend.

"Texas is big, boxing is huge in Texas, that's one of the main reasons I actually moved to Texas," she continued.

"It's just crazy to see people that I've known since even as a kid be here. And I'm happy for everybody who comes from where I come from to be able to get the opportunity. So best of luck to Miranda and to me."

Texas takeover incoming?

"For sure."

Sports.title: Aston Villa’s squad is crumbling while Spurs splash out. Are the financial rules fair?
Sports.content:
In theory Aston Villa supporters should have been rubbing their hands together at the prospect of a Champions League season. Equally, Tottenham fans could have been despondent after a relegation battle that went to the wire. A 17th-place finish meant Spurs earned about £35m less in Premier League merit payments, which are based on final league position, than Villa.

Yet the mood in the two camps is reversed. Spurs have spent an estimated £322m in the transfer window, and that excludes the loan of Manchester City’s Omar Marmoush, for whom they are committed to paying £55m after this season. Sales have reduced the outlay to a net £140m, but Spurs fans seemed buoyant, at least until the first match, when they were soundly thrashed by one of the data scientists’ teacher’s pets, Brentford.

Villa, on the other hand, have had a dispiriting summer in the transfer market. Morgan Rogers, Ezri Konsa, Youri Tielemans are the headline departures, Chelsea have agreed a £7.5m deal for Emiliano Martínez and a seemingly want-away Ollie Watkins may follow, probably offsetting money expected to be spent before Tuesday’s deadline, including on Nicolas Jackson and a centre-half. Over the course of the past five seasons Villa’s net spend on transfers is £3m, the second lowest in the Premier League. Only the other the data scientists’ teacher’s pets, Brighton, who beat Villa 4-0 last weekend, have had a lower net spend during that period.

Villa have finished ahead of Spurs for the past four seasons – narrowly in the first two, then by 11 and 13 places. They are coming off a memorable campaign, having won the Europa League, as Spurs did a year earlier, and secured a top-four berth. But as the former Villa player and lifetime fan Gabby Agbonlahor says: “How can an Aston Villa fans ever dream, in my lifetime, of fighting to lift the Premier League?”

Villa’s owners are Nassef Sawiris, who according to Forbes is Egypt’s richest man, and Wes Edens, the owner of the Milwaukee Bucks and also a multibillionaire. The two bought Villa in 2018 when the club was in crisis under the ownership of Tony Xia. But unlike Chelsea under Roman Abramovich and Manchester City under Sheikh Mansour in the years before cost control rules, they have been limited in their ability to spend as much money as they wish on the club.

The reason behind the spending restrictions has been the cost control environment that operates under Uefa and the Premier League. Introduced nominally to reduce debt in European football, the initially named financial fair play (FFP) had nothing to do with fairness. The FFP rules were then, in a Windscale-to-Sellafield-style ceremony, renamed profitability and sustainability rules (PSR), and had little to do with profitability or sustainability.

The rules encouraged the rise of the creative football accountant, masters of monetary chicanery, who were sometimes successful, occasionally not, at finding loopholes in the rulebook. These rules domestically meant that clubs could lose up to £105m over three years, subject to various adjustments.

In 2023-24 Uefa announced a change to its rules, and the brave new world of squad cost ratios (SCR) was introduced. SCR limits a club’s spending on squad costs to 70% of football revenue. Squad costs are defined as first-team player wages, amortisation (transfer fees spread over the contract life, so a £50m signing on a five year deal has an amortisation cost of £10m a year), impairment (don’t ask unless you are studying an accounting course) and agent fees.

Football revenue is in effect matchday ticket sales, broadcast income and commercial activities. It excludes the ‘Chelsea Way’ accounting method of selling club-owned real estate, women’s teams and anything else owned by the club to another company controlled by the club owners to generate additional profit.

The old cost control rules still operate in the background, limiting total losses for clubs in Uefa competitions to €60m over three years. The Premier League has followed suit, except it allows the remainder of its clubs to spend 85% of football revenue on squad costs. The Premier League rules also have added to the football fan vocabulary phrases such as sustainability and systemic resilience, green and red thresholds and negative feedback loops (not the ones seen on social media after a weekend defeat).

As a consequence, clubs have an incentive to generate as much revenue as possible, because for every £100 of revenue at least £70 can be invested in the squad. Provided the money is spent well it gives the richer clubs an edge in terms of results. This is why Spurs have such an advantage over Villa and many other ambitious/aspirational clubs in the Premier League such as Newcastle, Forest, Leeds and Everton. Daniel Levy, Spurs’ much maligned former chair, was visionary in the move from White Hart Lane to the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

View image in fullscreen Hosting NFL matches at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium has helped to boost the club’s revenue. Photograph: Ant Upton/AP

Spurs have been transformed from a football club to a multi-sport, multi-function entertainment group, which, importantly, has nearly all its profits from NFL matches, boxing bouts and summer concerts falling within the definition of football revenue.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The non-football events have proven so lucrative that Spurs are partly inoculated from a poor season on the pitch and/or non-participation in Uefa competitions. Since the stadium move commercial revenue has increased from £59m to £277m in 2024-25, a season in which Spurs played in the Europa League instead of the Champions League. Villa were in the Champions League with all the attention that brings but made £98m from commercial activities.

Spurs also have the benefit of London pricing. In 2024-25 the club generated an average of more than £82 per fan per match, compared with Villa’s £38, again despite being in a less prestigious competition.

The difficulty for Villa is that to challenge for the Premier League or Champions League title they need to invest in players. If they spend too much they are subject to restrictions. Villa failed Uefa’s rules and have been fined twice for breaches and forced to follow a business plan that curtails their ability to spend in the transfer market unless they first sell.

A problem for them is that it has cost a lot to improve the squad, with the wage bill rising from £108m in 2019-20 to £273m in 2024-25, including as bonuses for Champions League participation kicked in. This is big by the club’s historical standards but still some way behind other members of the “Big Six”, who can offer attractive packages to Villa players.

Villa generated £378m in revenue last time they were in the Champions League, and 70% of that is an SCR spend of £265m, but that compares with a £445m average SCR spend of the “Big Six”.

Critics of the rules say that it creates a closed shop, because only those clubs who have big stadiums and associated commercial benefits can compete for the best talent, often sourced from clubs such as Villa. Agbonlahor sums it up: “Clubs should be allowed to go to the next level. It’s very frustrating and very annoying to be a Villa fan at the moment.”

Kieran Maguire is professor of football finance at the University of Liverpool.

Sports.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
Sports.content:
1 Guéhi versatility crucial as Bouaddi arrives

Enzo Maresca has a shiny new £85m midfielder he could select for a debut but he may want Ayyoub Bouaddi, at 18 years old, to have a bit of time watching on from the bench to learn about the Premier League from his elders. The Moroccan may not have expected one of those to be a centre-back by trade. Marc Guéhi will be eager to make a triumphant return to Crystal Palace and may well have the opportunity to do so from central midfield, where he played last weekend in the victory over Bournemouth, scoring the equaliser. The centre-back was a surprise selection in the blocker role next to Elliot Anderson, but equipped himself admirably and was not limited to the dirty work, often being found in more advanced positions in open play and happy to have the ball at his feet. His long-term future is unlikely to be outside defence but further proof of Guéhi’s adaptability will be a positive for Maresca, as a long season awaits. Will Unwin

Crystal Palace v Manchester City, Friday 8pm (all times BST)

2 Liverpool need to stop Gibbs-White

“It is just not personnel,” insisted Andoni Iraola in response to Liverpool conceding two goals to quick Newcastle transitions in his first Premier League game as the club’s head coach. Some long-term faults cannot be rectified overnight – although that did not prevent some hysterical reactions to the performance at St James’ Park – and, with Liverpool prioritising wingers in the final days of the transfer window, the answer to this particular weakness, as Iraola indicated, lies on the training ground. Morgan Gibbs-White revelled in the spaces behind Liverpool’s midfield last season as he – and set pieces – helped Nottingham Forest to a second successive league win at Anfield. Iraola does not want to curb Ryan Gravenberch’s attacking instincts but greater tactical discipline and willingness to do the dirty work from the entire Liverpool midfield will be needed to stop Gibbs-White producing a repeat performance. Forest’s new record signing, Liam Delap, has also been registered in time to play. Andy Hunter

Liverpool v Nottingham Forest, Saturday 12.30pm

3 Everton note Cherries’ set-piece struggles

There were so many encouraging takeaways for Bournemouth despite an agonising late defeat at Manchester City. The catalyst for City’s turnaround was Marc Guéhi’s 84th-minute equaliser, the England defender heading in unmarked at a corner, after wasting a near-identical earlier chance. For Bournemouth, it was a familiar source of pain; only Liverpool conceded more set-piece goals in the top flight last season (20), with the Cherries and Crystal Palace both conceding 18. Bournemouth sought to address their vulnerability in the summer by hiring their first dedicated set-piece coach in Nicolas Gagnon, who worked with Canada at the World Cup and previously at Southampton and in Saudi Arabia. Only Arsenal, Manchester City, Manchester United and Aston Villa claimed more points away from home than Everton last season and David Moyes’s centre-backs, Jarrad Branthwaite and James Tarkowski, will be licking their lips if Bournemouth do not sharpen up their act. Ben Fisher

Bournemouth v Everton, Saturday 3pm

View image in fullscreen Bournemouth were again undone by a set-piece goal as they lost 2-1 at Manchester City. Photograph: Darren Staples/AFP/Getty Images

4 Too early for a relegation six-pointer?

Contrasting opening weekends for Coventry and Hull, harsh reality dealt out against the dream scenario lived out. At Arsenal, Coventry were well beaten by the champions, while in East Yorkshire, Manchester United were soundly, deservedly, defeated. Despite contrasting starts, both teams remain warm favourites for relegation. Two defeats in a row for Frank Lampard’s team would dim the optimism of a summer of expectation. Hull seek to extend the reverie of last week though Coventry are unlikely to be caught as cold as United last week, and surely cannot defend set pieces so badly. The last three Championship matches between these two teams ended in draws, last season’s meetings goalless, although both squads have since been upgraded by brisk transfer business. At Hull, much is expected of Lucas Herrington, who missed Australia’s fateful penalty against Egypt at the World Cup. The teenage defender shone against Stoke in the Tigers’ successful midweek Carabao Cup assignment. John Brewin

Coventry v Hull, Saturday 3pm

5 Tottenham keen for Tonali to tick

It has not taken long for Sandro Tonali to be reunited with his former teammates. After succumbing 3-0 on the opening weekend at Brentford, a home victory will be the minimum requirement for Tottenham. Roberto De Zerbi and his players will be desperate to show that things have changed after a busy summer in the transfer market. Tonali will be a key part of that; he was the only central midfielder who made it past half-time in west London, so at least has minutes in his legs to build on. The Italian will be eager not to suffer at the hands of a team that served him well after bringing him to England. Tonali is supposed to make his new team tick and a rousing home debut would do a lot for everyone’s confidence, while defeat would bring plenty more questions. WU

Tottenham v Newcastle, Saturday 5.30pm

View image in fullscreen Sandro Tonali (left) faces his old club Newcastle after a difficult debut against Brentford. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

6 Acheampong fights to stay with Blues

This is an important moment in Josh Acheampong’s development. The 20-year-old academy graduate did not have many opportunities last year but he started in Xabi Alonso’s back three when Chelsea beat Fulham on Monday. It was a big vote of confidence from Alonso in the young defender, who played well, and may indicate that Acheampong will stay at Stamford Bridge this season. Several clubs are interested in the England youth international and there is talk of a loan before the transfer window shuts, but Acheampong would strengthen his position further if he is selected again for Sunday’s home game against Brighton. Jacob Steinberg

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Chelsea v Brighton, Sunday 2pm

7

On Monday night, Jamie Carragher told a Sky Sports audience that he thought Sunderland might be relegated this season. The former Liverpool defender compared Régis Le Bris’s team to the Sheffield United side managed by Chris Wilder that went down in 2020-2021 – their second season after promotion – and suggested Sunderland were “arrogant”. How will Le Bris’s players respond against Fulham at the Stadium of Light on Sunday? Has the moment arrived to end a winless Premier League run against the west London club stretching back 12 years? If there are legitimate concerns about the ability of Le Bris’s players to cope with a Europa League campaign, regular Sunderland watchers struggle to buy into the accusations of arrogance, let alone the analogy with a very different Sheffield United side. Nonetheless, last Saturday’s 2-1 defeat at Ipswich has prompted a certain anxiety, leaving Wearsiders hoping Nordi Mukiele is fit enough to raise defensive standards. Louise Taylor

Sunderland v Fulham, Sunday 2pm

View image in fullscreen Sunderland fans have bristled at Jamie Carragher’s prediction for their team’s season. Photograph: Dylan Martinez/Reuters

8 Leeds look to strengthen as Bees buzz

Subplots abound at Elland Road as Leeds and Brentford meet after two wins apiece from their first competitive matches of the season. There is the goalkeeping beauty contest between Daniel Farke’s showpiece summer signing, James Trafford – who has two clean sheets in his opening games – and Brentford’s Caoimhín Kelleher. Further forward, fans can ponder the question of which centre-forward, the Leeds favourite Dominic Calvert-Lewin or his opposite number, Igor Thiago, will prove the more incisive. Similarly, the technical area tactical duel involving Daniel Farke and Keith Andrews looks extremely hard to call. Away from the pitch, Farke is hoping to win a race with Sunderland to sign Marseille winger Igor Paixão for about £30m as the Leeds manager urges his board to strengthen. “I’m happy with my group and my signings so far,” said Farke. “But we know we can definitely improve our squad. That is what Leeds supporters and Leeds United deserve.” LT

Leeds v Brentford, Sunday 2pm

9 Carrick under pressure to deliver

Manchester United are bloody-nosed and Ipswich definitely delighted after the tale of each team’s results on the opening weekend. At Hull, Michael Carrick’s team played with zero cohesion and conviction and went down to a miserable 2-0 loss. At Portman Road, Gary O’Neil’s side hosted Sunderland and claimed a rousing late 2-1 win, so arrive at Old Trafford with a bounce in the step. Carrick has to lift his men and get a result – preferably victory. A loss, at home, to another promoted team, would begin the latest inquiry into a United manager: a predicament suffered by all of Sir Alex Ferguson’s successors. Jamie Jackson

Manchester United v Ipswich, Sunday 4.30pm

10 Villa fans bid farewell to Konsa

At a time when the manner of a player’s departure feels particularly pertinent, especially at Aston Villa, Ezri Konsa can expect a warm reception on his return. Konsa could make his Arsenal debut at Villa Park against his former club, where he excelled across seven seasons. A £12m buy from Brentford in 2019, Konsa surely represents one of their finest signings in the Premier League era. He joined fresh from a single season in the Championship with Brentford and left as an England regular and a Europa League winner. Konsa’s role in Villa’s recent success should not be overlooked. Unai Emery can be judged by Villa’s extraordinary run of league finishes – seventh, fourth, sixth and fourth – but also his track record of turning promising talents, such as Konsa, into fully fledged internationals. BF

Sports.title: Forget H2H records: are Premier League games now about the manager’s form?
Sports.content:
New managers are facing an almost one-in-two chance of being fired before the end of the season, a finding from Guardian analysis that shows 22 of the last 50 permanent Premier League managers to leave their roles lasted less than a year.

The betting markets reflect this reality. Six of the eight Premier League managers deemed most likely by bookmakers to be next to leave their post were appointed in 2026. Football management is a very precarious employment position. It looks inevitable that some of the 11 men who have only been in their role since earlier this year will fall before the final hurdle of the 2026-27 season – even if none of them are the first to move on.

Vítor Pereira, Graham Potter and Thomas Frank became managers of Wolves, West Ham and Tottenham respectively in 2025, started last season in those roles and yet were removed by mid-February of this year at the latest. Across the preceding decade, 25 men who started a season as a new manager, appointed in that year, did not see out the season in question.

Uncertainty reigns because managerial turnover is so high, making predictions near-impossible. Nottingham Forest are at Anfield on Saturday; they have recently done well at Liverpool, winning their last two visits. The first of those, in September 2024, was the only Premier League defeat the Reds suffered in the first 30 games of what became a title-winning campaign. Arne Slot mentioned it in interviews for months afterwards, so bothered by the loss. But a lot has changed since then. The visitors were managed by Nuno Espírito Santo for the first of their two recent Anfield wins, Sean Dyche for the second. Forest are already on to their second manager since the latter was dismissed. Even allowing for Evangelos Marinakis’s volatile style of manager retention, the theme of rapid turnover of head coaches pervades the Premier League in 2026.

View image in fullscreen Nottingham Forest have had four managers since Nuno Espírito Santo’s sacking in September of last year. Photograph: Peter Cziborra/Reuters

All of which raises an interesting question. Where once we might have looked at the head-to-head record between two clubs ahead of a clash to get a feel for what might unfold, should we now focus on the managers instead? What they bring tactically and how quickly they can implement their ideas is increasingly relevant at the top level of English football.

Nottingham Forest’s Oliver Glasner makes for an ideal case study, not least because he is among the favourites to be the next Premier League manager to leave his post. He has a fantastic record against Liverpool, winning four of his seven matches in all competitions against them including a successful penalty shootout in the Community Shield). He only has three victories in 21 total games against Manchester United (two wins), Manchester City (one), Arsenal and Chelsea (both none). Glasner cracked Slot’s tactical code in a way he has not yet for the managers of most other big clubs.

But Glasner has a poor record against Liverpool’s new head coach, Andoni Iraola. From the five matches in which their Crystal Palace and Bournemouth sides met, the latter took two wins, three draws and kept four clean sheets. As they were 2-0 and 3-2 up in an eventual and eventful 3-3 draw at Selhurst Park last season, Iraola’s grip over Glasner could have been tighter still. How strongly that dominance comes into play this weekend is not easy to divine. Liverpool appeared very much like last season’s flawed side under Slot in their 2-2 draw at Newcastle last weekend. Their new manager has much work to do.

Glasner’s issues with Bournemouth may not improve this season. He and Marco Rose are each the manager the other has faced most often, their paths having crossed on 16 occasions. Rose dominates the win count by nine to two in what is the most frequent head-to-head among the 190 possible combinations of two current Premier League managers.

Only just over half of those potential matchups have previously occurred (97), even though the men leading Premier League clubs have collectively faced almost 1,700 different managers. Multiple coaches with no experience in England taking up positions this summer has left lots of combinations open for now. Rose and Glasner will share their first meeting outside their respective home countries in mid-November when Forest travel to the Vitality Stadium. There are numerous instances of managers who were appointed this summer clashing before then, though.

Not until week nine is there no such match, with weeks 16 and 27 the only other examples across the whole season. Even then, those rounds feature games between a brand new manager and the still-recently appointed Roberto De Zerbi. A total of 110 matches this season – 28.9% of the total – are currently scheduled to feature two managers who were appointed in 2026.

Iraola’s first campaign on Merseyside is heavily bookended by games of this nature. Liverpool face new managers in their first six matches, and also in seven of the final 10 games. The issue is whether the coaching opponents in question will still be in post when spring rolls around.

Sports.title: Danny Welbeck leads Chelsea past Luton but Enzo Fernández misses Carabao Cup tie
Sports.content:
Emiliano Martínez is on his way but another high-profile Argentinian is likely to be wearing a different shade of blue soon. Chelsea have dealt with their biggest weakness, satisfying Xabi Alonso’s wish for a new goalkeeper by agreeing a £7.5m deal to sign Martínez from Aston Villa, and it will surely not be long before they have put an end to the Enzo Fernández saga.

Fernández was the most notable absentee as Chelsea eased into the third round of the Carabao Cup with a 2-0 win over Luton. There is a desire to move on from the circus. Manchester City are poised to bid for Fernández and, with the noise around the midfielder becoming a distraction, Alonso and the club decided to leave out Chelsea’s supposed vice-captain.

Alonso explained that he had to think about the team. Chelsea’s manager was diplomatic. Alonso said that Fernández has been training well. He offered political answers but did not douse the sense that Fernández has played his last game for Chelsea, who host Leeds in the next round.

It is for the best. Fernández has been looking for a way out since March and Chelsea need committed players. Alonso wants to improve the squad’s culture and the attitude against Luton was good. Danny Welbeck, still going strong at 35, can be a standard bearer after joining from Brighton. The striker is not here to make up the numbers and played a key role in this win, grabbing his first goal since joining when he opened the scoring early in the second half.

“Danny was the patient player,” Alonso said of Welbeck breaking Luton’s resistance by leaping to head home a fine cross from Malo Gusto. “He did what he does best: score and to be in the right place.”

Welbeck will provide competition for João Pedro in attack this season. He also adds a vital dash of experience to a young squad. Chelsea can cope without Fernández, even though they will need to replace him if he goes to City.

View image in fullscreen Xabi Alonso has seen his Chelsea side win their first two games. Photograph: Ian Stephen/Every Second Media/Shutterstock

The early vibes under Alonso are encouraging. He has been decisive with the goalkeeping position, as exemplified by his ruthless response to Robert Sánchez’s skittish display against Fulham. There is nothing left to see with Sánchez. He is not good enough and Chelsea had to be opportunistic when offered the chance to sign Martínez. Mike Penders made his debut in goal on Thursday night. The 21-year-old Belgian is highly rated but will be behind Martínez in the pecking order.

Alonso is trying to win now. Although Chelsea have no European football this season it was surprising that they named such a strong side three days after their helter-skelter win over Fulham in the Premier League. Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer were part of an exciting attack and were supported by a thrilling display from Estêvão Willian on the right.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Third in League One, Luton battled to stay in contention during a first half in which the shot count was 17-3 in Chelsea’s favour. Rogers crashed an effort against the bar and Jack Wilshere’s side were defiant in defence. Josh Keeley made excellent saves from Palmer and Reece James, starting in midfield for the second time in three days despite his injury problems.

Chelsea stayed patient. Valentin Barco, Jude Bellingham’s Atlanta irritant, had an impressive debut next to James. Chelsea, who were still missing Moisés Caicedo, upped the pace early in the second half. Gusto overlapped and crossed. Welbeck was wily and deadly, creeping off his marker and heading home.

The second goal arrived late. Barco was involved and Palmer found Estêvão, whose shot went in off Hakeem Odoffin for an own goal.

Sports.title: Football transfer rumours: Rafael Leão to Aston Villa? Harvey Elliott to Napoli or Lazio?
Sports.content:
The absence of Enzo Fernández from the Chelsea squad that saw off Luton in the Carabao Cup on Thursday night set no end of tongues wagging before, during and after the game. Despite public pre-match assurances from Xabi Alonso that the Argentina midfielder would be included, Fernández was not selected, prompting further speculation that a move to Manchester City is imminent. Chelsea are reported to be holding out for £120m for the 25-year-old, while City are also believed to be interested in securing the services of Iliman Ndiaye, whom Everton value at £80m.

While Mikel Arteta insists he is “really happy” with the squad Arsenal have, talk persists that he’d be even happier if Julián Alvarez was part of it. A pariah among Atlético Madrid fans after stating he wants to leave their club, the Argentina forward wants a “dream” move to Barcelona. With his employers refusing to sell him to the Spanish champions and Alvarez having missed training for the past two days, Atlético officials are believed to be in negotiations with Arsenal over the sale of a player they value at £128m; Gabriel Jesus could be sent the other way in an effort to grease the wheels.

Milan have accepted a £38m bid from Galatasaray for Rafael Leão but Aston Villa remain hopeful of bringing the Portuguese winger to the Premier League on a season-long loan with an obligation to buy. Leão is in talks with Villa, although his Italian employers would rather finalise a permanent sale in the current transfer window. Everton striker Beto could be off to Fiorentina, who have also made enquiries about signing Manchester United’s Dutch striker Joshua Zirkzee.
