Oliver Glasner is hankering for a reunion with Daniel Muñoz, after they enjoyed much success together at Crystal Palace. Nottingham Forest have bid £22m for the 30-year-old right-back but may face competition from Everton in the race to liberate him from Selhurst Park.

An unused substitute in Newcastle’s draw with Liverpool last weekend, Nick Woltemade could be shipped out to Napoli on loan. Despite a promising start after his arrival from Stuttgart for £69m, the beanpole striker has not had a happy time of it on Tyneside and the evidence of Newcastle’s midweek Carabao Cup win over West Brom suggests Woltemade is totally unsuited to the intensity of Matthias Jaissle’s preferred style of play. The same cannot be said for versatile Lille forward Matias Fernandez-Pardo, who has been stood down from training until the end of the transfer window amid talks of an impending French exit.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Following a disastrous loan spell at Aston Villa, where he was restricted to just nine appearances, Liverpool midfielder Harvey Elliot could get his career back on track in Italy with Napoli or Lazio. Manchester United are in the market for a centre-back and Southampton’s Taylor Harwood-Bellis and Chelsea’s Tosin Adarabioyo are both being touted as potential new recruits. And finally, Roma’s speedy teenage striker Robinio Vaz is wanted by Hull, while Leeds reserve goalkeeper Lucas Perri is off to Torino and could be replaced by Standard Liege’s Matthieu Epolo.

Sports.title: Chelsea agree £7.5m deal to sign Emiliano Martínez from Aston Villa
Sports.content:
Chelsea have agreed a £7.5m deal to sign the Aston Villa goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez and are expecting Manchester City to make an offer for Enzo Fernández in the next 48 hours.

Xabi Alonso identified the signing of a goalkeeper as a priority after Robert Sánchez struggled against Fulham on Monday and the deal for Martínez has gone through quickly. The Argentina international is out of favour at Villa after their acquisition of Zion Suzuki and is due to sign a two-year contract with the option of a further year.

The signing of Martínez, who will be 34 next week, will raise questions over the future of Sánchez. Sources believe the Spaniard is unlikely to accept losing his spot as No 1 and may need to be moved on before the window shuts on Tuesday night.

Quick Guide How do I 

However iIt is unclear whether there is an obvious club for Sánchez to join and another complication for Chelsea will be working out what to do with Mike Penders, who was expected to challenge for the No 1 shirt this season. There is a feeling that Penders could leave on loan. The highly rated 21-year-old Belgian spent last season on loan at Strasbourg.

It is poised to be a busy end to the summer for Chelsea, who are also dealing with City’s attempts to sign Fernández. The Argentina midfielder is desperate to leave and was left out of the side for Thursday night’s Carabao Cup tie against Luton.

Sources at Chelsea insist a deal is not close and that there has yet to be any communication from City. Chelsea are adamant that Fernández will be sold only on their terms. City missed an unofficial deadline to sign the midfielder for £120m this month and there have been suggestions the price could be higher because the end of the window is approaching.

Chelsea also need to be able to strengthen their squad but have little time to act. They are aware Bournemouth do not want to sell Alex Scott and that Crystal Palace are similarly determined to hold on to Adam Wharton, while Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara could be a target. Chelsea may not look for a direct replacement for Fernández, but will not accept weakening their squad by helping out a rival.

View image in fullscreen Leon Goretzka has joined Aston Villa after leaving Bayern Munich earlier this summer. Photograph: Neville Williams/Aston Villa FC/Getty Images

Aston Villa, meanwhile, have signed the Germany midfielder Leon Goretzka on a free after his departure from Bayern Munich. The 31-year-old spent eight seasons at ​Bayern, making ‌312 appearances, and has played 73 times for his country.

“I had a bit of long vacation, and it was a process to find out what I really wanted. From the first moment, I had a really good feeling, and I’m really happy to be here,” Goretzka said after completing the move.“I had a good feeling from the first conversation with the coach. Aston Villa is a really big club. I want to help the team to achieve their goals and to bring my experience that I have from my whole career.”

“I’m really looking forward to playing in these kinds of big games every few days,” he added. “This is probably the biggest difference to the Bundesliga, where you have only several great games with big opponents.”

Sports.title: Champions League draw: Arsenal face Real Madrid, Man City get Barcelona and PSG
Sports.content:
Arsenal face mouthwatering assignments against Real Madrid and Bayern Munich as they bid to go one better than last season’s agonising near miss and win a first Champions League title.

Mikel Arteta’s side were pipped on penalties by Paris Saint-Germain in the final three months ago and will be expected to cruise through this season’s league phase. The bulk of their draw appears kind but they are tasked with a visit to the Allianz Arena to play Bayern, whom they beat 3-1 at the Emirates Stadium last November, and host Real, who are once again under the charge of José Mourinho. Two seasons ago, Arsenal beat the Spanish giants 3-0 at home in a quarter-final first leg, Declan Rice scoring two memorable free-kicks.

Arsenal will also welcome Borussia Dortmund, Lille and the Azerbaijani debutants Sabah to north London. Their other away fixtures involve trips to Napoli, Slavia Prague and a reunion with their ex-player Héctor Bellerin at Real Betis.

Manchester City will swiftly renew acquaintances with Rodri when they visit Barcelona during Enzo Maresca’s first Champions League campaign in charge. They will greet Kevin De Bruyne and Napoli at the Etihad Stadium, just as they did last season in cruising to a 2-0 win. Their other home ties bring an enticing meeting with the reigning champions, PSG, a tie against Sporting and a visit by AEK Athens. Trips to Porto, RB Leipzig and Lens will round off their schedule.

The return of Manchester United to Europe’s elite competition throws up home games with Bayern, Roma, RB Leipzig and Sabah. Michael Carrick’s team will travel to Como, who are managed by Cesc Fàbregas, along with Atlético Madrid, Sporting and Villarreal.

Liverpool will host Atlético, Porto, Villarreal and Lens. They visit Lask, the newcomers who sensationally beat Celtic on Tuesday, along with Club Brugge, Fenerbahce and Inter in a relatively kind-looking set of games.

Aston Villa, ravaged in recent weeks by the departures of key players, will hope to have strengthened sufficiently for a home tie with PSG and a visit to Barcelona. They will be heartened by a stirring performance in their recent Super Cup defeat to Luis Enrique’s side in Salzburg. Borussia Dortmund, Fenerbahce and the Norwegian new boys Viking Stavanger will also visit Villa Park. Unai Emery will also take his team to Club Brugge, Galatasaray and Slavia Prague.

Quick Guide Premier League teams' UCL opponents Show Manchester City: PSG (home), Barcelona (away), Sporting (h), Porto (a), Napoli (h), Leipzig (a), AEK Athens (h), Lens (a). Liverpool: Atlético Madrid (h), Inter (a), Porto (h), Club Brugge (a), Villarreal (h), Fenerbahce (a), Lens (h), Lask (a). Arsenal: Real Madrid (h), Bayern Munich (a), Borussia Dortmund (h), Real Betis (a), Lille (h), Napoli (a), Sabah (h), Slavia Prague (a). Aston Villa: PSG (h), Barcelona (a), Dortmund (h), Club Brugge (a), Fenerbahce (h), Galatasaray (a), Viking (h), Slavia Prague (a). Manchester United: Bayern (h), Atletico (a), Roma (h), Sporting (a), Leipzig (h), Villarreal (a), Sabah (h), Como (a). Order of fixtures to be confirmed by Uefa Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

While Chelsea did not qualify for European competition this season, their home will still host Champions League football. The Ukrainian champions, Shakhtar Donetsk, still unable to play continental matches in their homeland, will stage home games there. Real Madrid are the most high-profile of their four visitors, meaning Mourinho will return to his old stomping ground.

PSG’s bid to win a third successive Champions League title involves home league games against Barcelona, Roma, Galatasaray and Slovan Bratislava, as well as trips to Villarreal, Como, City and Villa.

The first set of fixtures will be played on 8 and 9 September. The schedule and dates for all eight match weeks will be announced on Saturday.

Sports.title: Liverpool legend gives blunt response to late transfer decision
Sports.content:
Mark Lawrenson doesn't think Liverpool will miss Cody Gakpo if he leaves before the end of the transfer window.

The Reds icon was speaking after head coach Andoni Iraola said he 'couldn't guarantee' Gakpo would stay at Anfield.



2 Gakpo started Liverpool's season opener amid interest from elsewhere in the Premier League Credit: Getty

Gakpo has been linked with Tottenham and, more recently, Manchester City.

The Netherlands winger impressed in Liverpool's season-opening 2-2 draw away to Newcastle last weekend, scoring the Reds' first equaliser at St. James' Park.

But that's not to see he won't have a new club this time next week, with the window closing on Tuesday, September 1.



Iraola 'doesn't know what's going to happen'

Speaking to the media ahead of Liverpool's first home game of the campaign against Nottingham Forest on Saturday, Iraola said of Gakpo: "I can say what I said last week, and even after the performance he had in the first game.

"He is playing very well for us. He has been very good since he came back from the World Cup and after the holidays, a good attitude and I hope we can keep him at that level because he has been very influential.



"When the market is open you cannot guarantee anything with anyone. When I arrived I would like to know how the market finishes and then when you finish with this one and this one, but I don't know what is going to happen with any of our players. I cannot guarantee anything.

"You think I can smell who we are going to sign or what position, but experience shows you that, if there is an opportunity on the last day [of the transfer window], let's take it."



Gakpo out, Barcola in?

Selling Gakpo could pave the way for Liverpool to sign Bradley Barcola.

The Reds have been linked with the Paris Saint-Germain winger throughout the summer, and talkSPORT understands the two clubs are finalising a deal worth at least £100million.

With both players preferring to play on the left, Liverpool would realistically be unable to accommodate both in any case.

2 Barcola could become one of the most expensive signings of this transfer window Credit: AFP



But Lawrenson isn't worried about the prospect of Gakpo moving on.

Asked by Alan Brazil on talkSPORT Breakfast if Gakpo leaving would come as a blow, the former Republic of Ireland international said: "No, I don't think so. I think they could cover for him.

"My worry is defensively. You've got to shut the back door and then let the guys go and play.

"But I'm just looking forward to the way that they're going to play as much as anything."

Liverpool's transfer window so far

Liverpool have made three signings this summer, with Victor Munoz the sole attacking addition.



That's after they bid farewell to club legend Mohamed Salah, who left at the end of his contract after a glittering nine years on Merseyside and his since joined Trabzonspor.

Sports.title: Chelsea identify Enzo Fernandez replacement available at half the price
Sports.content:
Chelsea have earmarked Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara as a potential replacement for Manchester City-bound Enzo Fernandez.

The 22-year-old is available for between £50million and £60m this summer, with Chelsea expecting to receive at least double that for Fernandez.

2 Camara has attracted interest from the Premier League already Credit: Getty

He has also been linked with a move to Liverpool, with both Premier League clubs being offered the Senegalese international as a late window opportunity.

Crystal Palace had a verbal bid of £35million turned down by Monaco earlier this month and personal terms are not expected to be an issue if a fee is agreed with Chelsea.

talkSPORT understands Fernandez is edging closer to reuniting with former boss Enzo Maresca with a blockbuster transfer in its final stages, despite Chelsea denying that formal talks have taken place.

They previously set a deadline of August 14 for interested teams to meet their £120m price tag, but speculation around his future has only intensified after he was a notable omission from their Carabao Cup victory over Luton Town.

A late-window midfield domino effect involving Maresca and his former employers may coincide with Monaco losing their star midfielder, who they signed for €15m from fellow French outfit Metz two years ago.

Who is Lamine Camara?

Having begun his career at the renowned Generation Foot academy which has fostered the likes of Sadio Mane and Ismaila Sarr, a move to France kick-started his career in February 2023.

He played an integral role in Metz’s promotion to Ligue 1 during the 2023/24 season, leading to his move to the French Riviera in the summer of 2024 and clinching the prestigious African Young Player of the Year award.

Camara asserted himself at the heart of Monaco’s midfield in his maiden campaign.

With 29 league appearances and two goals and seven assists to his name, the 49-cap Senegal international also starred in their UEFA Champions League campaign that season as they reached the round of 32.

He propelled his game to new heights last season as European powerhouses began to take notice of his stellar performances as Monaco secured a seventh-placed finish.

2 Camara has established himself as a star in Ligue 1 Credit: AFP

An ankle sprain towards the start of the season didn’t curtail his campaign with his tireless work rate and imposing 5'8" frame saw him establish himself as one of the most promising young talents in Ligue 1.

Aiming to build on a successful FIFA World Cup where he started in all of Senegal’s games, Camara is set to seek pastures new this summer as he continues on his career upward trajectory.

Chelsea have held talks and discussions with the player's representatives and a move is set to advance if Fernandez completes his switch to The Etihad Stadium.

Camara would add to a midfield department which has already undergone a significant makeover this summer, with Valentin Barco and Jordan Henderson already through the door from Strasbourg and Brentford respectively.

Sports.title: Liverpool finalising Bradley Barcola deal with £120million package close to completion
Sports.content:
Liverpool will finalise the signing of Bradley Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain in the next 24-48 hours, talkSPORT understands.

The Reds have agreed to pay PSG a fixed fee of just over £100million for the 23-year-old, with bonuses currently being worked on that could see the deal rise to £120m altogether.



4 Barcola looks set to depart Paris Saint-Germain this summer Credit: AFP

Bonus payments of around £20m are currently being finalised, with this the final hurdle before Barcola moves to Merseyside.

At one stage this summer, PSG were quoting a £145m asking price for Barcola.

As talkSPORT previously reported, Liverpool made it clear they were not willing to break their own Premier League transfer record.



The French international has wanted the move to Anfield for the whole summer.

Barcola was essentially made surplus to requirements by PSG after several attacking players arrived.



The Champions League holders have recruited Ferran Torres from Barcelona.

Mika Godts and Maghnes Akliouche have also arrived in the French capital.



The Reds are still looking to recruit a right winger as well.

They have seen two offers for Yankuba Minteh turned down, with them moving on for Ismailia Sarr.

There were reports of an offer from Andoni Iraola's side for the Senegalese international, but Liverpool sources have told talkSPORT that isn't the case.

4 Barcola has his move to Anfield, where he will be a key player Credit: Getty

End of a long chase

Barcola emerged as Liverpool's top target for the left wing position at the start of the summer.



There was fleeting interest from Arsenal, but the Gunners never pursued it further.

That left Liverpool with a free run at Barcola, though, the deal isn't done until he's put pen to paper.

talkSPORT initially reported that PSG wanted £145million for Barcola.

Liverpool were never prepared to pay that, so there has been some compromise on the fee.

Transfer dominos

Barcola's arrival and the pursuit of another winger is important for Cody Gakpo's future.



4 Spurs would like to add Gakpo to Savio and Omar Marmoush Credit: Getty

The Dutchman scored in the 2-2 draw against Newcastle United on Sunday.

But with Barcola, Iraola will have Victor Munoz and Rio Ngumoha as options on the left.

talkSPORT understands that Tottenham Hotspur are still keen on the forward.



Manchester City are also keen.

Spurs have signed Savio from Man City in a deal worth up to £85million, while Omar Marmoush is set to join on loan with an obligation to buy if certain conditions are met.

Got their man

Iraola made it clear ahead of the season that Liverpool were fully expecting to sign a winger.

4 Andoni Iraola is about to be handed a major boost with the addition of Barcola Credit: Getty

The fact Ngumoha was at right wing against Newcastle highlighted their problem.



Speaking about that situation during pre-season, Iraola said: "There are obvious situations that we know where we need to sign players. A winger, for example – we definitely need to sign a winger.

"But there are other situations that we will have to analyse what the market gives you, what’s the cost, how we also see the players we have.

"We have some tricky positions where we have injured players that we trust but it is still not the ideal situation.

"So, it will depend on a lot of things."

Sports.title: Chelsea player offered to Man United in late transfer window twist
Sports.content:
Manchester United have been presented with the opportunity to sign Chelsea defender Tosin Adarabioyo to bolster their centre-back options.

The former England youth international was not involved in their 3-2 victory at former side Fulham.



2 Adarabioyo is yet to play for Chelsea this season despite featuring in pre-season Credit: Getty

The tailor-made arrival of Maxence Lacroix for Xabi Alonso’s favoured three-at-the-back system means Adarabioyo is likely to see his game time restricted.

Manchester United transfer news

Kicking off their Premier League campaign with a humbling defeat at newly promoted Hull City, the Red Devils are aiming to sign a left-back before the window slams shut.

Lewis Hall of Newcastle United had long been mooted as an option in this position.



However, talkSPORT football correspondent Ben Jacobs understands they are also aiming to add to their centre-back department as they aim to compete on all fronts in Michael Carrick’s first full season in the dugout.

Ayden Heaven and Harry Maguire were the defensive duo at the MKM Stadium, while Lisandro Martinez and Leny Yoro were unused substitutes.



But both back-ups have endured injury problems during their time at Old Trafford.

The availability of Matthijs de Ligt has been a constant concern as well, having undergone back surgery and not featured since November, although he is set to return soon.



Chelsea's defensive deals an option

Hamstring and calf problems led to Adarabioyo only featuring on 16 occasions in the Premier League last term, struggling for continuity under three managers, and he is one of a plethora of centre-backs which Chelsea have put up for sale this summer.

Manchester United also hold an interest in the 28-year-old’s Chelsea teammate Josh Acheampong but they view their academy graduate as untouchable and an integral part of Alonso’s long-term plans.

The versatile defender starred at Craven Cottage in a centre-back role and impressed in their Carabao Cup progression against Luton Town.

2 Harwood-Bellis has also been on Manchester United's radar this summer Credit: Getty



Coventry City were keen to secure his signature on loan, with Frank Lampard interested in luring him to the West Midlands but those links now appear to have gone cold.

Who else could Manchester United sign?

Another option the 13-time Premier League champions are monitoring is Taylor Harwood-Bellis of Southampton.

Aston Villa and Benfica are among the clubs in the race for his services but neither have met the Saints’ £30million valuation.

The 24-year-old was at the heart of Southampton’s sublime end-of-season form as they went from relegation contenders to promotion hopefuls under Tonda Eckert, only for the ‘Spygate’ fiasco to derail their season.



This has coincided with their star defender being touted for a move away and he wasn’t involved in their Championship clash with Stoke City, only intensifying speculation over his potential departure.

The Red Devils completed most of their business early on with the double midfield acquisition of Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos, and more recently Carlos Baleba, yet their transfer activity is set to accelerate in the coming days.

Sports.title: Arsenal hold Endrick talks to test Jose Mourinho’s resolve over Real Madrid wonderkid
Sports.content:
Arsenal have held talks with Real Madrid over a move for Endrick, talkSPORT understands.

The 20-year-old Brazilian has attracted interest from multiple clubs this summer after a successful loan spell at Lyon last season.



3 Arsenal have become the latest club to express interest in Endrick this summer Credit: Getty

New Madrid boss Jose Mourinho has publicly insisted Endrick is not for sale.

However, talkSPORT understands the Gunners are ready to test the club's resolve, having made an official approach.

Arsenal are on the hunt for a forward in the final week of the window.



They failed to land Endrick's teammate Vinicius Jnr, who ultimately decided to agree fresh terms at the Bernabeu.

The Gunners remain keen on Atletico Madrid forward Julian Alvarez, having recently held talks with a delegation for the LaLiga side in London.



Who else wants Endrick?

Premier League clubs Aston Villa and Liverpool have both been linked with a move for Endrick this summer, along with Roma.

However, the versatile forward is highly-rated by Mourinho.

Speaking earlier this week, the Madrid manager said: "He's a player I like a lot and who has had many contacts from clubs that wanted him on loan or transferred.



"I didn't want to loan or sell him because I like the player, and I'd like to work with this young player who has important talents."

Endrick is currently sidelined with a hamstring problem and did not feature in either of Madrid's opening LaLiga matches.

3 Mourinho has made it clear he does not want Endrick to leave this summer Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

Alvarez latest

talkSPORT understands Atletico Madrid are ready to accept an offer in excess of £120m for Alvarez.



The Argentina star wants to join Barcelona, but Atleti have made it abundantly clear they will not sanction a move to their LaLiga rivals at any price.

It puts Arsenal in the box seat - although ex-Manchester City star Alvarez is yet to give the green light on a return to England.

The 26-year-old has missed the last two days of training, citing illness, and the Gunners are ready to pounce.

A loan deal has also been discussed as Alvarez weighs up his future.

Endrick could be a cheaper and younger alternative - although he will still cost a pretty penny.



3 Alvarez has made clear he wants to leave Atletico with Arsenal looking like his only option Credit: Getty

Madrid paid £51m to sign him as an 18-year-old in 2022 and talkSPORT has been told they will not sell for less.

South American football expert Tim Vickery said: "He hasn't been a failure at all.

"The problem with Real Madrid is he went to a club that didn't need him – but his numbers even with Real Madrid aren't bad.



"And he did very well on loan with Lyon, so there's no way that he can be worth less than he was as an 18-year-old when Real Madrid bought him."

Sports.title: ‘Dead bodies piling up’ – Ex-Premier League player reports himself to police after going missing
Sports.content:
‘Dead bodies piling up’ – Ex-Premier League player reports himself to police after going missing

Former Premier League player Akos Buzsaky has broken his silence after being reported missing, revealing he has handed himself in to the police.

The 44-year-old sparked huge concern earlier this week, when it was revealed that Hungarian police had launched a search for him.



3 Akos Buzsaky has reassured fans he is safe Credit: Getty

Local authorities had been searching for Buzsaky since August 18, who is best known for his stints with Queens Park Rangers, Plymouth Argyle and Portsmouth in English football.

Buzsaky releases statement

Now, in a message shared by the Hungarian's former club QPR, Buzsaky has revealed his absence came after he had deliberately withdrawn from his everyday life.

This followed what he described as serious changes in his personal circumstances over recent months.



In a message relayed by QPR, Buzsaky said: "Dear friends and acquaintances! Unfortunately in the past few months, there have been serious changes in my life that have tested me.

"The dead bodies have been piling up above my head, and there came a moment when I felt I had to break away from these daily routines, due to a misunderstanding, my worried mother pointed me towards the police.



“Thank you very much for all the concern and thoughts you have shown me.

"As soon as I became aware of the situation, I stopped my retreat and informed the authorities.



"I wish everyone a very nice day, and it felt really good to receive so much love!"

Buzsaky's message comes after Hungarian police published his details among their missing persons on 18 August.

The ex-footballer's father, Akos Buzsaky Sr, was not even aware his son had been missing when contacted by Hungarian publication Blikk.

3 Buzsaky spent nearly a decade in English football Credit: Getty



Buzsaky Sr said: “Since we don’t live under the same roof, it’s not surprising that we only speak less often.

“The last time I spoke to him was last week, when he was at home.”

News of Buzsaky's disappearance drew huge attention in England, with former clubs QPR and Plymouth expressing their concern.

The two teams shared messages on social media hoping the midfielder would be found safe.

Akos Buzsaky's career at a glance

The 44-year-old began his career at MTK in Hungary before moving to Porto in 2002.



A loan spell at Portuguese side Academica followed, with Buzsaky then joining Plymouth on loan in 2004 after impressing in a behind-closed-doors friendly.

3 The Hungarian played a major role in QPR's promotion to the Premier League in 2011 Credit: Getty

The Pilgrims then made the loan permanent after just one season, where the midfielder went on to make over 100 appearances for the club.

Buzsaky joined QPR on loan in October 2007, and then signed permanently months later in January.



He quickly became a cult hero at Loftus Road, scoring 10 goals and providing six assists in his first season.

The ex-Hungary international later helped the club achieve promotion to the Premier League in 2011, going on to represent the Hoops 18 times in the top flight.

It proved to be Buzsaky's only Premier League campaign as he departed QPR at the end of this contract in July 2012.

Following his exit from west London, Buzsaky moved to Portsmouth before returning to Hungary in September 2013 to join Ferencvaros.

Sports.title: Premier League strugglers  tipped to qualify for Europe after Man City mistake
Sports.content:
Leeds have got their season off to a flyer with two wins over Premier League rivals in just four days.

Not only that, it was the same foe as Nottingham Forest were beaten 1-0 in the top-flight and then 2-0 in the Carabao Cup.



5 Daniel Farke led Leeds to 14th in the Premier League last season and expectations may be higher this year Credit: Getty

After Anton Stach's late winner at the weekend, both teams made changes for the midweek tie.

The outcome was the same, though, with Leeds heading home from the City Ground with the win.

That comes just months after being relegation candidates before a late-season run of form got them out of trouble to secure a 14th-place finish.



Leeds have been Premier League strugglers in recent years but smart summer transfer business, underpinned by the free transfer of Harry Wilson from Fulham, appears to have Daniel Farke's men in an excellent early position.

Meanwhile, the marquee arrivals of World Cup star Tarik Muharemovic and James Trafford from Man City have given the Elland Road outfit big upgrades in key areas.



And this has got talkSPORT's senior football correspondent Alex Crook feeling Leeds could be in for a big season in all competitions.

Offering his hot take on talkSPORT's Fiery Fridays podcast, he said: "I want to talk about one of Manchester United's big rivals, Leeds, who for me, we're only a week into the new season, but they've been one of the success stories so far, beating the same team twice.



"Really impressive in both their trips to the City Ground and I think Leeds are going to qualify for Europe this season. Here's why...

"We've got nine new managers in the dugout, 11 new permanent managers, if you include Michael Carrick and Roberto Di Zerbi who came in at the end of the last season.

"Leeds actually, along with Brentford, who I also think have got a great chance of challenging for Europe, are one of the few clubs who've got that stability.

5 Leeds star celebrated a second win over Nottingham Forest with James Justin among the goalscorers Credit: Getty



"While there seems to be chaos up and down the country, they stuck with Daniel Farke when there was a possibility, a distinct possibility, both at the start of last season and midway through, that they would make a change of manager.

"It all turned for them when he went to a back-three, half-time against Manchester City. They've not looked back.

"They had a brilliant end to the season, including that win at Old Trafford, which I had to endure as a fan. I think their summer recruitment has been really good.

"I picked out James Trafford as potentially the signing of the summer. I think he's that good.



"Adrian Durham agrees with me that come the European Championship in two years, there's every chance that for the first time in a long time we might have a new England No.1.

"It won't be Jordan Pickford, it'll be that man, James Trafford. I love the arrogance that he's got, the way he backs himself.

5 Muharemovic looks like a brilliant signing for the Leeds defence Credit: Getty

"I loved his interview after the game against Forest. He went off on a bit of a tangent, but I'm here for that. He seems to be a really good character, as well as a great goalkeeper.



"I think the centre-back has gone under the radar. Tarik Muharemovic, coming in from Sassuolo, looks right at home in the Premier League.

"Harry Wilson on a free transfer, when you look at what he did at Fulham last season, is a no-brainer. They're still looking to strengthen at the top end of the pitch as well, maybe bringing a bit more creativity.

"I think this is a club, and it pains me to say it, with a rivalry between the two Uniteds, this is a club moving in the right direction.

"It wouldn't surprise me if they go deep in one of the cup competitions. They've already come through a tricky tie at Forest, and I genuinely think they can challenge for a place in Europe.



"What we know about the Premier League now, and we saw it on the opening weekend of the season, if you're one of those so-called big clubs, the so-called big six, and you're not at it, you're going to get your pants pulled down.

5 Stach scored Leeds' Premier League winner at the weekend as he looks to build on an excellent first season at Elland Road Credit: Getty

"As Man United did at Hull, as Tottenham did against Brentford, as Aston Villa did at Brighton, there are no mugs in the Premier League this season.

"Leeds, at home in particular, are more than capable of leaving some of those big boys with bloody noses.



"I think they can certainly finish in the top eight and maybe win one of the cups."

Leeds benefit from Man City mistake

talkSPORT host Adrian Durham was quick to get behind his view too.

"I do like the look of Leeds", he replied. "I actually did say a couple of weeks ago in pre-season that Leeds will finish above Manchester United. We'll see how that one goes. I wonder how that fits in with your Fiery Friday take, Alex Crook.

"I love that. the midfield duo of Anton Stach and Ethan Ampadu are really good. The Joe Rodon tackle against Forest was absolutely superb, and that said a lot as well. They have real defenders at the back, and that's what they need.

5 Trafford had a fine debut and looks like a brilliant signing for Leeds Credit: Getty



"Your James Trafford take is really interesting. I think Manchester City have let the wrong goalkeeper go.

"I think James Trafford is, I mean, people will hate me for saying it because Gianluigi Donnarumma has played for big clubs, but I think James Trafford is a better all-round goalkeeper.

"I think in terms of saving shots, you'd look at Donnarumma and say he's had some incredible games. I'm not saying he's a bad goalkeeper, but in terms of what future you've got, ball at your feet, which is so important these days, being able to throw it or kick it out long to the wings is exactly what James Trafford can bring for you.

"He's also very good at playing the ball with his feet. He's controlling the ball with his feet. There's not a lot he hasn't got, really. And yeah, he will make an error, but who doesn't make an error?



"He will definitely be challenging Jordan Pickford for the number one jersey. I'm actually going to be disappointed if James Trafford isn't the keeper at the Euros in two years' time. I think it'll only be James Trafford's fault because he's got everything you need to be a top-level goalkeeper. It's whether he can apply himself and mentally make it happen.

"And one other thing about James Trafford, Manchester City went for four trophies last season. The two they won were with James Trafford in goal. My case rests, m'lord."

Sports.title: FIFA quietly approves Argentina request to soften bans after World Cup shame
Sports.content:
FIFA has approved the Argentine Football Association (AFA) request to modify the sanctions handed down for the post-World Cup final chaos.

Leandro Paredes, Nahuel Molina and Thiago Almada were all handed suspensions for their roles in the ugly post-match scenes with Spain's players at the World Cup final in July.

5 Leandro Paredes pushed Spain's Gavi and Eric Garcia and appeared to throw a punch in wild scenes following the World Cup final Credit: Getty

Paredes was slapped with a ten-match ban and fined $90,000 for his actions, which saw him throw punches and attack opposition players.

Molina was banned for seven matches and fined $90,000, while Almada received a one-match ban and fined $30,000.

Argentina coach Roberto Ayala was also hit with a three-match suspension and a fine of $30,000.

All four were involved in the mass brawl after full-time at the MetLife Stadium, with Paredes found guilty of three counts of 'assault' after punching Spain's Gavi and showing him to the ground.

Handed a reprieve?

Argentina's players had been staring at lengthy spells away from international football, with Paredes set for over a year out of action.

However, FIFA has now approved the Argentine FA’s request to allow the bans to be served in Class A friendlies – as well as official games.

According to an AFA statement, FIFA’s Disciplinary Committee determined that the request complies with the current regulations and approved it.

The Argentine federation had formally asked for friendly and official matches to count toward the suspensions, taking into account the national team’s upcoming schedule.

This means Argentina's players can serve their suspensions in significantly less time, especially Paredes.

The Boca Juniors midfielder is now likely to complete the majority of his ten-game ban before the end of 2026 in a major boost.

5 Argentina were heavily punished for the brawl that broke out on the pitch after the World Cup final Credit: Getty

5 But a reduction to their initial sanctions could now see Leandro Paredes return earlier than first expected Credit: Getty

Argentina have not confirmed their fixture schedule but have already booked their spot at the 2030 World Cup as co-hosts and therefore do not need to go through qualifying.

The next Copa America, meanwhile, is not until 2028, but there is no qualification for South American teams to play.

But with Argentina's suspended quartet now able to serve their bans in friendlies, they could well look to schedule in a number of fixtures as soon as possible.

It might not be long before this happens, with two upcoming international breaks in autumn.

The first of the two - across September and October - is the longest, where teams can squeeze in four matches.

Then in November, there will be further opportunity to arrange fixtures with a regular two-game break.

5 It remains unclear if Lionel Messi will feature when Argentina next play

Should Argentina arrange six Class A friendlies during this time, Paredes will have only four more games to serve going into 2027 and Molina one, while Almada could play again from the end of September.

At present, Argentina have not announced any international games scheduled for the rest of the year.

Argentina announce further plans to appeal

While Argentina have been handed a major boost with FIFA's latest decision, they are still hoping for further reductions to their bans.

On top of suspension, they were also hit with a £237,000 fine and must play their next home match with a 50 per cent capacity for other violations during this summer's World Cup.

That includes their players holding up a banner on the pitch with a political message regarding the Falkland Islands.

This breached Article 12 of the Disciplinary Code, which relates to using a sports event for demonstrations of a non-sporting nature.

5 Argentina's players displayed a banner which read 'The Falklands are Argentina's' following their World Cup semi-final victory over England Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

However, in a statement released on Thursday, the Argentine FA declared their intention to appeal this move.

The AFA wrote: “The Argentine Football Association (AFA) has formally requested FIFA to allow the sanctions imposed on its players during the 2026 World Cup final, and on the association itself, to be served in Class A friendly matches and/or official matches, whichever comes first.

“Based on the AFA’s submission, Fifa’s Disciplinary Committee has deemed the request approved in accordance with current regulations.

“Nevertheless, the AFA, in defense of its rights and those of its players, is awaiting the written justification for the decisions in order to file the corresponding appeals with FIFA’s Appeals Committee, with the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) potentially as the final recourse.”

Sports.title: Xabi Alonso reveals details of Enzo Fernandez conversation which led to him being left out of squad to face Luton - as Monaco midfielder emerges as contender to replace Argentine if he leaves club
Sports.content:
Xabi Alonso says he chose a Chelsea squad that had the ‘desire to play’ and decided he could not select Enzo Fernandez after speaking privately with the Manchester City target. Fernandez was missing from the match-day selection for Thursday's Carabao Cup win over Luton Town. That was despite Alonso insisting the day before that he would use the Argentinian, 25. Fernandez’s absence immediately sparked speculation that City had opened club-to-club talks surrounding a potential £120million transfer. However, Chelsea sources on Thursday night insisted after defeating Luton that they were still awaiting a formal approach. Alonso described it as his decision to exclude Fernandez and explained: ‘We need the players that are in the best situation to play. We need to take everything into consideration – players that are in a good moment, players that are not feeling that energy to play. ‘For me, it is very important they feel this desire to play and to have good preparation.’ Alonso spoke with Fernandez after training on Wednesday with the Blues boss adding: ‘We talked and we decided it was better not to be part of the squad. He is a top player.’ Enzo Fernandez was left out of Chelsea's squad to face Luton in the Carabao Cup Xabi Alonso said he chose a Chelsea squad that had the ‘desire to play’ and decided he could not select Fernandez, who is a target for Man City Monaco's Lamine Camara is under consideration at Chelsea should Fernandez leave

Your browser does not support iframes.

While Chelsea wait for City to submit an offer, they have been working on potential replacements. The Blues have been interested in Alex Scott all summer. However, Bournemouth have never placed a price tag on their 23-year-old midfielder and have only ever said he is not for sale. It is understood Monaco’s Lamine Camara, 22, is also under active consideration at Chelsea. Asked if he would need a replacement if Fernandez is sold, Alonso said: ‘Sorry, but I’m not the one who talks too early. We will see what happens. We want to be ready always. ‘We are quite close to the plan we had. We will see where we finish, if it’s fully executed or there are things still to be done or things we couldn’t do. But overall the balance of what we have is going to be good. We have to see how the last few days develop. The team is coming together.’ Chelsea would have needed to sign Emiliano Martinez from Aston Villa by 12pm UK time on Friday in order for the 33-year-old goalkeeper to be eligible to face Brighton this Sunday if fit. Otherwise, Alonso would need to choose between Robert Sanchez, 28, and Mike Penders, 21. The arrival of Martinez could see Sanchez sold permanently with it appearing he has lost the trust of Alonso, having leaked two avoidable goals in Chelsea’s 3-2 win at Fulham on Monday. ‘Don’t ask but I know,’ Alonso said on who will face Brighton. ‘I prefer to tell the players first.’

Sports.title: Chelsea FINALLY set to end hunt for front-of-shirt sponsor after setting target for £50m deal - as they near lucrative agreement with American digital currency outfit
Sports.content:
Chelsea are set to end their search for a front-of-shirt sponsor – by signing a lucrative deal with a digital currency outfit.

Daily Mail Sport understands that the Stamford Bridge club are close to agreeing a partnership with US-based Circle Internet Group.

The deal is likely to be for an initial year, with the option to extend should both parties be happy to do so.

It would see the company’s USDC (US Dollar Coin) logo on the front of the club’s shirts in a yellow font, to match this season’s style.

While the numbers involved are likely to be kept private, Chelsea officials had reportedly been looking for a deal worth around £50m a season. It can also be disclosed that they are close to striking a sleeve sponsorship agreement - and that club insiders are confident that they will be ahead of budget across all areas of sponsorship this season.

The proposed deal with Circle would see USDC on the front of the men’s, women’s and academy shirts across all competitions.

Chelsea have found a main front-of-shirt sponsor for the first time since 2022-23: Circle Internet Group

Their previous major front-of-shirt sponsor was Three, but that deal expired in 2022-23

The club have secured temporary deals with clubs midway through each season since then

Chelsea have been keen to ensure they partnered with a company they club could align with and believe they have managed to do so. Circle has been viewed as a major success story in the expanding world of fintech, with its supply expanding by around $2bn in the past week, according to analysts.

It is viewed as a financial infrastructure, or platform, that speeds up the process of moving money across borders online. USDC is a regulated, dollar-backed currency known as stable coin, with the value rising and falling in line with American currency.

Last year, Formula One’s Aston Martin struck a multi-year sponsorship with Coinbase which was paid for entirely with USDC.

Should the deal, as expected, be confirmed, the intention is for the logo to be on Chelsea’s shirts when they take on Brighton at Stamford Bridge on Sunday.

The club has started the last three consecutive seasons with a blank space on the middle of its jerseys, since their deal with mobile network Three was brought to a conclusion at the end of the 2022-23 campaign. Deals have subsequently been penned mid-campaign.

Three suspended its deal, thought to be worth £40m a season, following Russia’s invasion of the Ukraine which led to the forced sale of the west London club by former owner Roman Abramovich.

The agreement with Circle would come as a further boost to the club who started the season with a 3-2 win at neighbours Fulham under new manager Xabi Alonso.

Sports.title: 'Disgraced and hairy... that's all your lot ever call me!': RICHARD KEYS and ANDY GRAY on fleeing bombs in Qatar, why Keys had to laser his hairy hands, the truth about his younger wife, Gray's regret, and what they think of today's pundits
Sports.content:
‘Disgraced and hairy, that’s all your lot ever call me,’ says Richard Keys.

Instinctively, I look to his hands. Where’s the hair gone? ‘Laser,’ he answers.

What, a vanity move? ‘Yes!’ intercepts Andy Gray.

‘No, no, no,’ corrects Keys. ‘I'll tell you what it was. After so many years of putting my hand into a bowl of crisps, and everybody else taking theirs out scared, I thought, “I have to do something about this”.’

There are no crisps on our table and Keys’ smooth paws are wrapped around a glass of pink champagne. Gray lowers his flute to imitate the buzzing of the laser treatment. ‘It’s true,’ he says. ‘He was f****** frightening everybody, me included!’

An afternoon with Keys & Gray is seldom anything but entertaining.

An afternoon with Richard Keys (right) & Andy Gray (left) is seldom anything but entertaining

This is the pair's first newspaper interview since returning to Britain after 13 years with Qatar-based beIN Sports

There is 2011 and their spectacular exit from Sky. Bombs over Doha. Marriage and morality. And, above all, perception

But here, on the top floor of the OXO Tower overlooking the Thames, in their first newspaper interview since returning to Britain after 13 years with Qatar-based beIN Sports, there is serious stuff, too. There is 2011 and their spectacular exit from Sky. Bombs over Doha. Marriage and morality. And, above all, perception.

‘I genuinely don’t know what people here think of me,’ says Gray. ‘But since I’ve come back, there have been more smiles than moans.’

Later, our French waiter returns excitedly after watching Gray’s goals on his phone. It is a nice moment, and a reminder of the player before the pundit.

Keys has a bigger battle with perception. ‘Honestly - and I haven't said this to anybody - the perception of me is, “Old man who left his dying wife for his daughter's best friend”. No one's ever bothered to ask, “Is that true?”.’

Is that true? ‘Of course it isn’t,’ says the 69-year-old.

Keys and his wife of 34 years, Julia, separated in 2016. He has been with Lucie, 31 years his junior, ever since. They married in 2023. Lucie and his daughter, Jemma, were routinely described as ‘best friends’ in the media.

‘I fell in love again, totally unexpectedly,’ he begins. ‘I just got blown off my feet. It was with someone who was not my daughter's best friend but had spent time in her company.

'My wife had cancer nearly 10 years before I left home. “Recovered” is a hard word with cancer, because you’re always aware of it, but she was not dying of cancer and I’m pleased to say she is still with us and hasn’t died. So the narrative suited those that wanted to find a reason to not like me.’

‹ Slide me › Keys and Gray presented the flagship Monday Night Football show on Sky until their exit in 2011

The duo moved to Qatar to work for beIN Sports from 2013 until the end of last season

Gray, 70, has been married three times. Still time for another? ‘My wife might say there's one or two left in her, so I don't know what that means for me!’ says Gray, a father of five.

How about children? ‘I think I'll answer that honestly as well,’ says Keys. ‘I don't have the right at my time of life to say to Lucie, “You cannot be a mother”. If she said she wanted children, then I need to partake in that.’

‘You better get a move on, then,’ says Gray. ‘That is also true,’ Keys laughs. ‘I had open-heart surgery nine years ago. My surgeon said two more days and I would have been dead. So now, as our great friend Peter Reid would say, “I’m going to enjoy my life”.’

So we were only 48 hours from Gray & Gray? ‘Wouldn't that be a good day!’ says Gray. ‘Gray & Gray. I like that.’

The truth is, he wouldn’t. They have been a double act for more than three decades and the future is Keys & Gray Unleashed, a podcast launched this month and already making headlines. They had Match of the Day in their crosshairs this week, Harry Redknapp the week before.

What was all that about? ‘I think Richard teased it by saying we could have gone to jail because of what happened,’ says Gray. ‘But you’ll have to wait for the full story.’

Keys disagrees: ‘Harry put us in a very difficult situation. We were confronted with a problem that we didn't want and had not created. Whether with malice or not, we don't know. But if you put together the different component parts, he was under a bit of pressure himself at the time, facing court action…’ Gray’s stare wins and Keys trails off.

‘I'm told he's bemused by what the problem is,’ says Keys. ‘One day, I hope to be able to tell him.’

Gray, 70, has been married three times. Still time for another? ‘My wife might say there's one or two left in her, so I don't know what that means for me!’

Keys, 69, marries Lucie, 31 years his junior, in Devon in 2023

Gray with Rachel Lewis, his third wife, in 2019

There is so much of their past still to pick through, we should not lose sight of the present. Why exactly are they here? They were the face of beIN’s Premier League coverage and, unlike Sky Sports, the parting was not hostile. The hostilities were happening outside.

‘I hit the wall about a year ago,’ says Keys. ‘I'd run out of steam when it came to match time. And the game, I hate to say, is not as enjoyable as it could be. And yes, the bombs were unsettling. What Andy Burnham did with the wildfire alert, we were getting that four times a night. We s*** ourselves.’

Gray takes over: ‘I was on my terrace one night. The next minute there's four streaks of light across the sky. Then, there's another four coming from the US airbase, taking them out. They exploded right above me. You think, “hmmm”.’

‘We were living and working in a war zone,’ says Keys. ‘We later led the chaps back into the studio after we were forced off air for a period. We presented, listening to missiles being blown up above us.

‘When I later got the first flight out… the delay at the terminal, leaving the gate, then at the end of the runway. You just think, “Get this f***ing thing on the move”. The relief when it did, I cannot describe.’

Keys wants to be in London now, living permanently at his West Kensington home with Lucie, who is a lawyer. He also wants to wear a blue cap and white trainers. ‘This is me now. I’ve been in a suit for 40 years.’

Television, insists Keys, is over. With Gray, though, you detect regret that his departure from Sky took him away from his favourite domain beyond the penalty box – the commentary box.

‘I'd like to think, somewhere, I could do a bit of commentary,’ he says. ‘Not television, maybe, but radio. Just to see what it feels like again. I would like that.’

With Gray, you detect regret that his departure from Sky took him away from his favourite domain beyond the penalty box - the commentary box

Keys wants to be in London now, living permanently at his West Kensington home with Lucie, who is a lawyer

Keys turns towards Gray: ‘I would be happy for you if that happened. I think you deserve it. I’ve had my moment and I'll still be talking football. But to hear him back, analysing a football match, that would be special. He’s the best I’ve ever known.’

Keys is warming to his theme now. ‘He means the world to me. What happened in 2011 brought us together in a way I did not expect. I remember saying to him, now more than ever we need to be together, because they were trying to divide us - and then we are weaker. He has trusted me implicitly with everything we've done ever since.’

So, 2011. Gray was sacked after an off-air conversation between the pair was leaked to the press in which they questioned whether female assistant referee Sian Massey understood the offside rule. Keys resigned soon after as further off-air footage emerged, including his infamous ‘Did you smash it?’ remark about Jamie Redknapp’s love life.

‘I could never defend it and never pretend it's not unpalatable,’ says Keys of the Massey incident. ‘I fully accept the responsibility for my part and he does his. It should not have happened.

‘But at the time, it was a smaller part of a bigger picture. Rupert Murdoch was trying to buy all of Sky. I’m told that Jeremy Hunt, the culture secretary, had said it would help if Sky News could prove they were an independent operator.

‘What better way to do that than fry your own? So, these two f****ers that work for Sky, it was open season on us in the media.’

Gray says: ‘I can’t imagine saying today what I said then, I just can’t. I think we were two of the first people ever cancelled. I had 20 reporters outside my house for weeks.’

Keys apologised to Massey at the time and she accepted it. In 2022, Gray found himself spending seven hours on a flight with her.

Keys watches on from the Sky Sports studio in 2011 at Molineux, where leaked audio of his and Gray's discussion of assistant referee Sian Massey led to their exit from Sky

Keys later apologised to Massey, who retired this summer

‘We chatted and I gave her my number and offered to help her with anything in Doha. It was nice.’

Keys says: ’Sian was brilliant with us. She messaged me that day and said, “You’ll never guess who I’m sitting in front of on the plane?”. I replied, “Does that make you offside?”.’ A bad dad joke, perhaps, but not one for which Keys should be cancelled this time.

‘I've taken a black-and-blue kicking, I promise you. Andy knows that. He’s lived with me through it. But if my wife thought I was the person described in the media, she wouldn't be with me.

‘So to be back here, this is liberating. I've been staggered by the reaction and enormously grateful, because the majority of people are saying, “It's good to have you boys back”. That’s touching. I have been beaten up. I've been kicked from pillar to post for a long time.’

It is a rare glimpse of his vulnerability. 'Everyone thinks I've the skin of a rhino...' he says.

The sun is setting beyond the capital’s skyline and it feels like a good time to pivot to some lighter conversation. This is my quick-fire round, much like Keys when it comes to ordering champagne.

One presenter, three pundits. Who are you watching?

‘Graeme Souness, Glenn Hoddle,’ starts Keys. ‘And Lianne Sanderson. She’s funny and knows football. I don’t want to sit and listen to guffawing buffoons. I can go to the pub for that. Frank Lampard is also brilliant and we like Alan (Shearer), he’s just a good lad. But those are my three. As for a presenter, Kelly (Cates) is very good. I'm proud to say that I helped her when she started.’

Both Keys and Gray list Graeme Souness (left) and Glenn Hoddle (right) among their favourite pundits on TV today

Kelly Cates (right), who presents on Sky and Match of the Day, is also a Keys favourite

Gray picks the same three but swaps Cates for Laura Woods. OK, which lineup would make you change the channel?

‘Oh no, I'm not answering that,’ says Gray. ‘He will!’

‘I have a deep affection and exchange messages with Phil Neville,’ says Keys. ‘I like Phil Neville.’

‘No,’ says Gray. ‘We want to know who you'd turn off.’

‘I've just answered the question,’ says Keys. He does later concede admiration for Gary Neville and the way he has impacted punditry.

What about Roy Keane? ‘Keane is a little like Graeme (Souness),’ says Keys. ‘He can say things that grab your attention. What I had to say to Graeme at one point was, “You now need to start watching football. You're only going to get so far with the story of being at the front of the line and looking behind for warriors”. And we love Graeme dearly.

‘But if I wanted to know about a football match and have someone tell me something different, it wouldn't be Keane. I think he's ideal for the modern world. He will give you something you're going to bite on.’

The rest of the world certainly bit when Keys recently revealed that he once spent Christmas Day alone with a can of tuna, a bottle of champagne and watched The Great Escape, Where Eagles Dare and The Guns of Navarone back to back.

'Roy Keane is a little like Graeme,’ says Keys. ‘He can say things that grab your attention'

'If I wanted to know about a football match and have someone tell me something different, it wouldn't be Keane. I think he's ideal for the modern world'

We turn the question on Gray – what would his Christmas Day alone look like? ‘I wake up and straight away I’d have smoked salmon chopped into scrambled eggs.’ Keys interrupts: ‘Andy, it’s just a quick question - food and three films.’

‘You’ve spoken for long enough,’ Gray shoots back. ‘I’ll continue. So, I’d go downstairs for a glass of champagne. Then, it would be a traditional dinner, the whole works. For dessert, apple crumble and custard. Then to the sofa, with a glass, to watch The Great Escape, The Bridge on the River Kwai and 633 Squadron.’ What’s the last one? ‘You’ve never seen it?’ says Gray, incredulous. No, I was born in 1982.

‘It’s like the Dam Busters, but the target is more difficult,’ he explains. ‘They fly in low and have to go up a mountain and drop a bomb so it hits where the German cannons are. Ah, it’s brilliant.’ Keys cannot resist: ‘Wait a minute, Andy. We’ll get a monitor and tactics board so you can explain this one in more detail…’

For two fellas who came home partly because they'd had enough of bombs over Doha, their choice of films is somewhat ironic.

Next. If you could take one moment from your career with you? ‘Bayern Munich. Goodison Park. 1985. All day long. Thank you. Good night,’ says Gray.

Keys does not hesitate, either: ‘Kevin Keegan has obviously been on my mind recently. I was fortunate to be part of his “I would love it” tirade, asking the questions. I just knew he had something to say and the producer was in my ear telling me to leave him alone. What he then said will always be remembered.

‘When Kevin came to Qatar we only ever called him King Kev, everywhere we went. So yeah, that moment, because it was the gateway to someone who was very special to me.’

Finally, how would you like to be remembered? ‘I would just like to be remembered!’ says Gray. ‘But I don’t know. As a good lad who was good fun to be with and was decent.’

If you could take one moment from your career with you? ‘Bayern Munich. Goodison Park. 1985. All day long. Thank you. Good night,’ says Gray, pictured right scoring that night

‘When Kevin (Keegan) came to Qatar we only ever called him King Kev, everywhere we went'

'I don't think people know me in a way I would have wished,' says Keys, while Gray adds: 'I would just like to be remembered!'

Keys, inevitably, has more to say: ‘In a manner that is different to the way I'm perceived now. I don't think people know me in a way I would have wished. There's a lot of good things I've done, in broadcasting and away from it, that have been scrubbed or ignored. And it does, if I'm by the Thames with a glass or two, yeah, it hurts.

‘I’ve probably accepted that won’t change. So when the likes of Andy and Souness - and they’ve worked with everyone - say what they do about me, that means a lot. I bow to that and say, “Thank you”.’

Thirteen years away has changed plenty. The hairy hands have gone. The suits, too. And so, in time, they hope will some of the old perceptions.

Keys & Gray, however, remain very much Keys & Gray. An afternoon in their company is seldom anything but entertaining.

Sports.title: Jamie Vardy's podcast secures live broadcasting rights for the BUNDESLIGA - as he beats Gary Neville to new gig
Sports.content:
Jamie Vardy's podcast secures live broadcasting rights for the BUNDESLIGA - as he beats Gary Neville to new gig

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Jamie Vardy has secured live broadcasting rights for the Bundesliga, beating out Gary Neville to the gig.

The former England and Leicester City striker, who is currently without a club, launched his YouTube channel and podcast in June.

And now he will broadcast seven Friday night Bundesliga matches throughout the season across the United Kingdom and Ireland.

Vardy's partnership, which will see him watch and comment on the games, begins tonight as Bayern Munich take on Stuttgart in the season curtain-raiser.

It follows streamer Mark Goldbridge picking up a similar arrangement last season for his That's Football channel.

His Bundesliga live streams have typically garnered somewhere between 20,000 and 30,000 views, though that is with an audience of 1.5 million subscribers. Vardy has 12,800 subs.

Jamie Vardy has secured the rights to live broadcast the Bundesliga on Friday nights

A source told The Sun: 'This is a huge move for Jamie as he expands his talents in broadcasting, while still playing football.

'He’s buzzing to reach Bundesliga fans and chat with star guests about action on the pitch.

'He’s hoping to creat a real community with his podcast and is loving getting into the nitty gritty of the sport.'

Rick Murray, CEO of producers Workerbee, added: 'Fans don’t just want to watch football anymore, they want to experience it with the people they already know and trust.

'Jamie has built an incredible community around the podcast, and thanks to our Bundesliga partnership, we can bring that audience closer to some seriously big games.'

Vardy has already had the likes of Sean Dyche, Wes Morgan, and David James on his podcast.

Interestingly, his best-viewed video by some stretch has been with automotive YouTuber Mat Armstrong. That has raked in 150,000 views.

Daily Mail Sport has reached out to Vardy's representatives for comment.

The 39-year-old is a free agent after leaving Italian club Cremonese upon their relegation from Serie A.

Sports.title: Sandro Tonali's reunion with Newcastle looms larger after Tottenham's season false started - the £100m signing must prove he can be the midfield authority figure Roberto De Zerbi's side need
Sports.content:
Sandro Tonali's reunion with Newcastle looms larger after Tottenham's season false started - the £100m signing must prove he can be the midfield authority figure Roberto De Zerbi's side need

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

The date has been circled on Sandro Tonali's calendar ever since he completed his £100million move to Tottenham in July.

'Newcastle second game, really I can't wait to play,' said Tonali in his first interview as a Spurs player, enthusing for the club's inhouse media about a transfer that made him feel 16 again and explaining his 'close to magic' connection with Roberto De Zerbi.

He remains the biggest investment of a summer spree now nearing £400million, after a double deal for Savio and Omar Marmoush from Manchester City were completed this week. But following the emphatic defeat at Brentford on the opening day, when the 26-year-old Italian was strangely anonymous in a midfield dominated by the Bees' new boy Mamadou Sangare, the Newcastle fixture looms larger than ever for Tonali.

He was signed to be a figure of authority in midfield. To enrich Spurs with more power and industry, to add tactical acumen without forgoing technical poise and restore a balance they lost in recent years.

'Definite links to (Andrea) Pirlo', as his former Newcastle boss Eddie Howe once said. 'And it's not just the hair.' Howe also came to value Tonali's influence out of possession, 'putting out fires' as much as on the ball.

Against Hoffenheim in pre-season, Tonali looked every inch that player. He set the Spurs tempo and oozed class, and Lucas Bergvall grew in stature alongside him. But friendlies can be deceptive and when the real business started in the Premier League neither he nor the team could rise to the intensity required.

Sandro Tonali was signed to be a figure of authority in Tottenham's midfield and help to restore a balance they lost in recent years

The £100m summer signing will go up against his former club Newcastle on Saturday

The fixture looms larger after Tottenham's heavy opening day defeat away against Brentford

Data from the Brentford game suggests it was not for lack of effort. Only Vitaly Janelt clocked more metres than Tonali's 11,948. Only two players on the pitch had more touches. Only two could claim more 'line-breaking passes' and he featured prominently in the pressing statistics for Spurs behind Richarlison and Conor Gallagher.

Brentford ensured the game was played on their terms, however, which is a sign of a good team. They won comfortably, scored three and it could have been more.

While the £100million fee is not Tonali's doing it commands attention. Eyes fell upon the club's record signing to see if he had the strength of personality to seize the game, give it a shake and disturb its rhythms in Spurs' favour, and it turned out he could not.

De Zerbi blamed the defeat and the atrocious display on too many players 'not in the right physical condition'. He issued a reminder it would take time for the team to find its spirit and organisation. Then he excused Tonali and Marcos Senesi from the Carabao Cup second round win over Charlton on Wednesday to train instead. 'Sandro has to work to feel better in terms of physical condition,' said De Zerbi.

Reasons why Senesi might be behind the fitness curve were perfectly clear. He played in the World Cup final for Argentina against Spain on July 19 and missed a chunk of pre-season. Tonali did not go to the World Cup because Italy failed to qualify for the third time in a row and has been with De Zerbi for the entire pre-season.

Only four of the Spurs starting XI at Brentford last weekend played at the World Cup, accumulating 901 minutes between them. Manchester City started against Bournemouth with eight players who had 3,351 World Cup minutes in their legs.

As fans wondered how their team could appear quite so undercooked, De Zerbi noted the extra time off granted to some players, including Rodrigo Bentancur, and the disruption of a pre-season tour to New Zealand and Australia. It was not a full-scale complaint, but he had already mentioned that captain Micky van de Ven had an injury that was something to do with one of the flights.

Others picked up injuries during the tour, including new £85million midfielder Mateus Fernandes, Dominic Solanke, Destiny Udogie and James Maddison. None were too serious but enough to interfere with fitness programmes and convince De Zerbi to start with them on the bench on the opening weekend.

De Zerbi left Tonali out of Tottenham's Carabao Cup win in midweek to work on his fitness

Tottenham have been boosted by the signings of Savio and Omar Marmoush this week

'At the beginning of Australia we played every three days,' said the Spurs boss when quizzed about Tonali before the Charlton game. 'The trip was 25-26 hours and the day after we couldn't work in the right condition.

'When we came here (back to London), we couldn't work immediately because there was a friendly game against Getafe. In the last two weeks, the players from the World Cup came and we worked in different situations, but I think he needs more time, like JP (van Hecke).'

Van Hecke had less than three weeks off between returning home from the World Cup and setting off on the tour Down Under and admitted the schedule had taken its toll on him and others.

'Physically, of course, it impacts your body,' said the £54million summer signing from Brighton. 'I also struggled for one or two weeks after and that's not ideal.'

All of which served as a useful reality check on expectations after a summer of Spurs spending, but five goals against Charlton's reserves in the Carabao Cup, a dazzling goalscoring debut for Savio, the subsequent arrival of Marmoush and the pursuit of Cody Gakpo from Liverpool might send them soaring again ahead of the first Premier League home game of the season.

It is the one Tonali has been waiting for against Newcastle, who emerged from weeks of turmoil to impress in a 2-2 draw with Liverpool on Sunday. He will not want to disappoint again.
