Sports.title: Ariel Helwani Rips Itauma Hrgovic Pay Per View
Sports.content:
It is unclear if greed is driving the decision or if promoters simply want the prestige attached to calling Itauma a pay-per-view attraction. Either way, chasing short-term revenue may damage his career over the long run.

DAZN entered the American boxing market in 2018 with a low monthly price and promotional messaging declaring pay-per-view dead. Subscribers were supposed to receive major fights without paying a separate event fee.

That sales pitch has disappeared. Customers now pay monthly or annual subscription charges while many of the most heavily promoted shows require another payment. Helwani’s reference to Teofimo Lopez versus Rolando Romero shows how quickly those charges are accumulating.

The timing is especially questionable because Itauma is attempting to make heavyweight history. He can no longer break Mike Tyson’s record as the youngest champion, but defeating Hrgovic would reportedly make him the second youngest. An achievement with that type of mainstream potential should be placed where the largest possible audience can see it.

Anthony Joshua’s rise offers a revealing comparison. His first pay-per-view headliner against Dillian Whyte also came in his 15th professional fight, the same number Itauma will have Saturday. Joshua, however, entered professional boxing as a London Olympic gold medalist, had received years of exposure on regular Sky Sports broadcasts and carried a personal rivalry with Whyte dating back to the amateurs.

Itauma has no comparable public introduction. He stopped a badly faded Whyte in the first round in August 2025 before becoming the first man to stop Jermaine Franklin seven months later. Those victories raised his position within boxing without making him a known attraction among the wider public.

Hrgovic gives him a legitimate sporting test, but the 34-year-old brings little commercial strength. He has gone through punishing fights against Zhilei Zhang, Daniel Dubois and David Adeleye, cuts easily and has shown increasing vulnerability under pressure.

Helwani’s argument comes down to timing. Premium pricing works after viewers have formed an attachment to a boxer. Itauma is being asked to sell an event before most casual fans have been given the opportunity to know him.

Putting Moses Itauma Behind A Paywall Hurts His Future

The commercial risk becomes clearer when the price and supporting lineup are examined. DAZN is charging £24.99 in the United Kingdom and $59.99 in the United States for a one-off purchase.

Sam Noakes against former WBO lightweight champion Denys Berinchyk is the strongest supporting fight. Constantin Ursu meets Ben Vaughan, while Guido Vianello faces Moses Jolly. Mike Perez withdrew from his cruiserweight bout with Aloys Junior and was replaced by Sherif Musah, who has a 4-2-1 record, before the fight was moved to the preliminary portion of the show.

Those contests may serve their purpose on a regular DAZN broadcast, but they add little selling power to a premium event. Itauma and Hrgovic are being left to carry almost the entire commercial burden.

The promoters are trying to collect star-level money before their young heavyweight has become a star. That may produce more revenue from dedicated followers on August 29, but it reduces the number of people who will witness the most important fight of his career.

Regular DAZN broadcasts should remain Itauma’s home until he is at least 26 and has been shown repeatedly to boxing fans. Five more years of accessible fights would allow viewers to follow his development, learn his personality and become invested in his career. It would also improve his future sponsorship value and give promoters a much larger audience to sell to later.

Winning the IBF title would give Itauma a belt without automatically making him an attraction. A strong performance against Hrgovic needs to reach people beyond those already following heavyweight boxing.

Calling Itauma a pay-per-view headliner does not make him one. It only limits the audience he still needs to build.

Sports.title: Andy Ruiz Let His Anthony Joshua Trilogy Expire
Sports.content:
“That’s something that I told Eddie Hearn. ‘Eddie Hearn, if I sign with Matchroom and with you, please give me the trilogy.’ That’s something that all my fans want to see. All my Mexican fans, and it can happen. It can happen,” Ruiz told the Mr. Verzace Podcast.

Since losing their December 2019 rematch, Ruiz has fought only three times, defeating Chris Arreola and Luis Ortiz before receiving a majority draw against Jarrell Miller in August 2024.

Knyba will be his first opponent in more than two years. The Polish heavyweight was stopped in three rounds by Agit Kabayel in January, so beating him will not establish Ruiz as a leading contender.

Hearn Already Gave Ruiz The Formula

Eddie Hearn left the trilogy available after the second fight but attached conditions to it. In March 2020, he said Joshua might face Ruiz again “if he keeps winning or if he’s still around.” He also questioned how the former champion would respond after making substantial money from their two fights.

“Who knows what Ruiz is going to do? He’s made a lot of money. Maybe he sails off into the sunset,” Hearn said at the time.

By October 2022, Hearn supplied an even clearer route. He said the trilogy was not among Joshua’s next two or three fights but added that beating Deontay Wilder would change the calculation.

The proposed Wilder fight later collapsed over money. Wilder’s team wanted a 70- 30 split, while Ruiz’s father demanded 50- 50. Wilder subsequently accused Ruiz of asking for as much as $25 million, although that figure was never established independently. The precise demands remain disputed, but Ruiz lost the fight that could have returned him to the front of the division.

No comparable opportunity followed. Ruiz remained out until the Miller draw and then disappeared for another two years.

Extended inactivity has also prevented Ruiz from showing any technical development since Joshua exposed his limitations in their rematch. Joshua stayed behind his jab, moved around the outside, and refused to trade combinations at close range. Ruiz followed him without cutting off the ring effectively and never forced Joshua into the exchanges he needed.

His three subsequent performances offer no solution. Arreola dropped him in the second round and hurt him again later. Ruiz defeated Ortiz largely because of three knockdowns, but the older Cuban still controlled long stretches from distance. Miller then pressured Ruiz into a physically draining fight in which he slowed before receiving a draw.

The hand injury against Miller was serious, but injuries have become part of Ruiz’s career rather than an isolated explanation. Sporadic training camps leave him rebuilding his conditioning every time he returns instead of sharpening the parts of his game that Joshua defeated.

A third meeting would therefore be sold almost entirely through memories of June 2019. Nothing in Ruiz’s recent performances suggests that the result would differ from the second fight.

Did The Joshua Money Remove His Ambition?

In the new interview, Ruiz admits that money, cars, fame, women, and partying caused him to neglect the Joshua rematch. It is impossible to separate the money he received from those fights from the decline in his activity.

Financial security gave him the freedom to stay away. Before beating Joshua, he was a hungry replacement accepting the opportunity of his career on short notice. After collecting two major purses, that urgency disappeared. Injuries and personal difficulties contributed, but neither explains the full seven-year pattern.

Hearn questioned in 2020 if Ruiz would remain committed after getting rich. His activity since then has largely supplied the answer.

Joshua Has More Valuable Opponents

The heavyweight division continued moving during Ruiz’s absence. Moses Itauma has become one of its leading young names, while Daniel Dubois built his position by stopping Joshua and continuing to face important opponents. Fans would rather see Joshua test Itauma or attempt to avenge the Dubois defeat than revisit a rivalry last active in 2019.

Older followers remember Ruiz’s stunning night at Madison Square Garden. Many younger fans have never watched him fight live. To that audience, he is simply another fighter, now 36, campaigning against a rebuilding opponent.

Beating Knyba must be the beginning of Ruiz’s rebuilding process, not the qualification for another Joshua payday. He says he wants to return in December. Following through and facing a leading contender would strengthen his case far more than repeatedly invoking the first Joshua fight.

There was enough time to force the trilogy into public demand. Staying active and beating Wilder or several top contenders would have made Ruiz difficult for Joshua and Hearn to ignore. Instead, he waited for one historic upset to retain its commercial power forever.

The rivalry is tied at one win apiece, but an unfinished score does not remain important when one fighter disappears. Ruiz did not lose his Joshua trilogy opportunity through bad luck. He allowed it to expire.

Sports.title: Shakur Stevenson Teases Fight Date After Haney Failure
Sports.content:
Stevenson stubbornly held to his demand of 144 pounds during the Haney talks. Under that arrangement, Shakur would have moved up four pounds while Haney came down three from the welterweight limit. He negotiated as though he were the A-side and Haney needed the fight badly enough to accept those terms.

Haney owned the larger following, held the welterweight title and had no obligation to weaken himself. Shakur’s demand also conflicted with his previous willingness to face Conor Benn at the full 147-pound limit. He even offered to accept Benn’s choice of rehydration restrictions during their confrontation in February. TalkSPORT reported that Stevenson proposed the fight at 147.

If Shakur was prepared to meet Benn at welterweight, his insistence on 144 for Haney was difficult to present as a simple safety issue. The catchweight would have reduced the physical size of a more technically accomplished rival.

Vargas Offers a Marketable Defense

Stevenson now has four leading WBO contenders available at 140 pounds: Emiliano Vargas, Lindolfo Delgado, Oscar Duarte and Ernesto Mercado.

Vargas would attract the most casual attention because he is the son of former world champion Fernando Vargas. At 22, however, Emiliano lacks anything close to Shakur’s professional experience.

His rise to the No. 1 ranking has been built on wins over domestic-level opposition rather than championship contenders. His two most recent victories came against Bryce Mills and Agustin Ezequiel Quintana, neither of whom had fought near the world level before meeting him. Top Rank lists those stoppages as the leading wins on Vargas’ record.

Vargas is therefore a commercially useful but manageable choice. Critics would see Shakur picking an inexperienced prospect whose famous surname gives the fight more value than his opposition has earned.

Mercado Brings the Greater Threat

Mercado has already accused Shakur of avoiding him.

“I’m in his head. I live in his head. He don’t wanna fight me,” Mercado said during an Inside The Ring interview.

Faster than Shakur and carrying considerably more power, Mercado can close distance quickly, match his hand speed and hurt him if the exchanges become physical. Stevenson owns the superior experience, defensive skill and championship background. Those qualities make Mercado the most dangerous fighter in the WBO’s top 15. He has also pursued a bout with Vargas, yet neither of the division’s more marketable names has shown much interest in signing to face him.

The financial calculation is easy to understand. Shakur has collected major purses on Turki Alalshikh’s cards. A loss to Mercado could disrupt that lucrative run without bringing Haney’s audience or Vargas’ family name.

Vargas supplies a recognizable opponent with a large experience disadvantage. Facing Mercado would test Shakur against the most hazardous available contender. Another attempt to bring a welterweight down three pounds would confirm that Stevenson prefers a physical concession when the opposition is skilled enough to threaten his major paydays.

Sports.title: Tyson Fury Has Replacements Ready If Joshua Fight Fails
Sports.content:
Netflix signed up for an international event driven by two famous British heavyweights and a rivalry years in the making. Its return comes through worldwide viewing, subscriber activity and interest beyond boxing’s regular audience, not individual pay-per-view sales alone. Remove Joshua, and that cultural event becomes a standard Fury broadcast against an unfamiliar opponent. Refusing to name either alternative also makes Brown’s announcement sound like pressure on Joshua’s side.

Fury’s camp is publicly presenting New York as a plan that can continue without him, but Brown still expects the original fight to be completed. Until Netflix confirms its involvement with another opponent, the alternatives provide Fury’s team with negotiating leverage more than certainty.

Netflix Faces A Difficult Replacement Decision

The available options leave Fury’s side trapped between commercial value and competitive danger. A soft opponent may not give Netflix enough reason to retain the date, venue and promotional budget. Madison Square Garden also becomes harder to fill once Joshua’s name is removed.

Selecting a leading heavyweight brings a different risk. Fury struggled badly against boxing newcomer Francis Ngannou before losing consecutive fights to Oleksandr Usyk. He looked heavy and slow in the second Usyk fight, with his movement and timing far removed from the fighter who controlled the heavyweight division earlier in his career.

Since then, Fury has beaten Arslanbek Makhmudov by a wide decision and stopped 46-year-old Mariusz Wach after seven rounds. Neither result proved that he is ready to defeat one of the division’s leading fighters. Makhmudov had already been stopped by Agit Kabayel and Guido Vianello, while Wach had lost 12 of his previous 18 fights. The last opponent Fury looked good against at championship level was Derek Chisora in December 2022, almost four years ago. Comfortable wins over carefully selected opposition do not erase what happened against Ngannou and Usyk.

Losing in November would damage the Joshua fight far more than another postponement. Yet selecting an opponent who offers little resistance may leave Netflix paying heavily for another tune-up.

Brown’s announcement shows that Fury’s camp has prepared for the Joshua negotiations to fail. It provides no assurance that Netflix will support the substitute plan or Madison Square Garden will remain the venue. Having two names available is the easy part. Finding someone credible enough for Netflix, manageable enough for Fury, and marketable enough for New York is the real difficulty.

Sports.title: WBA President Undercuts Teofimo Lopez’s Catterall Claim
Sports.content:
The timing and wording weaken Lopez’s argument that the requirement belonged only to Romero. Mendoza made the statement six weeks before Lopez captured the WBA welterweight title by majority decision on August 22. The obligation was described as applying to the winner rather than Romero alone.

Teofimo recently argued that he was not involved in the agreement requiring Romero to face Catterall within 180 days. His position was that beating Romero created a new championship situation because the original paperwork carried Romero’s name.

That contractual distinction does not answer Mendoza’s July 9 declaration. The WBA president knew Lopez was the challenger and publicly connected Catterall to the outcome. Lopez may not have signed Romero’s agreement, but he accepted the bout with that condition already stated.

The matchup also carries more danger than Catterall’s limited recognition in the United States might suggest. His patient southpaw counterpunching would require Lopez to lead and create openings without becoming reckless. Sandor Martin used movement, timing and the left-handed stance to disrupt Lopez in their disputed 2022 fight. Catterall would present some of the same complications while bringing greater experience at the championship level.

A step-aside payment offers one possible escape if Lopez pursues the Ryan Garcia versus Conor Benn winner, but Catterall has already said he will not accept even “$1” to surrender his opportunity. If he maintains that stance, Lopez may eventually have to defend, persuade the WBA to approve another fight or vacate the belt.

Vacating would preserve Lopez’s freedom at the cost of weakening his claim to control the welterweight division. He has talked about pursuing three unifications without making a defense. Giving up the title to avoid the first opponent connected to it would turn that ambition into promotional language rather than a championship plan.

Mendoza’s post is not the same as a published ruling from the WBA Championships Committee ordering Lopez to make the defense. The organization still needs to state how it will enforce Catterall’s status now that the championship has changed hands.

However, Teofimo can no longer characterize Catterall as Romero’s obligation alone. The WBA president’s own words support the British fighter’s demand for the next opportunity.

Teofimo Lopez Claims Catterall Deadline No Longer Applies

Teofimo Lopez is attempting to separate himself from the WBA order requiring Rolando Romero to face Jack Catterall within 180 days. Lopez argues that defeating Romero changed the championship situation, but the WBA Championships Committee, not his legal team, will decide if the obligation carries over.

Teofimo Lopez Sends WBA Dispute to Legal Team

“The contract they signed, I was never involved in that contract or that agreement,” Lopez told Ariel Helwani. “It’ll go to my legal team, and we’ll talk. I don’t duck anybody. We’ll fight. “That contract they signed for an extension, for whatever it was, 180 days, was with the name Rolando ‘Rolly’ Romero, not Teofimo Lopez. That means the whole situation with the mandatory changes now. It’s a reset, and I think people are forgetting that.”

Lopez is free to offer that interpretation, but the WBA has not publicly ruled that Catterall’s position or the November 19 deadline disappeared when the title changed hands.

Catterall defeated Shakhram Giyasov on May 23 to get the WBA’s secondary welterweight belt. The organization then required Romero to face the winner within 180 days. Catterall maintains that the WBA has told him he is next and that promoter Eddie Hearn has written to WBA president Gilberto Mendoza requesting an immediate order.

Lopez’s legal team can argue that the original directive named Romero, but a mandatory requirement issued by a sanctioning body is not simply a private contract that binds only the two fighters named in it. The WBA committee can transfer the obligation, modify the deadline, or grant Lopez another fight. Until it makes that decision, Lopez cannot declare on his own that the process has restarted.

The new champion also cited the cut over his right eyebrow and his resulting medical suspension.

“I’m suspended by all commissions right now due to the cut over my right eye. Until I get my license back from the commission, we don’t need to talk about any mandatories at this particular time.”

That suspension prevents Teofimo from returning to the ring until he receives medical clearance. It does not prevent the WBA from confirming Catterall’s status or ordering negotiations for a later date.

Nobody is asking Lopez to defend the belt before the cut heals. The dispute concerns who receives his next defense after he is cleared. Catterall says the WBA has already given him that answer, while Lopez is trying to persuade the committee to give him a different one.

Mannix: Teofimo Lopez Knows Ryan Garcia Is Next

Chris Mannix says Teofimo Lopez and his team already know Ryan Garcia is likely to be his next opponent. Their confidence suggests they do not regard Jack Catterall’s mandatory WBA title consolidation as an obstacle that will stop the fight.

“Ryan Garcia is the name that is at the top of everybody’s list. Ryan Garcia is the name that Teofimo Lopez and his team know that they’re likely going to face,” Mannix said on his DAZN show with Sergio Mora. “In fact, win or lose this fight against Conor Benn, I think Ryan Garcia is going to be next for Teofimo.”

A Garcia victory over Benn on September 12 would allow Lopez to request permission for a WBA-WBC unification. The organization could authorize that fight, give Catterall another deadline and argue that consolidating championships took priority over immediately eliminating its own secondary title.

Losing to Benn would remove that justification. Garcia would no longer bring the WBC belt, leaving Lopez to choose a commercially valuable voluntary defense over a mandated consolidation. Allowing it would amount to the WBA discarding its order because Lopez found a more profitable opponent.

Catterall is not merely a contender waiting after winning an eliminator. He captured the WBA Regular welterweight title by defeating Shakhram Giyasov and was promised a fight against the primary champion within 180 days. Lopez inherited that obligation when he took the WBA title from Rolando Romero.

The sanctioning body must now decide how much its own order is worth. A Garcia unification would produce greater attention and a larger sanctioning fee, but another postponement would further reduce the value of holding its Regular title. Fighters are asked to compete for that belt, pay sanctioning fees and trust that victory will lead to the primary champion.

Lopez’s apparent freedom to plan around Catterall shows that commercial appeal may defeat enforcement. If the WBA permits Garcia to go first, especially after a loss to Benn, it will make itself look second-rate by showing that its orders apply only when champions have nothing richer available.

Matchroom Presses WBA To Force Teofimo Lopez vs. Jack Catterall

Jack Catterall confirmed Tuesday that Eddie Hearn and Matchroom sent a letter to the WBA in an attempt to get his title fight with Teofimo Lopez enforced.

“Letter was sent to them yesterday by Eddie and Matchroom,” Catterall posted on X in response to a supporter asking his team to act.

Catterall also revealed that WBA president Gilberto Mendoza personally promised him that the 180-day commitment would remain in place regardless of who held the Super title.

“When I met Gilberto Mendoza in Egypt, I shook his hand and he gave me his word if I beat Giyasov, someone who was avoided and waited for his shot for two years, I will get my shot within 180 days regardless who has the belt. So I believe the WBA will do the correct thing,” Catterall posted.

That account removes much of the uncertainty about what the WBA intended. Its published resolution named Rolando Romero, but its president allegedly told Catterall that the commitment followed the title. Lopez still has a technical argument based on the written wording, yet the WBA would have to break Mendoza’s personal promise to let him move on.

The dispute began after Lopez openly denied that Catterall was his mandatory during Monday’s Inside the Ring show. Lopez plans to pursue the three additional titles he needs to become the undisputed welterweight champion, beginning with the winner of Ryan Garcia versus Conor Benn on September 12.

That pursuit leaves no place for Catterall, but the secondary WBA champion has rejected the easiest negotiated solution.

“There’s not $1 that can persuade me to step aside to allow a unification bout to happen. I’m here to fight,” Catterall said.

His refusal means Matchroom cannot be paid to wait while Lopez pursues the Garcia vs. Benn winner. The WBA must enforce the consolidation fight, permit a unification first, or allow its two welterweight champions to remain separated.

The 180-day period expires on November 19, based on Catterall’s May 23 victory over Shakhram Giyasov. That leaves less than three months to settle the dispute. The cut Lopez suffered over his right eyebrow against Rolando Romero places more strain on the schedule, although there has been no indication that it will keep him out for an extended period.

Teofimo may believe the WBA will permit a unification to take priority over its internal consolidation fight. Sanctioning bodies regularly move mandatory obligations aside when champions pursue another belt, giving his team a stronger argument than the wording omission alone.

Catterall brings tactical risk with little financial reward. His awkward southpaw style and sharp counterpunching deny opponents clean offensive opportunities. Ryan Garcia, Conor Benn and Devin Haney generate massive paydays. Catterall brings no comparable commercial appeal, only a genuine threat to expose Lopez inside the ring.

WBA Loophole Gives Teofimo Lopez Easy Out On Jack Catterall

A review of the WBA’s published rulings supports part of Teofimo Lopez’s argument. No public order currently names Jack Catterall as the mandatory challenger for Lopez’s newly acquired Super welterweight title.

The May 21 ruling required Rolando Romero to face the Catterall-Shakhram Giyasov winner within 180 days. Its language named Romero specifically. It did not say the obligation would transfer to Romero’s successor if the title changed hands.

That omission gives Lopez a technical basis for denying that Catterall has been formally assigned to him. The WBA would need to issue another ruling, clarify that the original order followed the championship, or designate Catterall as Lopez’s challenger.

Teofimo still goes too far by claiming Catterall was lied to. The WBA sanctioned the Giyasov bout and publicly stated that its winner would receive Romero within 180 days. Catterall’s expectation came directly from the organization, not from an invented promise by his team.

The real issue is poor wording from the WBA. It created two champions and ordered them to meet, yet attached the obligation to Romero by name rather than clearly attaching it to the Super title. Lopez is now using that opening to pursue the Garcia-Benn winner while Catterall waits for the WBA to explain what its own ruling means.

Teofimo Lopez Denies Jack Catterall Mandatory Status

Teofimo Lopez claims Jack Catterall is not his WBA mandatory and says the British contender was lied to about his right to challenge for the welterweight title.

During today’s Inside the Ring show, Catterall confronted the new WBA champion after Lopez discussed facing the Ryan Garcia vs. Conor Benn winner and eventually meeting Devin Haney for the undisputed championship.

“He’s not. He’s not my mandatory,” Lopez said when Catterall was identified as next in line. “By the sanctioning rules, he’s not my mandatory, and I think they lied. I think they lied to him.”

“It’s in the contract,” Catterall answered.

Teofimo’s denial conflicts with the WBA’s own published ruling. When the organization elevated Rolando Romero to Super champion in May, it sanctioned Catterall’s bout with Shakhram Giyasov for the vacant secondary title and stated that Romero had to face the winner within 180 days.

Catterall defeated Giyasov and now holds that belt. Lopez may argue that the ruling named Romero rather than whoever defeated him, or that no separate order has been issued since Saturday. Neither explanation supports his claim that Catterall was lied to. The WBA publicly connected the two titles and imposed a deadline for bringing them together.

The exchange became entertaining because Lopez tried to rewrite the situation while Catterall was on the screen looking directly at him. Rather than explain the supposed sanctioning rule, Teofimo declared that the obligation did not exist and blamed unnamed people for misleading Catterall.

After making that denial, the new champion returned to the familiar claim that he will face anyone.

“I’m always willing to fight anybody and everybody,” Lopez said.

“I’m glad you won on the weekend because I know you don’t duck nobody,” Catterall replied. “It would have been more difficult to get Rolly into the ring. I’m happy for you, but we’ve got to get it on.”

Catterall played the interaction perfectly. He congratulated Lopez, reminded him that Romero would have been harder to bring into the ring and declined to turn the conversation into a shouting match. That left Teofimo arguing against a contract he had not seen while Catterall calmly insisted the terms were already written down.

There was also some clever pressure inside Catterall’s praise. Telling Lopez, “I know you don’t duck nobody,” gave the champion little room to reject the fight without contradicting the reputation Catterall had just assigned to him.

The WBA now needs to explain the status of its own ruling. It can grant Lopez permission to pursue a unification, arrange a step-aside payment or order the title consolidation. What it cannot credibly do is remain silent while its new champion claims the other titleholder was fooled.

Lopez is clearly trying to look past the mandatory to chase the massive paydays against the Ryan Garcia vs. Conor Benn winner or a unification with Devin Haney. Catterall holds the regular belt after beating Shakhram Giyasov, which, in standard WBA procedure, makes him the direct mandatory to unify the titles.

Sports.title: Brandon Figueroa Gets Familiar Name Tomoki Kameda
Sports.content:
PBC announced Figueroa versus Kameda as the co-main event beneath Sebastian Fundora’s previously revealed WBC super welterweight title defense against Ermal Hadribeaj. The broadcast begins at 8 p.m. ET on TNT, truTV and DAZN.

Kameda’s selection is not ideal from a competitive-merit standpoint. The 35-year-old has not fought since losing a 12-round majority decision to IBF featherweight champion Angelo Leo in May 2025. He is moving directly from one failed title bid into another without recording a comeback win.

Familiarity is his appeal, but the name belongs to a fighter more than a decade removed from his best period. Kameda captured the WBO bantamweight title in 2013 and completed his three-defense reign the following year. His championship accomplishments are now part of boxing history rather than evidence of his present standing at featherweight.

Kameda has repeatedly fallen short when stepping up since that reign. He lost consecutive decisions to Jamie McDonnell in 2015, dropped a wide decision against Rey Vargas in 2019, and split two fights with Lerato Dlamini. His other wins came against middle-of-the-pack opposition before Angelo Leo defeated him last year.

That history limits how much can be taken from Kameda’s competitive performance against Leo. Another respectable defeat does not establish him as one of the leading featherweights. His recognizable name, durability and past championship remain the selling points.

Can Kameda Control Figueroa’s Pressure?

Through 47 professional fights, Kameda has never been stopped, but durability alone will not solve the tactical difficulty. Figueroa does his best work by forcing opponents into prolonged exchanges, attacking the body and maintaining a pace that becomes harder to match as rounds accumulate.

Keeping the fight at a controlled distance will require lateral movement, straight punches and counters. Kameda’s majority-decision loss to Leo showed that he can remain competitive over 12 rounds, although Figueroa presents a more exhausting physical test. That requires him to collect early rounds without allowing the champion to pin him down and begin sustained body attacks.

At featherweight, Figueroa looks physically established. Moving up from 122 pounds has not reduced his output, and the stoppage of Ball showed that his power carries late into championship fights. His combination of volume, physical pressure and finishing strength now gives opponents several concerns to manage.

Defensive openings remain available when Figueroa commits to extended combinations. Kameda’s best chance will come from making him miss during those attacks and answering before the champion resets his feet. Remaining on the ropes for extended periods would allow Figueroa to impose exactly the fight he wants.

“Brandon Figueroa is a great champion, and I know that when the bell rings, we’re going to give the fans a fight they’ll remember,” Kameda said.

This may also represent Kameda’s final title shot in a second division. More than 13 years have passed since he captured his bantamweight belt, and another defeat would leave him with consecutive losses in featherweight championship fights.

Carrington Fight Drives The Matchmaking

The booking gives PBC a practical compromise. Kameda is safer than placing Figueroa directly into another championship fight, but he is easier to promote than a little-known contender. His history, durability and competitive showing against Leo provide enough credibility for television. The weakness is that his selection follows a defeat and nearly 17 months of inactivity.

DAZN has already connected Figueroa with WBC featherweight champion Bruce Carrington. A unification between them would carry considerably more competitive value, with Carrington’s speed, movement and counterpunching testing Figueroa in ways Kameda may no longer be equipped to do.

This fight fills the space between Figueroa’s victory over Ball and a possible Carrington meeting. Kameda has enough experience to punish a poor performance, but his age, inactivity and latest result make this a favorable first defense for the champion.

Jermall Charlo will also meet Koen Mazoudier in a 10-round super middleweight bout on the October 17 card. Mazoudier defeated Sam Beck by decision on August 26 and will return fewer than eight weeks later.

Sports.title: Dmitrii Bivol And Callum Smith Agree WBO Title Fight
Sports.content:
“Please be advised that the WBO World Championship Committee has received written confirmation from RCC Boxing, on behalf of WBO Light Heavyweight Champion Dmitrii Bivol, and Matchroom Boxing, on behalf of Mandatory Challenger Callum Smith, confirming that the parties have reached terms, including an agreed date and venue for the WBO Light Heavyweight Mandatory Championship Contest. The WBO respectfully defers to the parties to formally announce the date, venue, and event details in due course,” said Olivieri on X.

Smith, 36, is finally getting the title opportunity he has waited for, but the financial value remains unknown. Bivol’s two fights with Artur Beterbiev were backed by Turki Alalshikh and carried undisputed championship status. A mandatory defense does not have the same commercial weight.

The venue will reveal more. Saudi involvement may turn the event into another major payday. If RCC Boxing and Matchroom are financing it without that support, Smith may receive considerably less than Bivol and Beterbiev earned from their two meetings.

Inactivity presents another concern for the challenger. He has not competed since going through a 12-round war with Joshua Buatsi in February 2025 and has boxed only twice since suffering a seventh-round knockout against Beterbiev in January 2024.

Bivol, 35, underwent back surgery after his questionable majority decision over Beterbiev in February 2025. He returned in May 2026 and defeated IBF mandatory Michael Eifert by a wide unanimous decision before undergoing surgery on his injured left elbow in July.

The champion has therefore boxed only once since the Beterbiev rematch and must now return from a second operation. Smith has been inactive longer, but neither man enters under ideal conditions. Bivol must show that his elbow permits him to throw combinations freely, while his challenger must overcome approximately 18 months outside the ring.

Those two Beterbiev bouts supplied Smith with a blueprint for troubling Bivol. Sustained aggression denied him room to settle, made him expend energy, and reduced the time available for his accurate combinations.

During the opening six rounds of their rematch, Beterbiev looked capable of breaking Bivol. His work rate dropped from the seventh through the 11th, however. Once he increased the pace in round 12, Bivol again looked vulnerable and close to being stopped.

Smith cannot afford similar quiet stretches. He must cut off the ring, attack the body and maintain the pace instead of following Bivol while absorbing straight punches. Knowing the plan and executing it for an entire championship bout are very different tasks.

At six feet three inches with a 78-inch reach, Smith owns major physical advantages but has not always used them effectively. He often retreats in straight lines before settling behind a static high guard near the ropes. That habit would give Bivol the stationary target he wants for his quick multi-punch combinations.

A counter left hook remains Smith’s best chance of changing the contest with one punch. Landing it cleanly will be difficult because Bivol maintains a disciplined defensive position while jabbing and rarely leaves his chin exposed for the shot that Smith used to stop Gilbert Castillo and Mathieu Bauderlique.

High guards also give Bivol opportunities rather than discouraging him. He can split the gloves with straight punches, attack around them with hooks and leave the pocket before the counter arrives. Canelo Alvarez and Gilberto Ramirez struggled to interrupt that rhythm once he began controlling the distance.

Their common opponents underline the size of Smith’s task. Bivol neutralized Canelo over 12 rounds and divided two close decisions with Beterbiev. Smith suffered a one-sided decision against Canelo before Beterbiev dropped him twice and stopped him in the seventh. Those results do not decide this contest, but they show that the champion has handled the elite opposition that overwhelmed his mandatory challenger.

At 36, this may be Smith’s final opportunity to win a world title in a second division. That urgency may force him to take risks, yet passive pursuit will not be enough. He needs to use his reach to push Bivol backward, work the body and prevent him from resetting without becoming trapped behind his guard.

Waiting preserved Smith’s mandatory position but took away valuable time near the end of his career. He finally has the opportunity he wanted. Now he must carry out an exhausting tactical blueprint against one of boxing’s most accurate technicians after approximately 18 months without competition.

Sports.title: Oscar Collazo Takes Major Flyweight Risk Against Sandoval
Sports.content:
Entering only his second fight at flyweight, Collazo is coming off a two-round stoppage of late replacement Neider Valdez. The 5-foot-2 unified minimumweight champion will give away four inches in height to the 5-foot-6 Sandoval while moving directly from a trial fight in the division to arguably its best fighter.

Sandoval earned the WBA and WBC titles by traveling to Japan and defeating Kenshiro Teraji by split decision in July 2025. He survived a fifth-round knockdown and recovered well enough to outwork Teraji across the later rounds.

That victory showed the difficulty of the task facing Collazo. The champion is larger, experienced against top opposition and capable of maintaining his output over 12 rounds. Collazo dominated at minimumweight, but beating fighters closer to his own size does not guarantee that his pressure and punching power will carry into a fight against a full-sized flyweight.

The seven-pound move from 105 to 112 represents nearly seven percent of Collazo’s former weight limit. He bypassed the 108-pound division entirely, although the Valdez bout gave him one short appearance at flyweight before challenging Sandoval. Two rounds against a late replacement could not show how his power, stamina and punch resistance will hold up against a natural 112-pound champion.

Their methods create a clear contest between precision and activity. Collazo uses timing, lateral movement and accurate body combinations, while Sandoval applied enough pressure and maintained sufficient output to defeat Teraji. The challenger must land with enough force to reduce that activity. Without earning Sandoval’s respect, the smaller man may struggle to control the pace over 12 rounds.

“Sandoval is a challenge that motivates me and my team. I was looking to make history and prove that there are no limits when you know what you’re capable of doing,” Collazo said. “This isn’t just for me. This is for Puerto Rico and to raise the level of Puerto Rican boxing.”

The southpaw stance gives Collazo a route inside. His rear left hand can reach Sandoval’s body from an angle, but he must cross the taller champion’s punching range to deliver it. Sandoval’s straight right hand and uppercut will be available whenever Collazo lowers himself or steps forward. Much may depend on how often the challenger reaches the body without taking a clean counter on his way inside.

Sandoval’s recovery against Teraji creates another question. He got up from a fifth-round knockdown and fought effectively enough over the remaining rounds to win the titles. Collazo carried useful power at 105 pounds, but hurting an established flyweight is a different physical test. Failure to slow the champion early may force him to match Sandoval’s activity deep into the contest.

His brief appearance against Valdez offered little evidence because it lasted less than two rounds. Collazo overwhelmed an opponent brought in on short notice, but Sandoval represents an entirely different level of resistance.

Rather than spending several fights adjusting to the division, Collazo is going directly after two flyweight championships while retaining his WBA and WBO minimumweight belts. Winning would give him recognized titles in two divisions simultaneously. This is far more than a ceremonial opportunity for a successful champion moving up in weight.

Ghana News.title: Sir Sam Jonah says Nigerian state agencies subjected his real estate investment to ‘sustained harassment’
Ghana News.content:
Ghanaian business leader Sir Sam Jonah has disclosed that a significant real estate investment he made in Nigeria has been subjected to what he describes as “sustained harassment” by state agencies.

He said Ghanaian workers at the project site had also experienced treatment similar to scenes of xenophobic attacks that have been condemned elsewhere on the continent.

Sir Sam Jonah made the disclosure while delivering the keynote address at the Global Business Forum – Ghana Edition on Friday, August 28, 2026.

He said he was sharing his experience to highlight the broader challenges confronting African investors operating in other African countries.

“I have made a significant investment in a real estate development in Nigeria, a country I hold in high regard and in whose promise I have long believed. That investment has been subjected to sustained harassment by state agencies,” he said.

“Ghanaian workers on the site have endured treatment not dissimilar to the scenes we deplore in South Africa,” he added.

‘What hope has the young entrepreneur?’

Sir Sam Jonah, who began his career underground at Obuasi before leading Ashanti Goldfields to become the first operating African company listed on the New York Stock Exchange, said his experience raised concerns about the prospects of smaller African businesses seeking to expand across borders.

“If this is the experience of an investor with my resources, my networks and my grey hairs, what hope has the young entrepreneur with none of these?” he asked.

He warned that the treatment of African investors within Africa could undermine efforts to deepen intra-African investment and trade.

“When African capital is harassed in Africa, we should not wonder why it flees to London and Dubai,” he said.

Sir Sam Jonah urged governments across the continent to give African investors and workers the same level of protection and attention afforded to foreign investors.

“Protect the African investor and the African worker in your jurisdiction as zealously as you court the foreign one — for no treaty can accomplish what hospitality refuses,” he said.

His comments come amid renewed calls for African businesses to expand across national borders and take advantage of opportunities created by the African Continental Free Trade Area.

The disclosure also adds to concerns about whether the treatment of African businesses and workers across borders is keeping pace with the continent’s ambitions for greater economic integration.

Ghana News.title: ‘Africa exports its savings and imports expensive capital’ – Sir Sam Jonah
Ghana News.content:
Ghanaian business leader Sir Sam Jonah has challenged African institutional investors to put more of their capital to work on the continent, warning that Africa is caught in a cycle of exporting its savings while borrowing expensive capital from abroad.

He said the situation was widening the continent’s infrastructure financing gap while leaving promising African businesses struggling to access long-term funding.

Delivering the keynote address at the Global Business Forum – Ghana Edition on Friday, August 28, Sir Sam Jonah described the situation as Africa’s “great paradox”.

“Here is our great paradox: Africa exports its savings and imports expensive capital. Our pension funds and institutional pools sit in short-term instruments while our infrastructure gap widens and our best entrepreneurs go begging — and we then borrow our own money back from abroad at punishing rates,” he said.

“No continent in history has industrialised on rented capital alone,” he added.

Sir Sam Jonah said foreign investment remained important and welcomed the contribution of international investors to Africa’s development.

He noted that he had spent much of his career raising foreign investment, partnering with international investors and deploying their capital.

However, he said African countries and investors must demonstrate greater confidence in their own economies.

“Capital follows conviction; it does not substitute for it,” he said.

Using an analogy, Sir Sam Jonah said investors were more likely to commit funds when they saw African investors and institutions taking risks in their own markets.

“Investors, like dinner guests, come far more readily to a table where the host is already seated and eating,” he said.

Sir Sam Jonah also called for the creation of more African companies capable of competing globally, creating jobs and growing over the long term.

He cited his experience with Ashanti Goldfields, which became the first operating African company to be listed on the New York Stock Exchange, as evidence that African businesses could compete on the global stage when properly built and managed.

“The lesson was not that we needed New York's validation. The lesson was that an African enterprise, properly built and boldly led, could stand anywhere on earth and look anyone in the eye,” he said.

He said Africa needed hundreds more companies of that scale across strategic sectors.

“We need a hundred more such firms. A thousand. In agribusiness, in finance, in energy, in technology, in manufacturing,” he said.

According to him, building such businesses should not be left entirely to governments.

“Building them is not the government's job. It is ours — the people in this room,” he said.

Sir Sam Jonah further urged African investors to embrace patient capital and take positions in promising businesses before risks were completely eliminated.

He argued that investors willing to properly assess and price risks at an early stage could benefit significantly from Africa’s long-term growth opportunities.

“The best-performing opportunities of the coming decades will not belong to those who arrive after the risk has gone. They will belong to those who priced the risk correctly while others were still afraid,” he said.

Ghana News.title: AfCFTA faces ‘grave danger’ from protectionism, xenophobia and investor harassment – Sir Sam Jonah
Ghana News.content:
Ghanaian business leader Sir Sam Jonah has warned that the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) is in “grave danger” of failing if African countries do not demonstrate stronger commitment to its implementation.

He said the continent’s most ambitious economic integration project since independence was not being threatened by a lack of vision, but by protectionist policies, xenophobia and the treatment of African investors and workers in other African countries.

Delivering the keynote address at the Global Business Forum – Ghana Edition on Friday, August 28, Sir Sam Jonah said African countries must move beyond declarations and ensure that the principles of free trade are reflected in how businesses and investors are treated.

“Let us also disabuse ourselves of one comfortable illusion: nobody will buy African out of a sense of duty to the cause. Sentiment is not a supply chain,” he said.

‘AfCFTA will die by our own hand’

Sir Sam Jonah, who began his career underground at Obuasi and later led Ashanti Goldfields to become the first operating African company listed on the New York Stock Exchange, said the fate of AfCFTA ultimately rested with its member states.

He warned that the agreement would not necessarily be undermined by external forces but could instead collapse because of actions taken by African countries themselves.

“If it dies, it will die by our own hand — border by border, permit by permit, prejudice by prejudice,” he declared.

He identified recent xenophobic attacks in South Africa as particularly damaging to the vision of a unified African market.

Describing the attacks as “a dagger aimed at the heart of continental integration,” Sir Sam Jonah warned that such incidents could trigger retaliatory actions in other African countries.

“A free trade area cannot survive among citizens who are not free to trade, to work, and to live among one another in safety,” he said.

Sir Sam Jonah also drew on his own experience as an African investor to illustrate the challenges facing businesses operating across the continent.

He disclosed that a significant real estate investment he made in Nigeria had faced what he described as “sustained harassment by state agencies”.

“Ghanaian workers on the site have endured treatment not dissimilar to the scenes we deplore in South Africa,” he said.

He said he was raising the issue not to embarrass any country but to highlight the broader implications for African investors.

“I say this not to embarrass anyone, but because silence would be the greater disservice,” he said.

He questioned what such experiences meant for younger African entrepreneurs who lacked the financial resources, networks and influence available to established investors.

“If this is the experience of an investor with my resources, my networks and my grey hairs, what hope has the young entrepreneur with none of these?” he asked.

He warned that continued harassment of African businesses on the continent could encourage capital to move outside Africa.

“When African capital is harassed in Africa, we should not wonder why it flees to London and Dubai,” he said.

Sir Sam Jonah called on African governments to focus on implementing existing commitments under AfCFTA rather than creating additional protocols.

He said the success of the agreement would depend on whether member states could create conditions that make intra-African trade easier, faster and more competitive.

“Implementation is the new innovation,” he told governments participating in the forum.

“We do not need another protocol; we need the last one to work.”

He urged African economies to improve their competitiveness while removing unnecessary barriers that make it difficult for businesses to operate across borders.

“Make it cheaper and faster for a Ghanaian firm to sell in Lagos, Abidjan and Nairobi than in Rotterdam,” he said.

Sir Sam Jonah said the AfCFTA could be sustained by countries that honour their commitments, economies that produce goods and services that other African markets want to buy, and governments that protect African investors and workers as strongly as they court foreign investment.

Ghana News.title: Opoku-Afari: IMF programmes unable to address political economy roots of debt accumulation
Ghana News.content:
Dr. Opoku-Afari

A former First Deputy Governor of the Bank of Ghana has stated that given Ghana’s long history of International Monetary Fund-supported arrangements, observed surveillance shortfalls may also reflect limitations in programme design and the translation of diagnostic findings into binding reforms.

According to him, over the past two decades, several gaps have appeared recurrent.

He disclosed this in his paper titled ““How not to Miss a Crisis: Lessons from Ghana”.

He explained that IMF programmes could not consistently address institutional manifestations of deeper political-economy drivers of debt accumulation.

This include electoral competition and patronage-related spending pressures where rollover and liquidity risks were at times underweighted; stress-testing of domestic debt and its interaction with the banking system was limited; coverage of the wider public-sector balance sheet (including SOEs [State-Owned Enterprises], guarantees, and other contingent liabilities) remained incomplete; and the sovereign–bank “doom loop” was not always assessed in a comprehensive, integrated manner.

According to him, these gaps point to a broader methodological question: whether Ghana was appropriately treated as a Lower Income Country-DSF case throughout the period, given its level of market access and the evolving structure of its debt.

In particular, he said, the framework’s limited ability to quantify rollover, liquidity, and currency-related risks may have contributed to underestimation of the probability of rapid market closure—risks that became acute as investor confidence deteriorated following rating actions, including Moody’s downgrade in February 2022.

The former Mission Chief at the IMF continued that although macroeconomic surveillance did not completely ignore Ghana’s rising vulnerabilities, three limitations stand out.

First, the Debt Sustainability Analysis baseline paths tended to be optimistic, assuming sustained fiscal consolidation driven by domestic revenue mobilisation, which was mostly missed and robust growth while giving insufficient weight to plausible downside scenarios.

Second, the analysis did not fully internalise domestic-debt dynamics and fiscal–financial feedback effects, leading to an under-appreciation of rollover, liquidity, and banking-sector channels.

Third, IMF-supported programme design often prioritized near-term consolidation over reforms that address the structural drivers of recurrent debt accumulation—particularly in energy pricing, SOE governance, and tax policy and administration.

He concluded saying, a recurring critique of Ghana’s engagement with the IMF is that programme conditionality has historically favored fiscal consolidation over comprehensive structural reform.

Ghana News.title: Mahama invited for 65th anniversary of Non-Aligned Movement in Belgrade – Ablakwa
Ghana News.content:
President John Mahama has been invited by Serbian President Aleksandar Vučić to attend the 65th anniversary of the Non-Aligned Movement (NAM) in Belgrade, Serbia, according to a post by Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa on his Facebook page.

Ablakwa said he held a “really fruitful meeting” with the Serbian Ambassador to Ghana, His Excellency Milutin Stanojevic, during which preparations for the upcoming summit were discussed.

According to Ablakwa, the Serbian President has extended a special invitation to President Mahama to attend the anniversary celebrations scheduled for August 31 to September 1, 2026.

He said President Mahama will serve as Special Guest of Honour, largely because Ghana’s founder, Osagyefo Dr Kwame Nkrumah, was among the founding fathers of the Non-Aligned Movement.

The movement was formally established in Belgrade, then part of Yugoslavia, on September 1, 1961. Its founding leaders included Kwame Nkrumah of Ghana, Josip Broz Tito of Yugoslavia, Egyptian President Gamal Abdel Nasser, Indian Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru and Indonesian President Sukarno.

Ablakwa said the foundational ideals of the NAM remain relevant 65 years after its establishment.

He highlighted principles including respect for territorial integrity and sovereignty, non-aggression, non-interference in domestic affairs, equality, nuclear disarmament and peaceful coexistence.

Quoting Dr Nkrumah, Ablakwa recalled the former Ghanaian leader’s famous declaration: “We face neither East nor West; We face forward.”

He added that Ghana would continue to cherish and uphold the enduring principles of Non-Alignment as espoused by Dr Nkrumah.

Ghana News.title: Ghana’s debt sustainability challenges persisted for 12 years, breached DSA indicators over period – Opoku-Afari
Ghana News.content:
Ghana’s debt sustainability challenges persisted and in several episodes intensified, particularly during periods without an International Monetary Fund (IMF) programme, a former First Deputy Governor of the Bank of Ghana, Dr. Maxwell Opoku-Afari has disclosed.

According to him, despite repeated recourse to the Fund for “policy credibility” and for liquidity or solvency support, debt sustainability remained fragile.

“Notably, several key Debt Sustainability Analysis (DSA) indicators breached their respective thresholds over 2010–2022”, Dr. Opoku-Afari disclosed in a paper titled “How not to Miss a Crisis: Lessons from Ghana”.

His article mentioned that the present value (PV) of public debt-to-Gross Domestic Product (GDP), which remained below the 55.0% threshold in the early 2010s, rose sharply after 2014 and persistently exceeded sustainable levels— reaching nearly 93% by 2022.

“During the 2015–2019 Fund programme, debt accumulation moderated, although the ratio remained above the benchmark”.

Similarly, the PV of external debt-to-GDP exceeded the 40% threshold from 2015 onward, reflecting in part the effect of exchange-rate depreciation on foreign-currency liabilities. The 2015–2019 Fund programme coincided with a modest reduction in this indicator, but it rose again during the COVID-19 period.

Dr. Opoku-Afari pointed out that subsequent debt restructuring reduced the foreign-debt burden and improved this metric. “Over the full period, however, the PV of external debt-to-exports remained below the 180 per cent benchmark”.

Again, liquidity indicators also weakened, whilst debt service-to-exports exceeded the 15% threshold from 2015, while debt service-to-revenue breached the same benchmark as early as 2013 and rose to more than 40% of government revenues by 2022.

Taken together, the former First Deputy Governor said these breaches point to systemic fiscal fragility, with solvency and liquidity risks reinforcing each other and ultimately contributing to debt distress and the need for restructuring.

In 2022, Ghana defaulted on its debt obligations, compelling the country to seek IMF support. This triggered the Economic Credit Facility (ECF) programme from the Fund.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”
