World.title: La Sociedad Interamericana de Prensa reconoce a Pilar Gil con el Premio Ejecutiva del 2026
World.content:
El audio de esta noticia utiliza una voz sintética generada por Inteligencia Artificial y podría tener algunas inconsistencias.

La SIP destaca el liderazgo y visión estratégica de la consejera delegada de PRISA Media

La Sociedad Interamericana de Prensa (SIP) otorgó a Pilar Gil, consejera delegada de PRISA Media, el Premio Ejecutiva del 2026, por su liderazgo, visión estratégica y destacada contribución al desarrollo y transformación de uno de los principales grupos de comunicación en español.

“Como consejera delegada y vicepresidenta del Consejo de Administración de PRISA Media, Gil ha impulsado una estrategia que combina la fortaleza de marcas periodísticas históricas con la innovación, la expansión de nuevas audiencias y la búsqueda de modelos de negocio sostenibles. Bajo su conducción, PRISA Media ha reforzado su presencia en mercados estratégicos de América Latina, ha promovido nuevas alianzas y plataformas de distribución”, detalló la SIP en un comunicado.

Gil se incorporó al grupo en 2000 e integra además los consejos de administración de Santillana, El País y el diario AS.

“Pilar Gil representa un liderazgo que combina experiencia, visión empresarial y capacidad de adaptación en un momento decisivo para la industria de medios”, afirmó Pierre Manigault, presidente de la SIP, en el comunicado. “Su gestión demuestra que la innovación y la transformación pueden avanzar de la mano de marcas periodísticas sólidas y de una estrategia de largo plazo para fortalecer la sostenibilidad y el alcance del periodismo”, agregó.

El Premio Ejecutiva del Año de la SIP reconoce a líderes de la industria de medios que, por su trayectoria, capacidad de gestión e innovación, realizan contribuciones significativas al desarrollo y fortalecimiento del sector.

La ceremonia de entrega se realizará durante la 82ª Asamblea General de la SIP, que tendrá lugar del 22 al 25 de octubre de 2026 en el Hotel Hilton Bogotá, en Bogotá, Colombia.

World.title: Dutch spy agencies to get more powers against foreign enemies
World.content:
The Netherlands’ two intelligence agencies are to gain new powers to track and disrupt “obvious adversaries” such as Russian hackers, Chinese spies and Iranian operatives without asking permission in advance, under a draft law published by the cabinet.

The domestic intelligence service AIVD and military intelligence service MIVD would no longer need prior sign-off to follow an individual hacker online. “By then they have already gone,” said defence minister Dilan Yesilgöz.

Once a foreign service is formally designated an adversary, the agencies could pursue anyone thought to be working for it, with a watchdog checking afterwards whether their actions were lawful and able to halt operations it considers inappropriate.

The plans have raised concerns about the privacy of Dutch citizens. Yesilgöz said oversight would remain in place. “Putin and his cronies do not deserve our privacy, but the people of the Netherlands do,” she said.

The bill would also let the agencies work more closely with Dutch banks, universities and online platforms, warn them of risks and, in some cases, demand information from them. Interior minister Pieter Heerma, who is responsible for the AIVD, declined to name specific organisations.

It follows the previous cabinet’s abandoned plan to screen 8,000 foreign researchers and students for espionage risks, which was judged unworkable. Oversight of the two agencies would be merged into a single body.

The draft is open for public consultation before it goes to parliament.

World.title: “We have to stop this man”: mass sperm donor fathered 121 kids
World.content:
A Dutch man has fathered at least 121 children as a sperm donor and is still active, according to an investigation by current affairs programme Nieuwsuur – the latest in a line of mass donors who exploit a gap in the legal rules by working outside licensed clinics.

The man, who is 43 and from the Groningen region, donated to several sperm banks but operates mainly online, approaching women directly. Investigators spoke to dozens of affected mothers, and said the true figure is probably far higher.

They also found that the man sat on a government commission that evaluated the Dutch donor law in 2019. It is unclear how or why he was appointed.

Dutch clinics may not use a single donor for more than 12 families. But donors and would-be parents who arrange conception privately are bound by no legal maximum, a gap that lets a determined donor father dozens or hundreds of children unchecked. Nieuwsuur revealed last year that clinics had produced at least 85 mass donors.

The health and youth care inspectorate IGJ, part of the health ministry, said it did not know the man and called the case “very undesirable”. But a spokesperson said the inspectorate oversees care provided in clinics, not conception arranged in the private sphere.

Evasive behaviour

The donor children’s foundation Stichting Donorkind and several of the mothers want him to stop. “We have to stop this man,” they told the programme.

The mothers say he lies about how many children he has fathered, growing evasive or hinting he will break off contact when pressed – leverage that matters to women who want their child to be able to know their biological father one day.

Some of the women told Nieuwsuur he sent them sexually suggestive messages, offering to help conceive via the “natural method.” One mother from the Randstad who tried to report him said the police were no help. “The police just stared at me blankly,” she said.

Traces abroad

There are also signs that the same man has fathered children abroad. One mother traced several children in Germany through an online DNA database, and the man has donated at a Danish sperm bank.

The man declined to be interviewed, saying he wanted any contact to run anonymously through the mothers or official bodies. He asked for privacy for himself and the families, and would not confirm how many children he has conceived.

The most notorious Dutch case remains that of Jonathan Meijer, who fathered some 550 children worldwide and was ordered by a court to stop in 2023.

World.title: Majority of student rooms priced well over the legal limit
World.content:
The majority of student rooms on the Netherlands’ biggest rental platform, Kamernet, are being advertised at prices well over the legal limit – an average of €239 a month, and more than €400 in Amsterdam – investigative outlet Argos has found. Local councils are not intervening and say they have no power to do so.

Argos compared rent on 2,637 ads against the maximum each room is legally allowed to charge. Six in ten rooms were priced above the legal maximum over July and August, with landlords of overpriced rooms asking an average of €239 a month more than the rules permit.

In some cities, like Amsterdam, where the average room costs nearly €1,000 a month, 97% of the rooms Argos sampled were above the cap, by an average of €421 a month. In Utrecht the figure was 72%.

Utrecht and Nijmegen issued no fines and lowered no rents last year, while Rotterdam and The Hague were the exceptions, acting far more often.

Amsterdam council reaction

Since the Affordable Rent Act 2025 was introduced, which caps prices by a points system based on a room’s size and features, councils have been required to intervene – something the investigation found is not being done in many cities.

A spokesperson for Amsterdam council housing executive Zita Pels told DutchNews that the council cannot take legal action on advertising alone – an illegal rent must already be in force before it can do something. So students must first get into an illegally high rental contract before they can be helped.

The spokesperson also said the council “strongly opposes” the way people “shamelessly” exploit the housing crisis in Amsterdam, but that it unfortunately cannot do more about the advertising problem.

They also said the council itself advertises on rental platforms, attends student events, and visits tenants at home, because many people are reluctant to report overcharging for fear of losing their room.

In March, Amsterdam council also imposed a €45,000 penalty on the manager of a student complex in Amsterdam’s Zuidoost district for a range of violations, the council highlighted, including excessive rents. The landlord can still object.

There is a tenant advice foundation called !Woon that the council subsidises. Its 2025 report records more than 19,000 contacts about rent or service charges and 575 reports of serious landlord misconduct, and lists cases it has won, including 21 rulings against a single landlord, one of which cut a rent from €1,076 to €280.

The council’s own enforcement report to councillors, published in May, shows direct action on rents is a small part of the picture. Of 726 complaints under the new rental laws in 2025, 96 concerned rent levels; 167 were passed to !Woon and 102 fell outside the rules. The bulk of the council’s 1,836 enforcement outcomes last year involved empty or misused homes, not overcharging.

World.title: It ain’t pretty: botched Botox on the rise in country’s youth
World.content:
Just as the new school year gets underway, the Dutch Health and Youth Care Inspectorate (IGJ) has warned about a five-fold increase in complaints resulting from failed cosmetic treatments involving Botox and other dermal fillers.

The IGC received 175 reports of failed treatments, up from some 35 per year in the preceding years. The skyrocketing numbers, they say, are largely due to increased demand for the procedures among youth looking for fuller lips and less wrinkles and a surge in places providing them.

Young people, IGJ inspector Rosemarie Jansen told broadcaster NOS, were especially vulnerable to cutthroat rates among providers who often lack the mandatory qualifications to provide them. That “lowers the threshold for young people, precisely because they do not have much to spend,” she said.

Some 67% of the complaints involved a practitioner who was not legally qualified or lacked the necessary medical competence.

In the Netherlands, a doctor is required to be present when a patient receives such cosmetic treatments, something which is lacking in the proliferation of places offering them.

The botched procedures have led to swelling and drooping eyelids, lip inflammation and allergic reactions. The ICJ says the number of complaints is likely unreported due to the shame many young people feel about getting cosmetic work.

Fillercheck.nl

To help combat the problem, the IGC, along with Tilburg University and the consumer platform wiemooiwilzijn, have created fillercheck.nl, a website where those seeking cosmetic treatments can go down a four-part checklist that gets them thinking about the treatment, lets them find out if their provider is qualified and, says the IGC, help them recognize red flags.

The Inspectorate is taking their message via pop-up clinics disguised as cosmetic treatment centres to students in Amsterdam, Nijmegen, Zwolle and Breda this week and next – just in time for university introduction weeks.

World.title: More deposit bottles returned but still short of legal mandate
World.content:
Although more people are returning their cans and bottles for recycling and cash back, the mandatory collection target of 90% is not being met, just as it hasn’t since the deposit scheme was first introduced five years ago.

According to Verpact, the foundation that oversees the statiegeld (deposit) system in the Netherlands, based on figures from the first half of the year, 78% of deposit bottles will be collected in 2026; for cans, that number jumps to 86%.

Since 2021, when the deposit scheme for bottles and cans was first introduced, producers and importers have been required by law to collect and recycle 90% of plastic bottles and cans.

While the percentages have been increasing – last year 77% of plastic bottles and 83% of cans were returned – the 90% target is unlikely to be reached again this year, according to Verpact’s preliminary 2025 annual report.

“We cannot continue doing what we have always done and expect to continue meeting our statutory targets in the future,” said Hester Klein Lankhorst, Verpact’s chair of the executive board, of the changing European landscape.

She said companies currently not taking a deposit should be obliged to and calls for more recycling capacity in Europe. She sees a ban on selling cans and bottles without deposits as a possible future step.

Fines

Following the Human Environment and Transport Inspectorate’s (ILT) threat of fines this year, Verpact came up with additional incentives for consumers: a national sweepstakes with cash prizes for those returning their bottles and cans and even a lottery to encourage people to do so.

Verpact also added 2,500 more drop-off points this year, saying it expects to meet its legal requirement to have 5,400 new collection points in supermarkets and public places before the end of the year.

Verpact invested more than €220 million in the deposit system last year and paid €626 million to consumers who returned their recyclables. But by failing to hand in all their bottles and cans, Dutch consumers left €129 million unclaimed. That money goes back into the deposit system and is spent on items like new return machines.

The Netherlands has some 9,900 deposit-return points and 23,000 donation points.

And although coffee capsules are not part of the cash-back scheme, since January 1, 2026, consumers can return them – along with household aerosols (think deodorant or whipped cream cans) – in the PMD bins (plastic packaging, metal packaging, and drink cartons) due to an agreement between Verpact and the Coffee Capsule Recycling Association, reports NU.nl.

World.title: Home buyers file nearly 1,000 complaints over unfair bidding
World.content:
House hunters in the Netherlands are still being pressured to raise their offers and kept in the dark about rival bids, according to almost 1,000 complaints logged since February by home owners’ association Vereniging Eigen Huis (VEH).

The association’s complaints hotline, which it reopened in February after a five-year gap, received 921 reports from buyers and sellers by early July, broadcaster NOS reported.

Buyers describe being pushed towards higher offers after being warned about competing bids that later could not be found in the official log, and winning bids being entered after the deadline or by the agent.

One buyer told NOS he was urged to add €10,000 to a €265,000 offer to secure a house, then found no higher bid recorded afterwards.

VEH says voluntary industry guidelines have failed to protect consumers. It found in May that most buyers experience unfair bidding. It wants the buying process written into law to improve transparency.

Buyers and sellers must be able to trust that the process is fair and verifiable, said VEH director Cindy Kremer, which is why statutory rules are needed “with supervision and enforcement, so breaches actually carry consequences”.

The government has promised action but not yet delivered anything concrete. Housing minister Elanor Boekholt-O’Sullivan signalled in the spring that she would put regulatory options to parliament over the summer – plans which have yet to appear.

The estate agents’ associations are not resisting changes. The largest, NVM, said the reopened hotline could be useful but defended its own bidding protocol. Rival body Vastgoed Nederland said it was for the government to set firm rules.

PVV MP Jeremy Mooiman is drafting a private member’s bill to set a statutory standard for all agents.

World.title: Number of young people relying on benefits continues to rise
World.content:
The number of people claiming welfare benefits in the Netherlands has risen for the third year in a row, with the steepest increase among people under 27 years old, according to figures from national statistics agency CBS.

At the end of the second quarter of 2026, 413,000 people below the state pension age were receiving welfare, 4,000 more than a year earlier.

The total has now risen year-on-year for 12 consecutive quarters, though it remains slightly below its level before the coronavirus pandemic.

Sharpest rise among under-27s

Claims went up across all age groups, but fastest among the young. The number of under-27s on welfare rose 5.7% from a year earlier to 44,000, and has climbed by 27% since late 2022.

Among people aged 45 up to the state pension age, the number edged up 0.2% to 229,000, while 140,000 people aged 27 to 45 were claiming, a rise of 0.8%.

In the first quarter, more people started claiming welfare than left it – the 14th quarter in a row that arrivals rose faster than departures.

Welfare, which is administered by local councils, is paid to people of working age with no other income. The rise comes as unemployment has grown, reaching 4% earlier in the summer.

A dispute has emerged between Poland’s government and the office of opposition-aligned President Karol Nawrocki over whether Poland would be willing to host allied nuclear weapons. Deputy defence minister Paweł Zalewski announced on Thursday that Poland wants to participate in the US-led NATO nuclear sharing programme, but without actually hosting warheads. That prompted criticism from Nawrocki’s senior foreign policy aide, Marcin Przydacz, who says Poland should host such weapons. Those remarks triggered criticism from the national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS), Poland’s main opposition party. Former PiS defence minister Mariusz Błaszczak said that refusing to host warheads “in practice means renouncing participation in nuclear sharing”. “Poland should strive for full participation in nuclear sharing,” added Błaszczak. “This is not a matter of Poland possessing its own nuclear weapons, but of strengthening NATO’s nuclear deterrence on the eastern flank.” Criticism also came from other sources, including retired Brigadier General Stanisław Koziej, who served as head of the National Security Bureau (BBN) of former President Bronisław Komorowski, who is an ally of the current government. Koziej called Zalewski’s announcement “an incomprehensible strategic mistake in the field of deterrence”. A ban on the use of fireworks that was introduced last year by Kraków, Poland’s second-largest city, has been withdrawn after the local authorities decided not to appeal against a court decision revoking it. Kraków had argued that the ban would boost the safety and health of both humans and animals. However, opponents of the measures, including the provincial governor, who launched the legal challenge against it, argued that it was excessive and undermined constitutional freedoms. Kraków bez zakazu fajerwerków. Miasto nie zaskarży wyroku WSAhttps://t.co/rPEYNhEMAQ — Fakty RMF FM (@RMF24pl) August 25, 2026 In November 2025, Kraków’s city council adopted a resolution banning fireworks, firecrackers, sparklers and other pyrotechnic materials being set off “for entertainment purposes”. The ban, which carried an exemption for last year’s New Year’s celebrations, applied in public spaces as well as private properties where the use of fireworks was deemed to impact public places. The city said the ban aimed to “protect the life, health and peace of residents” and “ensure public safety”, adding that the discharge of pyrotechnics created noise and air pollution and could pose a threat to the health and life of humans and animals. Some councillors also argued that a ban would benefit residents suffering from trauma, including World War Two veterans and Ukrainian refugees. The city’s then mayor, Aleksander Miszalski, cited a city poll finding that 67.5% of respondents supported a year-round ban on fireworks and 31.2% opposed it. However, the measures were criticised by the head of the Association of Pyrotechnic Importers and Distributors, Marta Smolińska, who told news service Puls Krakowa that the ban was an “extreme solution” that would hurt local businesses. She called instead for “promoting the responsible use of pyrotechnics”. In December, Krzysztof Klęczar, the government-appointed governor of the Małopolska province, of which Kraków is the capital, announced that he would challenge the ban in the Provincial Administrative Court. Klęczar argued that the measures may “violate the principle of proportionality of limiting constitutional freedoms and rights as well as the freedom…to conduct business activity”. National parks in Poland have appealed to revellers to refrain from using fireworks this New Year’s Eve to avoid awakening wild animals from their winter slumber. A number of cities have also called on residents to abandon the tradition to protect petshttps://t.co/T6RQHdsF9P — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) December 29, 2022 His arguments were endorsed by the court, which, in a ruling in late June, deemed the resolution introducing the ban “invalid” and ordered that the city of Kraków pay legal costs. The court said the ban “went beyond the competence of the city council” and “violated the principle of proportionality of the protection of constitutional freedoms and rights”. It added that it “was not necessary to protect health, life or public order”. While Kraków could have appealed against the ruling at the Supreme Administrative Court, it has decided not to take that step. An appeal “would probably have little chance of upholding the resolution,” spokeswoman Dominika Jaźwiecka-Bujalska told the Polish Press Agency (PAP). Poland's largest opposition group has proposed a law banning fireworks, arguing that they cause distress, and even death, among domestic pets and wild animals https://t.co/UVzFMv3IEn — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 23, 2021 At the national level, in 2021, Civic Coalition (KO) – which was then the largest opposition party and is now Poland’s main ruling party – proposed a law that would have banned the use of most fireworks and firecrackers to protect domestic and wild animals. While that legislation did not proceed beyond a parliamentary commission, two further bills seeking to limit the use of fireworks to protect animals are currently proceeding in parliament, reports local news service Portal Samorządowy. Several Polish cities have introduced their own restrictions, which in some cases have also faced legal challenges. Wrocław, Poland’s third-largest city, also introduced a ban in January, which was likewise revoked in an administrative court after facing opposition from the provincial governor, reports PAP. Year-round bans remain in place in the Baltic resort town of Sopot, where there is an exemption for 31 December and 1 January, and the southern mountain resort town of Zakopane, a popular destination for New Year’s revellers, where the New Year period is included. World.title: Polish Olympic Committee chief detained over links to collapsed crypto firm
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! The president of the Polish Olympic Committee (PKOl), Radosław Piesiewicz, has been detained as part of a criminal investigation into Zondacrypto, a cryptocurrency firm that collapsed earlier this year and was a major sponsor of Poland’s Olympic team. The development comes a day after Waldemar Żurek, Poland’s justice minister and prosecutor general, revealed that prosecutors are investigating possible crimes relating to Zondacrypto’s financing of various individuals and organisations, including PKOl, Piesiewicz, and figures from Poland’s right-wing opposition. Dziś w ramach śledztwa w sprawie ZondaCrypto zatrzymany został Radosław P. Prokuratura będzie przekazywała dalsze informacje po zakończeniu czynności z jego udziałem, prowadzonych w Śląskim Wydziale PZ PK. — Waldemar Żurek (@w_zurek) August 27, 2026 On Thursday afternoon, Żurek announced that Piesiewicz had been detained and would be charged. He said he was unable to reveal what the charges would be, but confirmed that prosecutors are investigating a €40,000 watch reportedly given to Piesiewicz by the former head of Zondacrypto, Przemysław Kral. Under Piesiewicz’s leadership, PKOl signed an agreement in 2025 with Zondacrypto that made the crypto firm the main sponsor of the Polish team at this year’s Winter Olympics in Italy. However, in April, Zondacrypto began to come under scrutiny after customers began reporting being unable to access their funds. The firm subsequently collapsed and Kral went into hiding abroad. Prosecutors estimate losses to its clients of at least 350 million zloty (€81.4 million). At a press conference today, Żurek confirmed that Piesiewicz had been detained in connection with the investigation into Zondacrypto, which concerns suspected large-scale fraud and other criminal activity. The development comes days after two leading media outlets, Wirtualna Polska and TVN, published a joint investigation in which they alleged that Piesiewicz received a watch worth €40,000 and other gifts from Kral. The gifts were allegedly given in exchange for Piesiewicz intervening on behalf of Zondacrypto with Poland’s consumer protection authority, UOKiK. Piesiewicz denies the allegations and says he bought the watch with his own money, with Kral simply helping facilitate the purchase. 🔴Szef Zondacrypto, prezes PKOl i złoty zegarek za 40 tysięcy euro Prezes Polskiego Komitetu Olimpijskiego Radosław Piesiewicz dostał od szefa Zondacrypto Przemysława Krala zegarek Patek Philippe wart 40 tysięcy euro oraz inne prezenty – wynika z ustaleń wspólnego śledztwa… — Wirtualna Polska (@wirtualnapolska) August 24, 2026 Piesiewicz, who became head of PKOl in 2023 under Poland’s former national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government, has long been a controversial figure. In 2024, after PiS had lost power, he publicly clashed with Prime Minister Donald Tusk’s new government following Poland’s poor performance at the Paris Olympics, where the Polish team finished with its lowest medal haul since 1956. This year, as Zondocrypto fell into crisis, it emerged that the company had failed to provide promised bonuses to Polish athletes following the Winter Olympics. In May, 82 of the 106 members of the Polish Olympic Committee supported a motion calling for an extraordinary meeting at which the sole item on the agenda was the dismissal of Piesiewicz from his position. He has so far refused to convene the meeting. Poland has finished @Paris2024 with just one gold and 10 medals in total – its worst result since 1956. The prime minister has suggested there are failings in how Polish sport is managed. But the head of the Olympic committee has blamed the government https://t.co/iS9OqF1RuB — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 11, 2024 On Wednesday, Piesiewicz and PKOl were among a list of individuals and organisations Żurek announced were being investigated by prosecutors over potential crimes relating to financing they had received from Zondacrypo. Most of them are linked to Poland’s right-wing opposition. They included the foundations of Zbigniew Ziobro, a deputy leader of PiS, and Przemysław Wipler, a former PiS politician now associated with the far-right Confederation (Konfederacja); conservative broadcaster Republika and its head, Tomasz Sakiewicz; and the Polish version of the American CPAC conference. Earlier this year, Tusk claimed that Zondacrypto’s financial success was “rooted not only in Russian money linked to…one of Russia’s most powerful mafia groups, but also to the Russian security services”. His ruling coalition has three times passed a bill to introduce tougher regulation of the crypto market. However, each time, it has been vetoed by opposition-aligned President Karol Nawrocki, who argues that the measures are too restrictive. Prosecutors are investigating possible criminal offences relating to financing by Zondacrypto, a collapsed crypto firm, of organisations and individuals linked to the right-wing opposition, including the Polish version of US conservative conference CPAC https://t.co/swceV864nA — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 26, 2026 On Wednesday, Tusk wrote on social media that “we now know why Nawrocki and PiS have blocked the cryptocurrency bill like maniacs”. “Cash for watches worth €40,000 euros, [financing] for media, election parties, foundations of right-wing politicians,” he continued. “And the ‘Zonda’ show is just getting started.” PiS figures have, however, denied any wrongdoing in relation to Zondacrypto. “I’m outraged by the suggestion that PiS was involved in anything illegal,” one of the party’s MPs, Piotr Kaleta, told news website Interia. He noted that no evidence had been presented and no indictments made against PiS politicians. “Instead, we have ministers threatening to hold others accountable, and nothing has happened. This is simply meant to cover up the incompetence of the current government.” Teraz już wiemy, dlaczego z uporem maniaka @NawrockiKn i PiS blokowali ustawę o kryptowalutach. Kasa na zegarki za 40 tysięcy euro, na media, wyborcze imprezy, fundacje prawicowych polityków. A przecież serial „Zonda” dopiero się rozkręca… — Donald Tusk (@donaldtusk) August 26, 2026 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Poland asks EU to fine Meta €250m over scam Facebook ads
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland has formally requested that the European Commission fine Meta, the owner of Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, €250 million (1.1 billion zloty) for failing to tackle fraudulent advertising on its platforms. Its decision follows a high-profile campaign by Rafał Brzoska, the billionaire owner of Polish delivery giant InPost, over scam adverts on Facebook that exploit fake images of him and other prominent Polish public figures, including President Karol Nawrocki. Platformy cyfrowe muszą ponosić pełną odpowiedzialność za swoje działania i dlatego zawnioskowałem o nałożenie na Metę kary w wysokości miliarda złotych. Po analizie materiałów, w tym tych otrzymanych od Meta, a także kolejnych doniesień medialnych o braku kontroli nad… pic.twitter.com/1zSZg8MGf4 — Krzysztof Gawkowski (@KGawkowski) August 27, 2026 On Thursday morning, digital affairs minister Krzysztof Gawkowski announced that he had sent a request to the European Commission to take action against Meta, including fining it €250 million. “Inaction and ineffectiveness in combating harmful s and fraudulent content targeting Poles will not be tolerated,” wrote Gawkowski. “I expect the European Commission to conduct the proceedings swiftly and impose the fine. There is more than enough evidence.” The minister also called on Meta itself to “immediately introduce effective tools to eliminate scams, fake s, and the promotion of illegal applications. This Wild West on the platform must come to an end”. Gawkowski shared an image of the first page of a letter he had sent to Henna Virkkunen, the European commissioner for technological sovereignty, security and democracy, in which he argued that Meta’s failure to combat fraud may violate the EU’s Digital Services Act. He pointed to a study by CERT Polska, a Polish state IT security body, which found that, of 122 adverts reported to Meta as being fraudulent, in 106 cases the company rejected requests to remove them. Gawkowski noted that the European Consumer Organisation has reported similar concerns to the EU. On Wednesday, Gawkowski also shared copies of correspondence he had exchanged with Meta earlier this month. In response to the minister’s concerns, the tech firm had argued that it “does not seek to profit from” fraudulent advertising and outlined steps it was taking to address the problem. Meta disclosed that, between July 2025 and June 2026, it had, in Poland alone, removed 380,000 examples of content and 137,000 adverts for violating its policies on fraudulent practices. It noted that the vast majority were removed before users even reported them. Meta przesłała odpowiedź o działaniach związanych ze zwalczaniem scamów i wskazuje, że niektóre dane przekazuje z zachowaniem ścisłej poufności. W państwie szanującym obywatela takie dane muszą być jawne i dlatego podjąłem decyzję o ujawnieniu treści pisma. W piśmie Meta… — Krzysztof Gawkowski (@KGawkowski) August 26, 2026 Gawkowski’s intervention follows a high-profile campaign by Brzoska, one of Poland’s richest people and who, along with his wife, former TV presenter and businesswoman Omenaa Mensah, is a prominent public figure. Brzoska and Mensah have long complained about the unauthorised use of their likenesses in fraudulent social-media advertising, especially on Facebook. In 2024, Poland’s data protection authority ordered Meta to stop displaying adverts that featured false reports of Mensah’s death to promote scams. Earlier this month, Brzoska renewed his campaign, highlighting an example of a scam on Facebook that used a fake image of him being handcuffed by police in his home. Tak działa koncern @Meta w Polsce-nieustająco tolerując fake newsy na mój i wiele innych publicznych osób temat… Może innym to nie przeszkadza, ale jeśli moje małoletnie dzieciaki wysyłają mi te screeny pytając "o co chodzi Tato?", to jak się polskiemu zarządowi tej gównianej… pic.twitter.com/rp4CUscah1 — Rafał Brzoska (@RBrzoska) August 14, 2026 Brzoska – who also pointed to examples of Facebook running fake adverts featuring other prominent Polish figures, including President Nawrocki – launched a petition calling for platforms that run scam adverts to be fined 150% of the revenue they received from them. The petition – which, at the time of writing, has been signed by almost 91,000 people – cited leaked data, reported by Reuters last year, indicating that Meta estimated 10% of its sales in 2024, around €16 billion, came from advertising scams or illegal products and services. In comments to Reuters, Meta said at the time that the estimate was “rough and overly inclusive” and that the actual figure was lower. But it declined to provide an updated figure. Nowy dzień i nowy scam serwowany bez żadnych oporów przez @Meta z Prezydentem @NawrockiKn w roli głównej. Ale to managerowie Meta (Robert Bednarski, Jakub Turowski,Tomasz Parfjanowicz i Ewa Tumanow) mówią,że nic nie mogą w tej sprawie. Jeśli chcemy temu powiedzieć stanowcze… pic.twitter.com/ZVZl04yYY1 — Rafał Brzoska (@RBrzoska) August 24, 2026 This week, Brzoska welcomed Gawkowski’s moves against Meta. He also noted that, while the minister’s letter to Meta had been addressed to Jakub Turowski, Meta’s director of public policy for Central and Eastern Europe, the firm’s response to him was unsigned. “First-class cowardice,” declared Brzoska, who has repeatedly published the names of four of Meta’s senior Polish managers, including Turowski. World.title: US provides equipment and training to protect Polish border from migratory pressures
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! We cannot do what we do without your support. The United States has donated $2.1 million worth of equipment for border protection, including drones and thermal imaging cameras, to Poland under an agreement signed on Tuesday. The Polish border guard says that the package is part of a wider US programme, worth an estimated €12 million, to support Poland and the Baltic states in response to the migration crisis engineered by Russia’s ally Belarus on their borders. Stronger border security strengthens our shared security. Today in Warsaw, the United States and Poland marked the donation of more than $2 million in U.S.-funded equipment to the Polish Border Guard @Straz_Graniczna . The donation, funded by the State Department’s @StateINL and… pic.twitter.com/8Mh1eHLo0t — US Embassy Warsaw (@USEmbassyWarsaw) August 25, 2026 “Stronger border security strengthens our shared security,” declared the US embassy in Warsaw, announcing the donation of equipment, which includes 45 drones and nine advanced thermal imaging cameras. “This is just the next step in our security partnership,” they added. “Additional equipment, training, and expertise will follow.” The Polish border guard also confirmed that the support includes training packages and bilateral study visits, as well as the delivery of 15 snowmobiles to Poland next year. On Tuesday, it also hosted a delegation of senior figures from the US Border Patrol and US Customs and Border Protection for talks on “exchanging experiences, strengthening cooperation, and implementing advanced technologies in response to migratory pressures”. Since 2021, Belarus has been encouraging and assisting migrants – mainly from Africa and Asia – to attempt to irregularly cross into the European Union over its borders with Poland, Lithuania and Latvia. Tens of thousands of attempted crossings have been reported each year. In response, Poland has strengthened physical and electronic barriers along the border with Belarus. It has also eased rules on the use of firearms by uniformed officers to protect the border, and has temporarily banned asylum applications by people who irregularly cross from Belarus. As a result of such efforts, attempted illegal crossings are down 98% so far this year, while Poland also claims to have a 100% success rate in apprehending migrants who do manage to cross. The number of attempted illegal crossings by migrants from Belarus to Poland fell from 15,500 in the first half of 2025 to 235 this year – a drop of over 98% Poland also now claims a 100% success rate in apprehending migrants who manage to cross illegally https://t.co/RFZkd7CeIk — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 20, 2026 After meeting with American officials on Tuesday, the Polish border guard said that the head of the US delegation, Jason E. Schneider, acting chief patrol agent for the US Border Patrol’s Rio Grande Valley sector, had praised Poland as a “model and benchmark” for dealing with migratory pressures. It also noted that Stephanie Holmes, the deputy chief of mission at the US embassy, had noted Poland’s role “protecting the entire eastern flank of NATO and [acting] as a guarantor of transatlantic security”. Belarus is a close ally of Russia, and the migration crisis engineered by Minsk on the EU and NATO’s eastern flank is seen as one element of the so-called “hybrid warfare” being waged by Moscow against the West. 🤝 Polska i USA wspólnie dbają o bezpieczne granice i stabilność całego regionu! 🇵🇱🇺🇸 W Warszawie odbyło się spotkanie kierownictwa polskich i amerykańskich służb, w tym U.S. Border Patrol. Wydarzeniu towarzyszyło podpisanie umowy z Departamentem Stanu USA, dzięki której na… pic.twitter.com/rN9umTfPfU — Straż Graniczna (@Straz_Graniczna) August 25, 2026 The Polish border guard reported that, as well as donating equipment, the US has since 2024 been providing and funding “advanced tactical and technical training”, including “courses in border protection tactics”, for Polish officers. Next month, they will provide training in operating the newly donated drones, which are being provided as part of a broader $12 million US programme to support Poland and the Baltic states in “direct response…to the situation on the Belarusian border”, said the Polish border guard. In January this year, Polish officials also conducted study visits to El Paso and Detroit in the United States to “learn about methods used for counteracting illegal migration on the US borders with Mexico and Canada”. A further visit to the southern US border is scheduled for November. Poland says that “specialists from the Middle East” have been brought to Belarus to dig tunnels under the border for migrants to cross into Poland. Four such tunnels have been discovered this year, including one last week that was used by 180 migrants https://t.co/4ConkQnj8z — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) December 16, 2025 In 2024, the EU itself announced that it would allocate €170 million to help member states neighbouring Russia and Belarus “counter hybrid threats from the weaponisation of migration”, which it said was being used “as a political tool to destabilise EU society”. Poland was allocated the largest share of the fund, with €52 million. Last year, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen visited Poland’s border with Belarus, where she thanked Warsaw for defending Europe from “cynical hybrid attacks” being orchestrated by Russian President Vladimir Putin, whom she called a “predator”. Prosecutors are investigating possible criminal offences relating to financing by Zondacrypto, a cryptocurrency firm that collapsed earlier this year, of organisations and individuals linked to Poland’s right-wing opposition. Among those named in an announcement by prosecutor general Waldemar Żurek, who also serves as justice minister, are Zbigniew Ziobro, a deputy leader of Law and Justice (PiS), the main opposition party, and the Polish edition of CPAC, an American conservative political conference. Meanwhile, a lawyer representing Przemysław Kral, who was Zondacrypto’s head when it collapsed, has revealed that his client is cooperating with prosecutors. That lawyer, Roman Giertych, is also a prominent politician in Poland’s main ruling party, Civic Coalition (KO). Mamy przełom w śledztwie dotyczącym ZondaCrypto. Połączyliśmy w jedno wielowątkowe postępowanie sprawy oszukanych inwestorów oraz sprawę zaginięcia S. Suszka, prześwietlając nielegalne strumienie finansowe płynące w stronę polityków i powiązanych z nimi podmiotów. Więcej w… — Waldemar Żurek (@w_zurek) August 25, 2026 Zondacrypto came under scrutiny in April after customers began reporting being unable to access their funds. By late July, prosecutors had received several thousand notifications of suspected criminal activity connected with the exchange. Potential losses have been estimated at at least 350 million zloty (€81.4 million). In a statement published on Tuesday, Żurek said investigators had secured extensive evidence, questioned numerous witnesses, and carried out proceedings involving suspects who have already been formally charged, though he declined to identify them or disclose the charges. However, he added that there had now been a “breakthrough in the investigation”, including “looking into illegal financial flows towards politicians and entities associated with them”. Polish prosecutors have so far identified hundreds of possible victims and potential losses of at least 350m zloty relating to troubled crypto exchange Zondacrypto. The firm's oversight board resigned last week and many users say they cannot access funds https://t.co/ib4bGhzg2m — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) April 21, 2026 Żurek revealed that, “based on the evidence secured in the case, the prosecutor’s office is verifying information…regarding the possibility of crimes being committed in connection with the financing by Zondacrypto of” individuals and entities associated with the right-wing opposition. They included the foundations of Ziobro and Przemysław Wipler, a former PiS politician now associated with Confederation (Konfederacja), a far-right group; conservative broadcaster Republika and its head, Tomasz Sakiewicz; the CPAC conference; and Radosław Piesiewicz, head of the Polish Olympic Committee. CPAC and the Olympic committee were previously sponsored by Zondacrypto, while Republika sold extensive advertising space to the crypto firm. Żurek also said they were investigating potential financing by Zondacrypto of actions taken by individuals who helped fugitive former PiS deputy justice minister Marcin Romanowski. Both Ziobro, who served as justice minister when PiS was in power, and Romanowski are currently on the run from criminal charges in a separate case. They were initially given asylum by Hungary, then in May Ziobro fled to the United States. Romanowski’s current location is not confirmed, but he is believed to be in Transnistria, the pro-Russian breakaway region of Moldova. Prime Minister @donaldtusk says that, based on intelligence sources, Poland is now “99% certain” that fugitive opposition politician Marcin Romanowski is in Transnistria, a breakaway region of Moldova that has close links to Russia https://t.co/mdvmJpkFf7 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 18, 2026 Meanwhile, on Tuesday, Giertych confirmed that he was the defence counsel for Kral, who reportedly fled Poland after reports of wrongdoing at Zondacrytpo began to emerge. In an interview with state broadcaster TVP, Giertych said that his client is “cooperating with the justice system as best he can” and that his “motive is to mitigate his sentence”. Giertych is himself an MP for KO, the centrist party led by Prime Minister Donald Tusk. Giertych has previously acted as a lawyer for Tusk as well as members of his family. Kral had previously been represented by Bartosz Lewandowski, a lawyer who represents Ziobro and Romanowski. Giertych told TVP that he had been representing Kral pro bono since May. “I made a commitment to my voters that I would hold PiS to account,” he said. “Drawing people out from that side is the most effective way of holding them to account.” 🗣️ "Ta afera ujawni, czym było PiS. Czym była ta zorganizowana w moim przekonaniu grupa przestępcza, która podzieliła sobie kraj i kradła. (…) To ujawnienie zakończy mit patriotów, którzy walczyli o Polskę z Bogiem na ustach"@GiertychRoman w rozmowie z @DorotaWSch ⤵️ pic.twitter.com/1hVJafmRwQ — tvp.info 🇵🇱 (@tvp_info) August 25, 2026 In response to yesterday’s developments, Ziobro, in an interview with Niezależna, a news website also run by Sakiewicz, confirmed that his foundation had received 450,000 zloty from Kral’s law firm. “Zondcrypto collaborated with major media outlets, sports clubs, social organisations and other reputable entities…All of this created the image of a large, legally operating enterprise,” said Ziobro, adding that he refused to accept any further money when public doubts arose about the company. Ziobro accused the current authorities of being too lenient towards Kral because he had “become politically useful”. “This is the desperation of a regime fighting for its own future impunity…This is being done even at the expense of the victims and the recovery of their money,” Ziobro said. On Tuesday, Sakiewicz noted that, while Zondacrypto had bought advertising on Republika, it had also done so with many other media outlets. He claimed that Kral was now “under the thumb of the current authorities” and “will say whatever is convenient” to get out of his “difficult situation”. Czy pod pozorem rozliczania jednej afery Tusk z Giertychem właśnie tworzą kolejną? O tym mówię w wywiadzie. https://t.co/7Suu9SbCS3 — Zbigniew Ziobro | SP (@ZiobroPL) August 25, 2026 The Zondacrypto case has become entangled in a wider political dispute, with senior government officials alleging that the company had links to illicit financial networks and that money associated with it was used to support political and public initiatives connected to the right-wing opposition. During a speech in parliament in April, Prime Minister Donald Tusk alleged that the company’s financial success was “rooted not only in Russian money linked to…one of Russia’s most powerful mafia groups, but also to the Russian security services”. The allegations have fed into a broader dispute over cryptocurrency regulation. Opposition-aligned President Karol Nawrocki has vetoed government legislation aimed at introducing tighter regulation of the crypto market three times. The president argued that the bill threatened citizens’ freedoms and could drive Polish companies abroad. The government, however, said the lack of regulation left consumers vulnerable to unscrupulous operators and without adequate protection. World.title: Polish far-right leader charged with Holocaust denial for calling Auschwitz gas chambers “fake”
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Polish far-right leader Grzegorz Braun has been charged with denying Nazi crimes, a criminal offence in Poland that carries a prison sentence of up to three years. The charges relate to statements last year in which Braun, who has a long history of promoting antisemitic conspiracy theories, suggested that the gas chambers at Auschwitz, which was the Nazis’ main killing centre during the Holocaust, are “fake”. Komunikat o przedstawieniu posłowi do Parlamentu Europejskiego zarzutów publicznego i wbrew faktom zaprzeczania zbrodniom ludobójstwa popełnionym w niemieckim nazistowskim obozie koncentracyjnym i zagłady KL Auschwitz-Birkenau w Oświęcimiu. https://t.co/nLq3XKnXCK — IPN Kraków (@ipn_krakow) August 25, 2026 On Tuesday morning, Braun was summoned to appear as a suspect at the Kraków branch of the Institute of National Remembrance (IPN), a state historical body that has the power to prosecute crimes relating to the periods when Poland was under Nazi and communist rule. A group of his followers gathered outside the building to express their support for Braun, who finished fourth in last year’s presidential elections. Since then, his Confederation of the Polish Crown (KKP) party has risen to around 9% in polls, making it a potential kingmaker after next year’s parliamentary elections. After meeting with Braun, IPN prosecutor Robert Janicki announced that they had presented him with charges for “publicly and contrary to the facts denying the crimes of genocide committed by officers of the Third Reich in the German concentration and extermination camp KL Auschwitz-Birkenau”. The charges relate to two interviews Braun gave in July last year. He declared that “Auschwitz with its gas chambers is unfortunately a fake” and said that claims about the use of gas chambers are part of a “propaganda narrative” supporting a “quasi-religious cult”. In fact, gas chambers were used at Auschwitz, which was located in German-occupied Poland, to kill around 900,000 people, the vast majority of them Jews. Janicki noted that Braun’s remarks “clearly contradict common historical knowledge based on documents, witness accounts, perpetrators’ statements and findings from past criminal proceedings”. Far-right leader Grzegorz Braun says the gas chambers at Auschwitz are “fake” and it is a “fact” that Jews have committed ritual murder. Prosecutors have launched an investigation into whether he violated Poland's law against denying Nazi crimes https://t.co/7UUKzH5ndG — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 10, 2025 When Braun originally made his remarks, they were widely condemned in Poland, which suffered enormously under German occupation during World War Two. Justice minister Waldemar Żurek asked the European Parliament, where Braun sits as an MEP, to lift his legal immunity so he could be charged. “For me, it is a scandal that, in a country that suffered such enormous war losses, there is a politician who can deny historical facts that are so painful for Poles,” said Żurek at the time, quoted by the Onet news website. “I won’t let this go. We must bring such people to justice.” In March, the European Parliament approved Żurek’s request, allowing Braun to face charges in relation to his Auschwitz comments, as well as for other alleged crimes. The European Parliament has again voted to strip Polish far-right leader Grzegorz Braun of immunity to face further charges for Holocaust denial as well as various antisemitic, anti-Ukrainian and anti-LGBT incidents during last year's presidential campaign https://t.co/4EHVEuSDnM — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 26, 2026 On Friday last week, the district prosecutor’s office in Warsaw charged Braun with those other crimes, including the theft of Ukrainian and EU flags he tore down and vandalism of an LGBT+ exhibition being displayed in parliament. In a separate case, in February this year, Żurek also asked the European Parliament to strip Braun of immunity to face charges of denying Nazi crimes over another incident in which he called the gas chambers at both Auschwitz and Majdanek, another Nazi-German camp in occupied Poland, “fake”. Meanwhile, Braun is already on trial in Poland for four other alleged crimes, including using a fire extinguisher to attack a Jewish Hanukkah ceremony in the Polish parliament in December 2023. The trial of Polish far-right leader Grzegorz Braun for his attacks on a Hanukkah celebration in parliament and a Holocaust lecture has begun. Polish state defence firm Mesko has signed an 8 billion zloty (€1.9 billion) agreement to supply its Piorun man-portable air-defence systems to the armed forces of Poland, Norway, Lithuania and Latvia. The deal is being financed through the European Union’s SAFE mechanism. The agreement represents the largest-ever purchase of Pioruns, which have become an export hit for Mesko after proving their worth during Ukraine’s defence against Russian aggression. The purchase is being funded through SAFE, which provides loans at preferential terms for defence spending. While SAFE can be used individually by countries to make purchases for their own armed forces, some funds are designated for joint procurement by groups of countries (including non-EU member Norway). “Our partners from Lithuania, Latvia and Norway have decided to purchase from Poland,” declared deputy defence minister Magdalena Sobkowiak-Czarnecka, who oversees Poland’s participation in SAFE. “We are a leader in the SAFE mechanism and are the first to create such agreements. Since SAFE launched in May, the firm’s staffing, which stood at 3,200 by the end of last year, has increased by around 200, added the minister. Poland is by far the largest recipient of SAFE funds, with around €44 billion. World.title: Slavia Prague to Face Bayern Munich, Arsenal and Porto in Champions League
World.content:
Slavia Prague have learned their eight opponents for the 2026/27 UEFA Champions League league phase following Thursday’s draw in Monaco.

Slavia will play four matches at home at Eden Arena and four away.

At home, Slavia will welcome Arsenal, Aston Villa, Villarreal and Lens. Their away fixtures will take them to Bayern Munich, Porto, Fenerbahçe and Sabah Baku in Azerbaijan.



The most high-profile home fixture will be against Arsenal, the reigning Premier League champions. Slavia also faced the London club in last season’s Champions League campaign, making the return meeting at Eden Arena particularly notable.

The toughest away assignment is likely to come in Munich, where Slavia will face six-time European champions Bayern at the Allianz Arena. The team will also travel to Portugal to meet Porto and to Istanbul for a match against Fenerbahçe.

The longest trip of the league phase will be to Baku to face Azerbaijani champions Sabah, who are making their debut in the Champions League league phase.

How the Champions League league phase works

The 2026/27 competition is being played under UEFA’s new league-phase format for the third consecutive season. Instead of a traditional group stage, all 36 teams are placed in one league table.

Each club plays eight matches against eight different opponents, with two opponents drawn from each of the four seeding pots. Every team has four home and four away games.

The top eight teams in the final standings will advance directly to the round of 16. Teams finishing ninth to 24th will enter a knockout playoff for the remaining eight places, while clubs finishing from 25th to 36th will be eliminated.

The league phase begins on September 8–10, with six rounds taking place before the end of 2026. The final two matchdays will be played in January, with the league phase concluding on January 27. UEFA will announce the exact dates and kick-off times for each individual match later.

World.title: MINT Market Returns to Prague’s Náplavka with More Than 130 Local Brands
World.content:
MINT Market returns to Prague’s Rašín Embankment on Sunday, September 6, bringing more than 130 independent brands and makers to the Vltava riverbank.

From 10 a.m. to 5 p.m., visitors can browse a wide selection of independent fashion, jewellery, ceramics, natural cosmetics, illustrations and original accessories, with many of the products made by small Czech and Prague-based businesses.



The popular design market is also known for its relaxed atmosphere, food stalls and chill-out area. Admission is free, and the riverside venue is fully accessible. The event is suitable for visitors of all ages.

MINT Market has been supporting independent and local creators since 2010.

Over the past 16 years, the project has grown from a small market into a nationwide platform, hosting more than 450 events in over 20 Czech cities and bringing together a community of more than 1,500 designers and makers.

For visitors, the September event offers a chance to discover products that are often made locally and in small quantities, while meeting the people behind the brands directly.

View this post on Instagram A post shared by The best design markets in CZ (@mintmarket.cz)

“Supporting small and local brands has been one of the core ideas of our project from the very beginning,” says MINT Market organizer Lenka Šašková.

“We provide creators with a place where they can showcase their products and meet their customers, because nothing can replace a personal meeting.”

The full list of vendors and further information about the September market can be found on the MINT Market website. Updates are also available through the Facebook event and Instagram.

World.title: Historic Invalidovna Building in Prague Begins Major Reconstruction
World.content:
The long-awaited reconstruction of Prague’s Invalidovna has officially begun.

The Baroque complex in Karlín will undergo a major renovation costing CZK 2.15 billion, with work scheduled for completion in 2030.

The project is the largest investment in the history of the National Heritage Institute (NPÚ). Alongside the restoration of the historic building, two new extensions will be constructed on the southern side of the complex.



One will provide facilities for the Prague Philharmonic Choir, while the other will house technical infrastructure needed to operate the site.

Much of Invalidovna will remain open to the public

Once the reconstruction is complete, the NPÚ will use part of the complex for restoration workshops, laboratories, archives and study rooms.

An underground garage with space for 50 vehicles is also planned.

Around 80 percent of the complex is expected to remain accessible to the public. The restored site will include exhibition and conference spaces, visitor routes through the Baroque interiors, a café and facilities for children’s groups operated by Prague 8.

A new multi-purpose hall in one of the extensions will be suitable for concerts, conferences and other events. The modern section will also contain technical facilities that cannot be accommodated inside the protected historic building.

The courtyard and gardens will be opened through the original entrances.

A Baroque complex with a long military history

Invalidovna was built between 1731 and 1737 based on plans by Kilián Ignác Dientzenhofer, one of the leading architects of the Czech Baroque. The institution provided accommodation and care for war veterans and their families until 1935.

The original complex was designed at a time when European armies were beginning to develop more systematic forms of care for soldiers who had been wounded or disabled in war.

Military campaigns were often accompanied by outbreaks of diseases such as cholera and typhus, which could kill even soldiers whose battlefield injuries were not life-threatening. Separate psychiatric institutions were later established for veterans suffering severe mental trauma after their military service.

World.title: PIZZA! PIZZA! POP-UP Returns to Holešovice Market on September 3

World.title: Manifesto Market’s Craft Beer Returns for Its Third Edition

Prague’s beer lovers can look forward to one of the city’s biggest beer events of the year as Manifesto Market brings back its annual beer festival for a third edition.

Zichovec, Sibeeria, Chroust, MadCat, Fracek, Pivovar VIK and Berlin-based BRLO will each have their own pop-up tent, giving visitors the chance to explore a wide range of beer styles directly from the breweries.

The beer will be accompanied by food from more than 10 international kitchens at Manifesto. Visitors can expect everything from juicy burgers and tacos to spicy ramen and authentic Chinese roast duck, making it possible to turn the beer tasting into a full weekend meal.

World.title: More Czechs Are Living Paycheck to Paycheck, New Survey Finds
World.content:
The number of Czechs who have nothing left from their paycheck at the end of the month is rising.

This year, 13 percent say they have no money left after covering their expenses, up from 9 percent last year. Meanwhile, 84 percent have at least a small amount left over, five percentage points less than in 2025.

The findings come from a May survey conducted by loan provider Provident Financial among 1,000 respondents.



According to the survey, Czechs’ ability to save is declining. Only 43 percent of respondents have at least 20 percent of their monthly income left after covering their expenses, down nine percentage points from last year. Almost half of Czechs nevertheless regularly set aside part of their paycheck each month.

At the same time, their overall financial resilience appears to be improving. More than a quarter of respondents have enough savings to cover their expenses for more than a year, compared with just 15 percent last year. The share of people with no financial reserve at all has also fallen, from 18 percent in 2025 to 13 percent this year.

The gap between men and women in the amount of money left at the end of the month has also narrowed. This year, 45 percent of men have at least 20 percent of their paycheck left after expenses, compared with 59 percent last year. Among women, the figure has fallen from 45 percent to 39 percent.

The share of Czechs with enough savings to cover 12 months without their main source of income has increased sharply this year, rising by 11 percentage points compared with 2025. At the same time, the proportion of respondents whose savings would last less than three months fell to 12 percent, down from 17 percent a year earlier.

Men are considerably more likely than women to report having enough savings to cover at least six months of expenses. The figure is 63 percent among men, compared with 39 percent among women.

Education also appears to play an important role in financial preparedness. Seven in ten respondents with a university degree say they have enough savings to cover at least six months, compared with 43 percent among people with lower levels of education.

World.title: Not Ready for Summer to End? 3 Places to Take the Kids Before August Ends
World.content:
The end of the summer holidays is in sight. While school supplies, pencil cases and sports shoes are already making their way onto shopping lists, there are still a few days of summer left to enjoy.

Before the September school routine kicks in, here are three ways to make the most of the final days of August with the family.



Letni Letna

When: 12–31 August

Where: Prague, Letenské sady

Letenské sady is taking on a new look until 31 August, transforming into a colourful festival village. The Letní Letná Festival isn’t just about evening acrobatics for adults. It also offers a programme for younger visitors called Letní Letná for Children.

From morning until late afternoon, the huge children’s tent comes alive with fairy-tale performances and other activities. Kids can take part in creative and juggling workshops, explore an interactive play area made from recycled materials or take a ride on the iconic hand-carved wooden carousel.

Most of the children’s activities take place under the festival tents, so an unexpected rain shower won’t disrupt the day.

The festival also offers a “Night Watch” childcare service for children aged four and up. Parents can enjoy the evening programme while experienced entertainers look after their children.

When: 24–29 August

Where: Liberec and the surrounding area

Fancy a trip beyond Prague at the end of August? Head north to Liberec from 24 to 29 August, when the city hosts Crystal Valley Week, a celebration of Czech glassmaking and jewellery.

This year’s theme focuses on the interconnection of cultures, with the Czech glass bead at the centre of the programme. Children can also enjoy a free ride aboard the special Crystal Tram, which has been decorated this year to resemble a long-distance train.

There are plenty of opportunities to make your own jewellery from glass beads, with workshops and craft sessions taking place throughout Liberec for both children and adults.

When: Sunday, 30 August, 11:00–19:00

Where: Prague, Ladronka Park

On the last Sunday of the summer holidays, skip cooking lunch and head to the F.O.O.D. Picnic in Prague’s Ladronka Park. The popular event returns for its 16th edition this year.

Entry to the festival grounds is free, with 120 food and farm stalls to explore, including food trucks. There is also a large children’s zone with games and creative workshops, as well as a raffle for younger visitors.

It’s a family-friendly way to spend the final Sunday of the holidays, combining food, activities and a relaxed atmosphere before the new school year begins.

World.title: Airbnb Accounts for 1 Percent of Prague’s Housing Stock, Analysis Finds
World.content:
Prague’s short-term rental market has grown into a professional business but Airbnb accounts for only a small share of the city’s housing stock, according to a new analysis.

In June 2026, around 7,878 entire apartments and houses in Prague were actively listed on Airbnb. With roughly 720,000 apartments across the capital, that represents about 1.1 percent of the total housing stock.

The situation is very different in individual parts of the city. In Prague 1, Airbnb-listed properties account for around one-fifth of all apartments, according to the Prague Institute of Planning and Development (IPR). In Prague 2, the share is around 7 percent, while in some outer districts it is below 0.5 percent.



The concentration of short-term rentals has also changed the nature of the market. IPR data show that hosts managed an average of two apartments in 2019. By 2024, that figure had risen to three, while more than half of Prague’s Airbnb listings were operated by hosts with at least five properties.

This means short-term accommodation is increasingly being run as a business rather than as occasional home-sharing.

Prague’s housing shortage is much larger

Despite the impact Airbnb can have in central neighborhoods, the analysis points to a much bigger problem behind Prague’s housing crisis — a long-term shortage of new construction.

Since 2006, Prague has accumulated a housing deficit of more than 91,000 apartments, according to the analysis. That shortfall is about 11.5 times larger than the number of apartments currently listed on Airbnb.

Even if every Airbnb property in the city were suddenly returned to the long-term rental market, Prague would still be short more than 83,000 homes.

The accumulated construction deficit reportedly became larger than the number of active Airbnb apartments around 2009 or 2010. Since then, the gap has continued to grow.

This suggests that Prague’s housing crisis began well before short-term rentals reached their current scale.

Tourism brings other concerns

Housing availability is also not the only issue surrounding short-term rentals.

Residents in central Prague have complained about noise, disruption and visitors staying in residential buildings.

The city also collects accommodation fees from short-term stays, although payment is not automatic because apartment owners must register and pay the fees themselves.

The debate over Airbnb in Prague therefore extends beyond housing. While short-term rentals can change the character of central neighborhoods and create problems for residents, the latest figures suggest that the city’s wider housing shortage is primarily the result of years of insufficient construction.

World.title: FBI alert leads Hungarian police to arrest British fugitive wanted for 20 years, court makes questionable decision – video
World.content:
Hungarian police have arrested a 60-year-old British man who had been wanted internationally for more than two decades over alleged sexual offences committed in the United States. The arrest followed a tip-off from the FBI’s unit based in Hungary, which alerted the Hungarian National Bureau of Investigation (KR NNI) on 25 August that the fugitive might be travelling through the country.

According to Hungarian police, US authorities had been investigating the man since 2003 in connection with alleged offences involving a minor, including coercion and solicitation to engage in illegal sexual activity.

The man reportedly fled the United States in September 2004 and was believed to have travelled to England. US authorities charged him in 2004 and issued an arrest warrant that November. An international wanted notice was subsequently issued in 2006, with the Washington Interpol office also seeking his arrest.

FBI alert triggers Hungarian investigation

After receiving the information from the FBI, Hungarian investigators identified a vehicle with British registration that was being used by the wanted man. They established that he had entered Hungary from Romania on 26 August and then tracked his movements.

The KR NNI alerted the Hajdú-Bihar County Police Headquarters that the vehicle, believed to be carrying the fugitive, was travelling towards them on the M3 motorway from the direction of Szabolcs-Szatmár-Bereg County. Several police units were dispatched to intercept the vehicle.

If you missed it: Missing Hungarian football star Buzsáky breaks silence after 10 days

Fugitive arrested near Polgár

Officers caught up with the vehicle near Polgár and directed it into a motorway service area, where they stopped and checked the driver. The police’s suspicions were confirmed: the driver was the 60-year-old British national wanted by US authorities.

He was arrested and taken to the Hajdúnánás Police Station, where he was placed in custody. Hungary’s International Criminal Cooperation Centre (NEBEK) coordinated the necessary international cooperation and assisted in bringing the man before a court.

Court releases the suspect

The case took an unexpected turn after the arrest. The KR NNI requested that the man be placed in extradition custody pending further proceedings. However, the court rejected the request and released him, according to Hungarian police.

The authorities have not provided further details about the court’s decision. The arrest itself brought to an end more than 20 years of efforts to locate the man, who had been internationally wanted since 2006.

World.title: EU Council President António Costa to meet Hungary’s Péter Magyar in Budapest
World.content:
European Council President António Costa will meet Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar in Budapest on Wednesday, 2 September, as part of a wider tour of EU member states. Costa announced the meeting in a statement on Friday, outlining the schedule for the second week of his tour of European capitals.

On Wednesday, the European Council president is due to meet Luxembourg Prime Minister Luc Frieden before travelling to Zagreb for talks with Croatian Prime Minister Andrej Plenković. He will then continue to Budapest, where he is scheduled to meet Magyar.

The Budapest meeting will be one of a series of discussions Costa is holding with EU leaders as the bloc prepares for negotiations on its next long-term budget.

Costa touring EU member states

Costa announced on Monday that he would visit most EU member states between 25 August and 17 September. The tour is intended to give him an opportunity to discuss key European issues directly with national leaders, including the European Union’s next long-term budget, formally known as the Multiannual Financial Framework (MFF).

The EU’s long-term budget sets spending priorities and funding levels for a seven-year period and is expected to be one of the bloc’s major political negotiations in the coming years. Costa’s meetings with national leaders are therefore aimed at gathering their views and building common ground ahead of the wider discussions at EU level.

If you missed it: Hungary sets 2030 euro target: Government reveals when budget deficit could fall below 3%

Budapest meeting comes amid major EU decisions

The meeting will be one of Magyar’s first high-level discussions with the president of the European Council since taking office as Hungary’s prime minister. The European Council brings together the heads of state or government of the EU’s member states and sets the bloc’s overall political direction and priorities. Costa has served as its president since December 2024.

His meeting with Magyar in Budapest is expected to provide an opportunity to discuss Hungary’s position on the EU’s future budget as well as European priorities. Costa’s tour will continue until 17 September, with the European Council president scheduled to meet leaders in most EU member states during the three-week diplomatic effort.

World.title: BREAKING: Hungary’s new asset recovery chief elected in secret vote
World.content:
Hungary’s Parliament has elected Anna Unger Róza as president of the country’s newly established National Asset Protection and Asset Recovery Office (NVVH) in a secret ballot.

Unger received 137 votes in favour, seven against and one abstention in Friday’s parliamentary vote. At the same time, MPs voted on the institution’s investigative deputy president. Katalin Tasnádi was elected with 139 votes in favour, six against and one abstention.

The votes mark a major step in the establishment of the new body, which is intended to play a key role in recovering and protecting public assets.

Unger and Tasnádi take their oaths

Following their election, Unger and Tasnádi both took their official oaths in Parliament.

Tasnádi briefly stumbled while repeating one of the particularly lengthy sections of the oath, which refers to the position of investigative deputy president of the National Asset Protection and Asset Recovery Office. Unger was seen smiling in the background, but Tasnádi subsequently completed the oath without further difficulty.

The two newly elected officials then signed their oath documents.

If you missed it: PM Magyar announces headquarters of new asset recovery office

Government figures congratulate the new leaders

Prime Minister Péter Magyar congratulated Unger and Tasnádi following their election, followed by Andrea Bujdosó, parliamentary group leader of the Tisza Party.

Most Fidesz and KDNP MPs were not present in the chamber at the time of the congratulations. Some representatives of the Mi Hazánk party were also absent, although István Apáti, a Mi Hazánk MP, congratulated the newly elected office holders.

The establishment of the NVVH has been one of the new government’s key institutional projects, with Magyar previously promising that it would have broad powers and a multi-member leadership structure.

The new office is expected to begin operating from the former Supreme Court building on Markó Street in Budapest, where it will initially use vacant offices after the Supreme Court moves to its renovated historic headquarters opposite Parliament.
