World.title: Iraq debuts first tech pavilion at LEAP 2026 in Riyadh
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — For the first time, Iraqi technology and digital enterprises will exhibit in a dedicated national pavilion at Saudi Arabia’s LEAP 2026, providing a new platform for Iraq’s developing tech industry to seek collaborations and investment from Saudi Arabia and the broader Gulf.

The Iraq Pavilion will be held from August 31 to September 3 at the Riyadh Exhibition and Convention Center in Malham, bringing together Iraqi enterprises in artificial intelligence, fintech, digital transformation, logistics, media, and technology services in one location.

The premiere is noteworthy for Iraq’s young technology economy, as LEAP has grown into one of the region’s biggest meetings of technology businesses, entrepreneurs, and investors.

This year’s event is expected to draw more than 201,000 people, including 1,800 global technology companies, 600 startups, and 1,900 investors.

– LEAP 2026 –

The Iraqi delegation includes Media World, part of March Holding, alongside Nass Al Iraq Holding, Digital Transformation Company (DTC), NAI, Theki Tech, Qafia Creative Agency, Daman Digital Platform, Zaeem Express Delivery, Advenature, MATIC, Rabee Securities and Dofied.

The companies represent an expanding Iraqi private sector.

Nass Al Iraq Holding’s activities include telecoms, digital transformation, real estate, and advertising, with its technology subsidiary DTC focusing on digital transformation and Theki Tech providing infrastructure and smart-building technologies.

Media World links digital content suppliers with telecom carriers in regional markets, while NAI concentrates on business-oriented artificial intelligence solutions.

Qafiya provides advertising and creative services.

Financial technologies will also be significant.

Rabee Securities, one of Iraq’s biggest securities brokerage firms, has worked on key Iraq Stock Exchange listings, and Dofied is creating digital cash-collecting systems to replace paper-based records.

Meanwhile, Zaeem Express symbolizes Iraq’s fast-increasing logistics and e-commerce infrastructure, with its delivery network delivering over 50,000 packages each day throughout the nation, according to pavilion information.

The participation of LEAP investors might make the event more valuable for Iraqi entrepreneurs seeking Gulf finance and regional partners. T

he conference offers specific startup and investor programs that link entrepreneurs with possible investors and firms looking for new markets.

The pavilion also comes as Iraq’s and Saudi Arabia’s economic ties expand beyond their usual emphasis on oil and government-to-government collaboration.

Bringing Iraqi technology businesses directly into Riyadh’s economic ecosystem might assist in strengthening linkages in AI, finance, logistics, digital services, and venture capital.

For Baghdad, luring Saudi and other GCC funds into technology would help diversify an economy that is still largely reliant on oil and generate more chances for Iraq’s private sector.

Tahaluf organizes LEAP 2026, which is currently in its fifth edition, with support from Saudi Arabia’s Ministry of Communications and Information Technology and the Saudi Federation for Cybersecurity, Programming, and Drones. Saudi officials see the event as a key component of the kingdom’s efforts to transform Riyadh into a global technology and investment powerhouse.

The Iraqi Pavilion will be in Hall 3, Booth H3.G160, for the duration of the four-day event.

World.title: Iraq-Gulf trade faces Hormuz strain, IRIS says
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — According to a new report by the Institute of Regional and International Studies (IRIS) at the American University of Iraq, Sulaimani, Iraq risks losing some of its growing commercial ties with Gulf states as the Strait of Hormuz is disrupted, forcing Iraqi traders to seek alternative supply chains through Turkey.

According to the August Iraq Economic Review, Iraq’s economic integration with the Gulf has expanded in recent years as a result of a mix of big government initiatives and smaller commercial networks that link Iraqi enterprises to GCC ports, suppliers, and logistical companies.

The Hormuz crisis is now challenging both.

Qatar is cited as one of the most notable instances of the investment trend.

According to the research, Doha has committed more than $9 billion in energy, logistics, infrastructure, and real estate investments since 2023, excluding its interest in TotalEnergies’ Iraqi energy project.

Saudi energy interconnection projects, UAE engagement in Grand Faw Port, Qatari investments, and the Development Road are all steadily strengthening economic ties between Iraq and its Gulf neighbors.

According to the report, Iraqi participation in the GCC is not required for this integration, which may be achieved via bilateral investment, infrastructure, and private-sector collaboration.

However, the analysis highlights a less noticeable issue affecting Iraqi traders.

Businesses that formerly depended on the UAE, notably Jebel Ali, to import Asian commodities and industrial inputs into Iraq are now experiencing greater transportation and logistical expenses as a result of the Hormuz interruption.

Some have started going north to Türkiye, where existing land links provide a more dependable option.

The move might have long-term effects.

According to IRIS, economic connections among smaller merchants are based on suppliers, credit, and trust, so if such networks relocate to Turkey, they may not immediately return to Gulf routes, even if circumstances near Hormuz improve.

Türkiye is especially appealing since its manufacturers can provide items, including building materials, at costs and qualities appropriate for the Iraqi market.

Traders contacted for the research said that certain Gulf-made alternatives were too costly for their consumers.

According to the paper, Baghdad could react by engaging directly with chambers of commerce, trade groups, and transportation firms to identify the real challenges that businesses face, rather than depending only on high-level agreements with Gulf states.

It offers temporary tariff reductions, speedier customs processing, and freight assistance for lower-value commodities traveling via alternate Gulf routes, notably Fujairah.

It also suggests establishing an Iraq-GCC platform to provide merchants with information on freight prices, transit times, and the profitability of routes via Jebel Ali, Khorfakkan, and Turkish ports.

The study also emphasizes that Gulf investment will be contingent on circumstances inside Iraq.

Baghdad must strengthen administration, lower business costs, shield investment from the militia economy, and deliver promised infrastructure if the present wave of Gulf interest is to result in long-term economic integration.

IRIS cautions that the opportunity for action is dwindling. If more Iraqi enterprises develop suppliers, financial contacts, and transportation networks in Turkey, reestablishing the Gulf-oriented trade lines created over the last decade may become more challenging.

World.title: Iraq offers oil loading off Oman in new route beyond Arabian Gulf
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraq is providing buyers the option of collecting petroleum from Oman, establishing a new loading point outside the Arabian Gulf as Baghdad strives to keep oil earnings coming despite disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz.

According to Bloomberg, SOMO, Iraq’s state oil marketer, is selling Basrah Medium and Basrah Heavy for September loading via ship-to-ship transfers along the Omani coast.

The tender concludes on August 28.

The agreement would see Iraqi petroleum delivered through Hormuz before being transferred to buyer boats near Oman, eliminating the need for clients to ship their tankers far into the Arabian Gulf to fill at Basra.

The decision comes after months of interruption in Iraq’s southern exports due to the US-Iran war.

Baghdad has offered high discounts to persuade importers to continue loading inside the Gulf.

According to Argus statistics quoted in publications, Iraq’s southern oil exports increased to roughly 1.4 million barrels per day in July from 100,000 bpd in May but remained much lower than pre-war levels of more than 3.3 million bpd.

The Oman agreement does not abolish Iraq’s reliance on Hormuz, since oil must still transit the strait.

However, it provides Baghdad with another method to lessen risks for purchasers while still protecting oil sales, which account for the majority of government revenues.

World.title: In shadow of Premier League, Serie A flexes financial muscle
World.content:
Rome – For Italian football this has been a chastening year, yet, ahead of a likely frenzy before their transfer window shuts on September 1, Serie A clubs have spent the summer asserting their place in Europe’s financial pecking order.

In both overall outlay and net spend, Serie A is a clear second among the ‘Big Five’ leagues.

While fee structures, conditional payments and financial sleights-of-hand can make the precise transfer values a little hazy, German site Transfermarkt on Thursday put Italy’s total outgoings at more than one billion euros ($1.165bn), far ahead of La Liga, at three-quarters-of-a-billion, and then the Bundesliga.

In all, the 20 Serie A clubs are almost 430mn euros in the red this summer, against just under 300mn euros in Spain. Both the Bundesliga and French Ligue 1 are in profit.

Of course, the ‘Big Five’ is a misleading phrase. European club football has become the Premier League and everyone else. English clubs have, so far, spent 3.2bn euros, more than the other four league put together.

The second round of the Serie A season opens Friday with AC Milan, for now restored to their role as Italy’s biggest spenders, hosting smartly-dressed yoyo club Venezia.

When Milan spent a reported 74mn euros to acquire Goncalo Ramos from Paris Saint-Germain, he became the most expensive Serie A signing since Juventus bought Dusan Vlahovic from Fiorentina five years earlier.

With Diego Moreira, coming from Strasbourg for 50mn euros, Milan have spent a total of almost 160mn euros, a whisker more than Juventus, with plenty of moves to come.

Under new boss Ruben Amorim, Milan opened the season with a 2-1 win at Torino.

On Thursday, Amorim did not rule out further recruits.

“We have to wait five more days until the transfer window closes,” the Portuguese coach, who started last season in the Premier League with Manchester United, told his pre-match press conference.

“If someone arrives, it will be because they can help us both now and in the future.”

– ‘Things will take time’ –

He made clear that the transfer market was not simply about spending to bring players in.

“It’s impossible to train during the week with 27 players. Nobody is going to be prepared, nobody is going to be satisfied, so there are some players that if they stay, they will not be part of the squad,” he said, when asked about reports that the club was trying to unload Fikayo Tomori, Youssouf Fofana and Santiago Gimenez.

After a summer in which Italy missed the World Cup, sparking a debate on the lack of talent in the national team, Amorim said clubs need to develope from within.

“We need to take time and believe in our young players,” he said. “We are going to have some problems with young players in some games, but big surprises happen.

“Everyone wants everything really fast and I’m a little bit old school. I think a lot of things will take time.”

Yet on the opening weekend, five of the six biggest spenders, Milan, champions Inter Milan, Juventus, Roma and Napoli all won. The exception were Fiorentina, trying to spend their way into the top end of the table, who crashed to Roma.

World.title: Tanker pays record $5.3 mn to transit Panama Canal: administrator
World.content:
Panama City – A tanker carrying liquefied petroleum gas has paid $5.3 million for priority passage through the Panama Canal ahead of El Nino-related restrictions, the waterway’s deputy administrator, Ilya Espino de Marotta, told AFP on Thursday.

South Korean company SK Gas paid the record sum for the G. Spirit to transit the shipping lane on September 1, two days before canal authorities reduce the number of transits due to the El Nino weather phenomenon, Bloomberg reported.

Panama on Tuesday became the latest Central American country to declare an emergency over El Nino, which has caused dwindling water levels in the canal due to a severe drought across the region.

El Nino is a weather pattern that raises surface temperatures in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific Ocean, generating global changes in winds and rainfall as well as erratic weather conditions.

It is also nudging up global temperatures in a year predicted to be the hottest on record.

Ships transiting the Panama Canal book their passage well in advance, and ships without bookings wait an average of five days to get through, but there is an auction where last-minute transits can be purchased.

The Panama Canal Authority said in a statement that the average auction price between October 2025 and February 2026 was around $55,000.

But in April, a vessel carrying liquefied natural gas paid $4 million to skip the line and avoid a wait to pass through the canal as the war in the Middle East boosted demand to move vital cargo through the waterway.

The shipping route, which handles five percent of global maritime trade, will cut the number of daily transmits from 36 to 34 from September 3, and to 32 later in the month.

World.title: Fresh flood warnings for disaster-hit Nepal and Tibet, 1,400 still missing
World.content:
Bidur – China and Nepal warned of fresh flooding risks, complicating rescuers’ search Friday for more than 1,400 people missing after a deadly deluge and landslides swept away entire villages along their remote Himalayan border.

Emergency teams have recovered 392 bodies after a devastating tsunami-like wall of freezing water and mud wiped out towns under a torrent of sludge, burying homes, smashing bridges and dams and sweeping away vehicles.

Many of the missing are foreign tourists, including trekkers in the Himalayan nation and scores of Hindu pilgrims to Tibet’s sacred snow-capped Mount Kailash.

The US Geological Survey (USGS) said the disaster was caused by a glacial collapse that triggered a vast flow of icy debris.

Climate change is causing glaciers to melt worldwide, increasing the risks of glacial lake floods and glacial collapses.

Emergency teams were racing to pluck survivors from affected zones, while Nepali soldiers used sniffer dogs to search for bodies buried under the suffocating dirt.

But their efforts are hampered by fears of new floods as water trapped by the immense piles of debris blocking the valley risks surging out.

Chinese authorities warned that a lake formed by the Wednesday’s mudslide faces a “high risk of breaching and sending floodwaters downstream”, according to state media late Thursday.

Kathmandu’s Flood Forecasting Division separately issued a “special notice”, warning of a growing lake behind debris left by the landslide and urging extreme caution.

– Thousands still missing –

Survivors in a makeshift Nepali hospital endured an agonising wait for news of their missing loved ones.

Kula Priya said she had lost everything when the deluge hit — including her eldest son, who is missing.

“I don’t care for wealth. I just want my son back. If any of you could rescue my son, please do it for me,” she said.

“I don’t know where to go. We had three houses, all of which were washed away by the floods.”

Nepali police say they had recovered 389 bodies.

A further 910 people, including 517 foreign tourists, are out of contact in the country.

Beijing said 100 Chinese citizens — not accounted for in that tally — are also missing in Nepal.

Indians make up the largest number of missing foreigners, while the United States said 90 of its citizens were out of contact.

Across the border in Tibet — where the only sources of information are Chinese authorities — officials say hundreds are missing and three have died.

Chinese authorities also said they had evacuated 555 stranded tourists — as well as 499 local residents –from Tibet.

Authorities have mobilised nearly 800 emergency workers, as well as sniffer dogs, speed boats, satellites and drones to help the rescue efforts, the state-run Xinhua new agency said.

– ‘Inland tsunami’ –

Nepal’s Prime Minister Balendra Shah, who urged the nation to “stand together” hours after the disaster, toured some of the hardest-hit areas on Thursday.

Shah told local authorities to “provide immediate relief to displaced families” and to open blocked roads, his office said in a statement.

Other foreigners out of contact include citizens from Australia, Britain, Malaysia, the Netherlands, Portugal, South Africa and South Korea, Nepal’s tourism board said.

The sudden rush of mud and debris was “like an inland tsunami”, travelling nearly 170 kilometres (105 miles) south into Nepal, said environmental historian Ruth Gamble, of Australia’s La Trobe University.

Buddhist spiritual leader the Dalai Lama, who lives in exile in India, said he would “pray for all those who have lost their lives”.

– Glacial collapse –

The USGS said a glacial collapse caused seismic activity and had “catastrophic” downstream impacts in Nepal and Tibet.

“This event was initially reported as a magnitude 4.4 earthquake,” it said, but the seismic recordings were analysed and it was found instead to be a “glacial collapse and debris flow”.

Scores of Hindu devotees from across the world are among the hundreds missing on the border, as many were on a pilgrimage to Mount Kailash, on the Chinese side of the border.

Logadarrsiny Raman, 26, from Malaysia, said her parents, aunt and uncle were on a pilgrimage but she lost contact with them after dawn on Wednesday.

Raman said the travel agency told her its last contact with the group of 17 Malaysians was at 8:18 am Nepal time, when they were travelling towards the Nepal-China border.

The flood crashed into the area where they last were soon after.

“I’m very anxious,” she told AFP. “My only hope is to hear back from them that they are safe.”

World.title: China’s help critical, but unlikely, for US to choke off Iran
World.content:
Beijing – The United States has threatened the “economic asphyxiation” of Iran, but analysts say that a successful chokehold would require unlikely cooperation from China.

Almost six months into the Middle East war, Washington this week laid out plans to expand sanctions against the Islamic republic, warning that any nation which continued to enable Tehran would become a “global pariah”.

China is among countries whose entities have already been hit by the sweeping US plan, with Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent telling Beijing to “get with the programme”.

But Beijing instead has defended its cooperation with Tehran and vowed to safeguard its interests.

The apparent impasse is likely to further strain ties between Beijing and Washington, ahead of an expected visit by China’s President Xi Jinping to the US capital in September.

– Oil ‘central lever’ –

Iran has weathered sanctions for decades, using complex international financial networks to evade restrictions.

Cutting off Iran “would certainly require China’s help”, said political scientist Dylan Loh of Singapore’s Nanyang Technological University.

Beijing is a key customer for Iranian oil, while “a good amount of their trade also relies on (the Chinese currency) renminbi, which can be outside the reach of US sanctions”, Loh told AFP.

Before the war, Tehran exported millions of barrels of oil a day, mostly to China.

“Oil is the central economic lever,” said Nino Lezhava, a fellow at the Washington-based Center for European Policy Analysis.

Although most ship traffic in the vital Strait of Hormuz is still blocked, China is not totally cut off from Iran’s crude thanks to the highways and railways of Central Asia, said Sun Degang, a professor of political science at Shanghai’s Fudan University.

Despite Chinese purchases being lower than before, they remain an important source of revenue.

“Simply continuing to… maintain commercial channels and provide alternative payment mechanisms can substantially reduce the effectiveness of economic isolation,” said Lezhava.

– ‘Economic sovereignty’ –

The United States is well aware of this.

Bessent said “no one is above the reach of US sanctions” when asked if Washington would target Chinese banks that do business with Iran.

However, while its sanctions announced on Monday targeted some Chinese entities accused of helping Tehran procure “critical technology”, Washington has so far held back from punishing major Chinese financial institutions.

The United States “can’t expect to obtain China’s support if it continues to implement sanctions on Chinese companies”, said Fudan University’s Sun.

“Sino-Iranian trade relations are legitimate and China will safeguard its economic sovereignty.”

China is already feeling some consequences from the Strait of Hormuz disruption, adding to economic strain from persistently sluggish domestic consumption.

Cutting off Iran would exacerbate that, as well as implicate Beijing in a messy conflict that has already weakened its strategic rival Washington.

Overall, China has “little reason” to cooperate with the United States on sanctions, said Chong Ja Ian, an associate professor of political science at the National University of Singapore.

– ‘Push back’ –

On Tuesday, China’s foreign ministry said its cooperation with Iran has “always been conducted within the framework of international law and should not be interfered with or disrupted”.

Chong said that “Beijing seems highly confident of its ability to push back successfully against the US”, were it pressured.

China has expanded its capacities to deal “precisely with such scenarios”, said Loh.

“China has its own tools to respond to protect its own interest as we have seen in the tit-for-tat export controls,” he added.

China and the United States spent much of last year embroiled in an escalating trade war but reached a fragile truce when the two presidents met last October.

A successful global campaign against Iran may require Washington “to provide incentives” to Beijing to join it, said Lim Tai Wei, a professor and East Asia expert at Japan’s Soka University.

China would only cooperate “if the costs of supporting Iran became significantly higher than the strategic and economic benefits”, said Lezhava.

World.title: Most Asian stocks advance as attention turns to Warsh speech
World.content:
Hong Kong – Asian stocks mostly rose Friday ahead of a closely watched speech by Federal Reserve boss Kevin Warsh that investors will be parsing for clues about the outlook for interest rates amid elevated inflation and no sign of an end to the Middle East crisis.

With the euphoria following Nvidia’s blistering earnings report petering out, the attention is back on the economy as debate surrounds if or when the US central bank will tighten monetary policy.

Last month’s Fed meeting saw policymakers keep borrowing costs on hold but with three of them dissenting in favour of a hike, and while the latest figures showed inflation easing slightly it remains well above the two percent target.

Worries that price rises will remain elevated for some time — fuelled largely by a spike in energy costs caused by the Iran war — have put upward pressure on long-term Treasury yields, making government borrowing increasingly expensive.

Traders are hoping Warsh’s speech at the annual meeting of central bankers and economic leaders at Jackson Hole, Wyoming, will give them an insight into decision-makers’ thinking.

However, his last major public appearance after the July meeting was widely panned as giving an ambiguous message, and analysts warn that his refusal to give forward guidance will likely mean investors are left disappointed.

Stephen Innes at Quintex Intel said the address — Warsh’s first since taking the helm at the Fed — was “the most consequential central bank speech left this year”, and comes almost three weeks before the next policy announcement.

“Recent data have reduced the immediate need for tighter policy, giving Warsh room to re-establish the Fed’s inflation-fighting message without signalling imminent action,” he wrote.

“The speech arrives against a difficult policy backdrop. Inflation remains above target for a sixth consecutive year, while Fed officials have begun debating whether tighter policy may still be required.”

Asian equity markets were broadly higher in early trade, with tech firms struggling to extend Thursday’s rally that came on the back of Nvidia’s profit blowout and bumper forecast, which soothed worries over the AI boom.

Tokyo, Hong Kong, Shanghai, Sydney, Singapore, Jakarta and Taipei all rose, though Seoul retreated along with Wellington and Manila.

Wall Street had provided a positive lead, with all three main indexes rising, though the gains were based entirely on the tech sector, which was the only one of 11 to advance.

Oil prices edged down but remain in danger of spiking further as investors await a breakthrough in efforts to reopen the Strait of Hormuz to tanker and cargo traffic.

US officials have vowed further economic pressure to make Iran open the waterway — through which about a fifth of world oil passes — after six months of war, but attempts at a diplomatic solution remain elusive.

World.title: 61% of children in India exposed to one more month of heat stress due to climate change: Study
World.content:
File photo: Heatwave in India

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: In India, 61 per cent of children, or 145 million, are exposed to at least one additional month of heat stress due to climate change every year, new global research has estimated.Findings published in the journal Science Advances show that climate change has doubled the number of children aged up to nine exposed to at least five total months of dangerous heat stress per year -- from 59 million to 118 million (50 per cent of children).An international team of researchers, led by those at Vrije Universiteit Brussel in Belgium, said the study is the first-ever analysis quantifying how heat exposure directly linked to climate change affects different age groups globally, both now and in the near future.Excess heat disrupts the human body's normal functioning, aggravates underlying diseases, and can lead to serious complications such as heatstroke, dehydration, and organ failure.The study focuses on humid heat, which is more dangerous than dry heat because it impedes the body's ability to sweat to cool back down, leading to dangerous levels of heat stress.Globally, up to 560 million children aged 0-9 -- 43 per cent of all children in this age group -- are living through at least one additional month of heat stress per year due to human-induced climate change, the analysis found.The exposure outpaces that for any other age group and is nearly triple the 190 million people (30 per cent) aged 60-69 experiencing the additional health threat, the researchers said.They added climate change is increasing humid heat the most in tropical regions and poorer countries, where populations are younger, and more children are therefore affected.South Asia, Southeast Asia, and West Africa are the regions with the highest number of children exposed to dangerous heat stress today, the team said."Climate change is already causing hundreds of millions of children to suffer from dangerous heat worldwide, posing severe risks to their health. Children in developing countries face (a) disproportionate exposure to climate extremes now and into the future, despite contributing the least to historical greenhouse gas emissions," lead author Rosa Pietroiusti, a PhD researcher at Vrije Universiteit Brussel, said."At the same time, poverty, inadequate housing, limited access to cooling, and overstretched health care systems leave many children with few ways to protect themselves from the heat," Pietroiusti said.The number of children affected by an additional month of dangerous heat is expected to increase to 620 million (49 per cent of all children) and 650 million (59 per cent) children under projected climate change scenarios of 1.5 degrees Celsius and 2 degrees Celsius of global warming, respectively.In India, 166 million children (74 per cent) are projected to experience at least one additional month of heat stress per year under a global warming of 1.5 degrees Celsius.The figure could be 169 million children (96 per cent) under a global warming of 2 degrees Celsius.

World.title: From Tagore's thread of unity to booming trade opportunity - how Raksha Bandhan became Rs 25k-crore business
World.content:
From Tagore's streets to 10-minute delivery: The business of Rakhi

When Tagore turned a ritual into protest

A festival with a turnover

Threads with a message, threads with a name

A thread for every trend

Minutes, not days

The vendors left behind

Opportunity online, obstacles offline

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

A hundred and twenty years of the same thread

In August 1905, as Bengal braced for a partition designed by the British to split its Hindu and Muslim population along communal lines, Rabindranath Tagore walked through the streets of Kolkata asking strangers to tie threads on each other's wrists. It was Raksha Bandhan, and Tagore had repurposed a domestic ritual, sisters protecting brothers, into a public act of protest. Hindus tied rakhis on Muslims, Muslims tied them on Hindus, and for one day at least, the colonial administration's attempt to engineer division through the Bengal Partition met a street-level answer in silk thread. The gesture was Tagore's response to a strategy of divide and rule that he saw threatening the nationalist movement at its foundations; the rakhi, in his hands, stopped being only a family custom and became a symbol of a shared, non-negotiable bond between communities.More than a century later, the thread has kept its symbolism but acquired a balance sheet. Raksha Bandhan is now one of the biggest festival-linked retail events in the Indian calendar, and the story of how it got there says as much about India's e-commerce boom, its gig economy and its small-manufacturing base as it does about siblings and sentiment.The Confederation of All India Traders (CAIT) estimates that Indiaâs rakhi trade could reach nearly Rs 25,000 crore this year.The broader Raksha Bandhan-related trade, including sweets, dry fruits, gifts, apparel, electronics, decorative items, puja articles and other festive products, is expected to cross Rs 30,000 crore nationally. Delhi alone is estimated to account for around Rs 4,000 crore, with major markets such as Chandni Chowk, Sadar Bazaar, Karol Bagh, Lajpat Nagar, Kamla Nagar, Rajouri Garden, Gandhi Nagar, Khari Baoli and Laxmi Nagar seeing increased shopping activity ahead of Raksha Bandhan. These figures are CAIT estimates based on inputs from traders and trade associations, rather than audited market data.Much of the physical production still runs through India's traditional craft clusters. Kolkata remains a major wholesale and manufacturing hub, supplying rakhi traders across the country. Khadi rakhis from Nagpur, Sanganeri prints from Jaipur, seed rakhis from Pune, tea-leaf rakhis from Assam, jute rakhis from Kolkata, and bamboo and Madhubani-art rakhis from Bihar now sit alongside mass-produced options, driven in part by women's self-help groups and artisan collectives for whom the rakhi season is a source of supplementary household income.What has changed most visibly is the design vocabulary. This year's rakhi shelves carry threads built around Viksit Bharat, BrahMos and women's-empowerment themes alongside the more familiar Rudraksha, Swastik and Bhaiya-Bhabhi pairs, a sign of how quickly manufacturers now respond to the news cycle and government messaging, treating the rakhi as a wearable billboard as much as a ritual object. Superhero and cartoon-branded rakhis for children, evil-eye designs marketed as fashion accessories that can be worn past the festival, and premium metal or stone-studded pieces round out a market that has moved well beyond plain thread.Personalisation has become the dominant pitch, and not just at the top end.Sellers now routinely offer rakhis with a brother's name sublimated onto acrylic or wood, or a sibling photograph printed directly onto the pendant, products that would have required a jeweller or an artist a decade ago and are now templated, priced from under Rs 50 apiece, and turned around in bulk by small manufacturing units in cities such as Ahmedabad, Delhi and Jaipur. The wider gifting trend has moved the same way: industry trackers this year note a decline in generic mass-market combo set, the standard thread-plus-sweets hamper, in favour of curated boxes that buyers can customise by age, taste or budget, from wellness kits to eco-friendly packaging.The most disruptive change, though, has been in delivery. Quick-commerce platforms have turned the rakhi thali, once assembled by a sister at home or bought over a shop counter, into a same-day, sometimes same-hour order: thread, roli-chawal, sweets and a small gift bundled and dispatched from a neighbourhood dark store. For siblings living in different cities, or those who simply left the shopping too late, this has effectively replaced the courier parcels and last-minute market runs of previous years.That speed now comes with an asterisk. Since January this year, the quick-commerce platforms have all dropped explicit "10-minute" delivery claims from their branding, after the Union Labour Ministry pushed quick-commerce companies to stop advertising rigid delivery windows, citing rider safety concerns following gig-worker protests. Blinkit's tagline shifted from promising goods "in 10 minutes" to simply listing what it delivers; some of them now advertise "groceries in minutes" rather than a fixed number. The underlying model, dark stores, real-time inventory, delivery fleets built for speed, is unchanged, and rakhi orders still move fast during the festival rush; platforms have simply stopped putting a number on it.For the street sellers who used to own this season, the shift has been harder to absorb than a change in app copy. Rakesh, who sells rakhi threads and thalis from a stall in one of Delhi's older markets, has watched the balance of the trade move online over the past few years."The availability of Rakhi threads and thalis online have changed things a lot for us," he said. "People get things delivered in minutes, there is also the aspect of personalisation. Customers can get their money back if they do not like a design but that is not the case for us. The demand has not dropped dramatically but we can definitely sense a shift now."His account captures something the trade-body turnover figures don't: this isn't a market in collapse so much as one being quietly redistributed. Total demand for rakhis hasn't fallen, traders' projections for this year are, if anything, higher than last year's, but a growing share of it is being captured by platforms that can offer instant refunds, endless design catalogues and delivery to a doorstep hundreds of kilometres away, none of which a pavement stall can match. A street vendor operates on thin, fixed margins and cannot offer the kind of no-questions-asked returns that have become standard on e-commerce and quick-commerce apps; a design that doesn't suit a customer is a sunk cost for him in a way it isn't for a platform with centralised inventory. What he is describing is less a festival in decline than a festival whose profits are migrating toward whoever controls speed, choice and convenience, the same forces reshaping most other categories of Indian retail.The same platforms squeezing street vendors have opened a door for a different kind of small operator: the home-run, social-media-first rakhi business. Instagram and WhatsApp catalogues have made it possible for someone with no shop and little capital to sell personalised or handcrafted rakhis directly to customers, without a physical stall or a wholesaler in between.But reach isn't the same as revenue, says says a woman running an online rakhi business. "The biggest opportunity is using social media to reach more customers and promote products," she said. "But the biggest challenges for a new small business are building a customer base, increasing sales, competing with larger companies and recovering costs. When sales are low in the initial stages, profits can be very small, or there may be no profit at all.It's a reminder that the barriers for small players haven't disappeared with the shift online â they've simply moved. A social media page can put a home business in front of thousands of potential buyers, but it competes in the same feed as established D2C brands and marketplace sellers with bigger budgets, faster fulfilment and the cushion to absorb a slow first season. For someone starting out, the gap between visibility and an actual, sustainable customer base can take more than one festival cycle to close.The distance between Tagore's Kolkata processions and this year's app-driven rush is, on the surface, total: one was a deliberate refusal of commerce, staged to make a political point about unity in the face of engineered division; the other is commerce itself, organised around choice, speed and margin. But the thread running between them, literally, is the same one: an ordinary domestic ritual, elastic enough to be pressed into whatever a moment demands, whether that moment calls for resistance or for a same-day delivery slot. What has changed is not the rakhi but who gets to decide what it means, and increasingly, that decision is being made by whoever can get it to your wrist the fastest.

World.title: ‘We are very clear’: TN minister says Rahul Gandhi is INDIA bloc’s PM pick for 2029
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu minister P Viswanathan on Friday dismissed calls to project TVK chief Vijay C Joseph as the INDIA blocâs prime ministerial candidate for the 2029 Lok Sabha polls, asserting that Rahul Gandhi is the âdefinitiveâ choice.

âAs Congress leaders, we are very clear. Our beloved leader and leader of the opposition, Rahul Gandhi, is the INDIA blocâs prime ministerial candidate for 2029,â Viswanathan said.

His remarks came after several TVK leaders pushed for Vijay to be projected as a prime ministerial candidate for 2029 Lok Sabha polls , drawing sharp reaction from Congress.

TVK leaders, including KA Sengottaiyan and D Sarathkumar, have compared Vijay with former Tamil Nadu chief ministers MGR and Jayalalithaa, claiming he would not only rule Tamil Nadu but also lead the country in the future.

TVK legislator Kallanai, who organised an event marking the partyâs 100 days in office, said people had immense faith in Vijayâs leadership. He expressed confidence that Vijay would eventually lead the country and hoist the national flag at the Red Fort as a representative of the Tamil people, news agency PTI reported.

Meanwhile, Congress MP Karti Chidambaram said that while party workers may have deep admiration for their leader, national leadership ultimately depends on securing the numbers required to form a government.





âI fully accept that they have great love, affection, expectation, and admiration for their party leadership. This is their party. What they say within their party makes no difference to the public discourse. In public discourse, what you should ask about is policy and the law. Their wishes within a party make no difference to me,â Chidambaram told reporters, according to ANI.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

He said every political party has its own ambitions and aspirations, but any prime ministerial aspirant must ultimately have the numbers to command a majority in the Lok Sabha.

âEvery party has dreams, ambitions, and desires. One cannot pass laws to stop that. Everyone expresses their own wishes and talks about their favourite leader in their party. But we know what the political reality is. There are 543 constituencies," Chidambaram said.

According to the Constitution, the leader of whichever alliance wins 272 constituencies, or whichever party wins, will be the Prime Minister of India. Anyone who achieves that number can become the Prime Minister, individually or collectively. You and I both know what that political reality is,â he added.

World.title: 'Wore camouflage uniforms': Manipur ambush survivor recalls details of attackers
World.content:
Manipur ambush survivor says attackers wore camouflage uniforms

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

A survivor of the ambush that killed four members of the Liangmai Naga community in Manipur's Kangpokpi district on Friday has recalled how armed attackers, dressed in full camouflage uniforms, opened fire on their vehicle in a forested area.Forty-four-year-old Gaikamang Ringkangmai, who sustained a bullet injury to his left arm, was rescued by security forces from the ambush site and admitted to Senapati district hospital.Recalling the attack, Ringkangmai said as quoted by news agency PTI, "I am from Makui village. Yesterday, there were six of us in a vehicle. We frequently travelled by that route. We were going to Senapati district when we were ambushed by militants. Four of our colleagues died on the spot, while two of us escaped."He said he was injured during the firing but managed to flee the vehicle and take shelter in nearby bushes."I received bullet injuries on my arm but jumped from the vehicle and ran to hide in the bushes," he added.Describing the attackers, Ringkangmai claimed they were positioned in pairs and wore full camouflage uniforms. "They had red ribbons tied to the top of their rifles, from which they continued firing," he added.The other person who survived the ambush has been identified as Japou MK.The attack took place around 8.30 am on Thursday in an isolated, forested stretch between Makui Ashang and Thabamba Naga villages in Kangpokpi district. According to reports, the armed attackers targeted the vehicle carrying the group, killing four people on the spot and injuring another.The deceased have been identified as Tadsongbou Ringkangmai, founder and principal of a private school; M Wijunamai; Anil Wijunamai; and Wisobou Charenamai, chairman of the Chawangkining Village Authority. All six people travelling in the vehicle belonged to the Liangmai Naga community.The killings have triggered demands for justice from the Naga community, even as authorities move to identify and apprehend those responsible.W Charenamei, younger brother of deceased Wisobou Charenamai, said the family and community were not seeking retaliation."We donât seek any revenge against the militants. We just want the facts to be established and swift justice for our murdered brothers."Manipur chief minister Y Khemchand Singh has directed security officials to arrest those involved in the killings and initiate action against them.The United Naga Council (UNC), the apex Naga body in Manipur, has alleged that two Kuki militant outfits, the Kuki National Front (P) and Kuki Revolutionary Army (KRA), were behind the ambush.

World.title: ‘Accountability-evading gimmick’: Jairam Ramesh tears into Centre over free online coaching
World.content: Ramesh cited the latest report of the parliamentary standing committee of the ministry of social justice and empowerment, tabled on August 10, to question the government's record on its existing free coaching scheme.

World.title: 'Not publisher of Sonia Gandhi's memoir': Penguin rejects 'editorial changes' claim
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Penguin Random House India on Friday clarified that it is not the publisher of Congress leader Sonia Gandhi's memoir Belonging: A Journey of Love in India.

The Publishing house rejected reports that it decided against publishing the book because the author declined editorial changes.

In a statement posted on X, the publishing house said it had remained "willing and keen to publish" the memoir and stressed that fact-checking and providing editorial recommendations are a normal part of the publishing process.

"In response to the news reports about Sonia Gandhi's book 'Belonging',

Penguin Random House India is not the publisher of 'Belonging' in India. Any suggestion that Penguin Random House India decided not to publish 'Belonging' because the author declined editorial changes does not accurately reflect the circumstances.

As a publisher, it is both our prerogative and our responsibility to fact check and provide authors with recommendations that are in the best interests of their books. This is a normal part of the publishing process. Throughout the relevant discussions, Penguin Random House India's position was that we remained willing and keen to publish the book.

We will not comment further on confidential discussions with the author."





The clarification comes weeks after US publisher Alfred A Knopf, an imprint of Penguin Random House, announced that Belonging would be released on November 10.

The status of the memoir's publisher or distributor in India remains unclear. An e-commerce listing has shown an ebook edition of Belonging available for pre-order at Rs 2,615, with William Collins, an imprint of HarperCollins UK, listed as its publisher.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Sonia Gandhi, 79, is expected to offer a personal account of her life, including her childhood in post-war Italy, her marriage into the Nehru-Gandhi family and the death of her husband Rajiv Gandhi, according to Alfred A Knopf.

The memoir will also cover her entry into the "public world of politics" following Rajiv Gandhi's assassination and her decision to turn down the prime minister's post in 2004.

The publisher had earlier described the book as tracing Sonia Gandhi's life "from her childhood in post-war Italy, to the romance that brings her to India, to the shattering losses that will reshape not only her own future but also that of her adopted home".

Sonia Gandhi has rarely discussed her private life at length in public, making the memoir one of the most closely watched political books ahead of its release.

World.title: CPI urges govt. to declare delta districts as drought-hit
World.content:
The Communist Party of India (CPI) has urged the State government to declare the delta districts as drought affected in view of non-release of Cauvery water from the Mettur dam impacting the kuruvai cultivation season due to which the coverage of paddy got reduced substantially.

The party has urged the State government to provide ₹30,000 per acre as compensation for those farmers who had suffered heavy losses during kuruvai cultivation season due to water shortage.

It wanted the government to provide ₹15,000 as relief to the agricultural labourers of the delta region who were rendered jobless in view of the drought-like situation. It urged the government to waive the crop loans as promised; take special measures to provide rice and other essential commodities to all those families in the drought-hit areas and take steps on a war footing to tackle the drinking water shortage prevailing in several villages and ensure steady supply of drinking water to them.

A section of CPI members staged a demonstration in support of its demands in Tiruchi on Friday. The demonstration was held near the District Collectorate for nearly an hour.

In Nagapattinam, a group of CPI members, led by party’s former State secretary R. Mutharasan and Nagapattinam Lok Sabha member V. Selvaraj, submitted a memorandum to the Nagapattinam Collector K.J. Praveen Kumar at the District Collectorate.

World.title: B. Nagedra resigns from Karnataka Cabinet amid Valmiki Corporation scam row
World.content:
Barely 25 days after returning to the Karnataka Cabinet, Planning and Statistics Minister B. Nagendra resigned on Friday (August 28) over allegations of involvement in the embezzlement of funds from the State-run Karnataka Maharshi Valmiki Scheduled Tribes Development Corporation Ltd.

The Minister announced his decision to step down at a press conference at the State secretariat. Mr. Nagendra said he had no role in the scam but he resigned to avoid the embarrassment to the party and the government.

He also decided to quit the membership of the Karnataka Legislative Assembly and challenged the BJP to face him in the Ballari Rural constituency (ST reserved).

At the press conference, Mr. Nagendra was accompanied by Ministers Ajay Singh, Rizwan Arshad and MPs Nasir Hussain and G.C. Chandrashekar at the State Secretariat.

This is the second time Mr. Nagendra has resigned from the Cabinet over the same issue. He had earlier resigned on June 6, 2024, when he was Minister for Scheduled Tribes Welfare, Youth Empowerment and Sports in the Siddaramaiah government.

The four-time MLA from Ballari Rural is the first Minister to quit the Cabinet since D.K. Shivakumar became Chief Minister on June 3. Mr. Nagendra was re-inducted into the Cabinet on August 3.

Mr. Nagendra decided to step down after Mr. Shivakumar met Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and other senior leaders in Delhi. He was also in the national capital and is understood to have decided to resign after discussions with the party’s central leadership.

The Opposition BJP and JD(S) had mounted pressure on the government for his resignation during the recent monsoon session of the Legislature. Although Mr. Nagendra sought to invoke the Dalit issue to defend his continuation in the Cabinet, the Opposition’s decision to undertake a 10-day padayatra from Raichur to Ballari from September 1 over the alleged scam appears to have increased pressure on him to quit.

Mr. Shivakumar, who had earlier described Mr. Nagendra as a “disciplined soldier of the party”, will accept his resignation in a move aimed at preventing further political embarrassment to the Congress government.

Sources said Mr. Nagendra’s continuation had increasingly become a liability for the Shivakumar government, particularly since the alleged irregularities occurred during the previous Siddaramaiah government.

The possibility of Governor Thaawarchand Gehlot granting sanction for prosecution, following a plea by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), is also believed to have influenced the decision. The Governor has reportedly written to the State Cabinet seeking clarity on Mr. Nagendra’s continuation in the Ministry.

The Enforcement Directorate has already filed a chargesheet in the alleged multi-crore scam in the corporation.

During the Siddaramaiah government, Mr. Nagendra announced his resignation at a press conference at the State Secretariat in June 2024. On that occasion, the BJP had taken out a march from the Secretariat to Raj Bhavan and submitted a memorandum to Governor Gehlot seeking his resignation over the alleged financial irregularities in the corporation. The BJP had also demanded a CBI probe. The CBI and the Enforcement Directorate subsequently investigated the case.

The alleged fraud came to light after corporation accounts superintendent P. Chandrashekharan was found dead on May 26, 2024. In a note, he had alleged that funds were illegally transferred from the corporation to various accounts, including those allegedly linked to IT companies and a Hyderabad-based cooperative bank.

World.title: ‘Digital open-distance learning can democratise higher education’
World.content:
Digital technologies, open educational resources and innovative learning models can transform open and distance learning into a powerful tool for democratising higher education, Director, Commonwealth Educational Media Centre for Asia (CEMCA), Basheerhamad Shadrach, said.

Delivering the keynote lecture on ‘BRAOU and the promise of democratised education’ at Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Open University’s 45th Foundation Day celebrations on Friday, he said asynchronous digital learning allows students to learn at their own time, pace and language. Farmers, homemakers and working professionals could pursue education alongside their daily responsibilities, he said.

Mr. Shadrach noted that AI-driven personalised learning was making education more adaptive and learner-centric. Digital ODL could help institutions expand access, reduce costs and continuously update course content. He said BRAOU’s TV broadcasts, Hi-BRAOU Digital Radio, iBooks and integrated DigiLibrary offered a multi-channel approach to reach learners online and offline.

Vice-Chancellor Ghanta Chakrapani said that BRAOU was transforming into a full-fledged digital and online university by embracing technology and AI, while retaining its focus on inclusiveness, accessibility and quality.

World.title: Nepal flash floods LIVE: Death toll rises to 547; fear of fresh floods looms
World.content:
Fears of a second wave of flash floods loomed large in Nepal after authorities issued a fresh warning on Friday (August 28, 2026) following an increase in the water level in the Bhotekoshi River area, as the death toll from the flood-related devastation crossed 547.

The National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority said the rise in the water level at the same site raised the risk of another flood in the area.

WATCH | Why did the flash floods happen in Nepal?

Earlier, the Nepal Police issued an alert after receiving information that a water dam on the Tibetan side had burst again. Chinese state broadcaster CCTV also warned that a dammed lake upstream of ‌the Gyirong border port had begun to overflow.

Nepal’s Prime Minister Balendra Shah and his Council of Ministers on Friday (August 28, 2026) decided to deposit a month of their salaries to Prime Minister’s Disaster Relief Fund in the wake of devastating floods in the country. Meanwhile, Nepal’s Foreign Ministry said it does not ‌need help from ⁠other countries to conduct search and ‌rescue operations.

Also Read | Danger from above: On the Nepal flood

A preliminary assessment suggested the collapse of a high-altitude glacier in Nepal was behind the mudslides and floods along the Nepal-China border, China’s Foreign Ministry said on Friday (August 28, 2026). Chinese authorities said 555 tourists had been evacuated from Gyirong county in Tibet. As of Friday (August 28), Chinese authorities had confirmed five deaths but added that more than 558 people were still missing.

World.title: Liquor sales curbed in Hayyal (B) village till Monday
World.content:
Deputy Commissioner Rahul Pandve, who is also the District Magistrate, has passed an order prohibiting liquor sales till 6 a.m. on Monday in Hayyal (B) village and the areas surrounding the Sri Hayyalalingeshwar temple in Wadagera taluk in view of the annual fair of the temple.

​Exercising powers conferred on him under Section 21 of the Karnataka Excise Act 1965, the District Magistrate has ordered temporary closure of all retail and wholesale liquor shops, wine shops and bars situated within a 5-km radius of Hayyal (B) village to ensure law and order during the festival.

World.title: Konaseema villages breath sigh of relief as seven missing fishermen return home
World.content:
Seven missing fishermen from Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema district of Andhra Pradesh returned home on Friday, ending their 23-day ordeal of being stranded in the Bay of Bengal.

The five coastal villages in the Odalarevu breathed a sigh of relief as the missing fishermen reunited with their families.

On August 3, the fishermen sailed into the Bay of Bengal from Odalarevu fish landing centre in search of Tuna fish. They lost contact with their families on August 5, after their boat engine failed.

The boat with the seven missing fishermen on board was sighted by local fishermen near Shankarpur fishing habour in Purba Medinipur district off West Bengal coast.

“We lost our way at around 150 to 200 nautical miles off the Andhra Pradesh coast. Our boat drifted towards the Odisha and West Bengal coasts,” the fishermen said.

The fishermen reached their villages at around 11.30 a.m. on Friday and their family burst into tears of joy.

Surrounded by their loved ones, Karri Rambabu and Kopanati Rama Krishna of Komaragiripatnam village; Kollati Yesudasu Bendamuri Lanka, Kollati Srinubabu and Palepu Santa Rao of Odalarevu; S. Tata Rao of Brahma Samedhyam village of Katrenikona mandal; and Katadi Satish Kumar of Pasuvulanka in I. Polavaram mandal broke into tears.

TDP MLA Vanamadi Venkateswara Rao received the fishermen in Kakinada upon their arrival from West Bengal by road. In Amalapuram, Member of Parliament G. Harish Madhur met them and inquired about their health condition.

During an interaction with Fisheries Department officials, the survivors and their family members thanked the officials for the rescue operation.

World.title: ‘No going back on Mangaluru’s integration with SWR’
World.content:
Udupi-Chikkamagaluru Member of Parliament Kota Srinivas Poojary on Friday said the Railway Ministry would not reverse its decision on bringing Mangaluru Railway region from Southern Railway’s Palakkad Division to South Western Railway’s Mysuru Division.

In a statement here, Mr. Poojary said Minister of State for Railways V. Somanna informed him over telephone on Friday that the Ministry would not succumb to pressure tactics from the Keralam government and political leaders. He assured the people of Karnataka that they need not worry whether the Ministry would reverse the August 21 decision.

The Minister told the MP that Mangaluru’s integration with SWR was not just an issue for coastal Karnataka, but would positively impact the entire State. The decision would also boost income to the State government through enhanced and efficient operation of freight and passenger traffic.

Mr. Poojary said he had earlier congratulated Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw, and Mr. Somanna for the historic decision on Mangaluru’s integration with SWR. It was the culmination of joint efforts by the region’s representatives, past, and present. This significant decision was taken without any role played by the Karnataka government, the MP stressed. Still, the Union government has rendered justice to the people of Karnataka, he said.

Stating that the integration would help augment railway infrastructure and enhance train operations in the region, Mr. Poojary said people’s representatives would continue their efforts to merge Konkan Railway Corporation Ltd. with Indian Railways. They are focused on doubling the KRCL network and bringing in new projects.

Capt. Chowta meets Somanna

Meanwhile, Dakshina Kannada MP Captain Brijesh Chowta met Mr. Somanna in Bengaluru and personally extended his gratitude on behalf of the people of Karnataka for the historic decision.

He said he expressed his gratitude for Mr. Somanna’s guidance and for “aiding the long-pending transfer of Mangaluru to Mysuru Railway Division of SWR.”

World.title: Dalit man transporting cattle forced to eat cow dung by ‘cow vigilantes’ in Maharashtra; no arrest made yet
World.content:
Six ‘cow vigilantes’, suspected to be Bajrang Dal members, have been booked for allegedly assaulting a Dalit man and forcing him to eat cow dung after accusing him of attempting to sell a bull he had bought in Jalna district of Maharashtra.

While the incident took place in May 2026, the victim lodged the FIR on Thursday (August 28, 2026) when a video of the purported assault went viral online, officials said.

A case was registered at Taluka police station under Sections 126(2) (wrongful restraint), 115(2) (voluntarily causing physical hurt to another person), and 189(2) (unlawful assembly) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) besides provisions of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act. The six accused have been identified as Venkatesh Bhagat, Arjun Singh, Shivraj Picchade, Somesh Patil, Yash Sarkate, and Ritesh Deshmukh, said police inspector Santosh Sable.

Parameshwar Suhas Hiwale, the complainant who works as a truck driver, told police that he was returning to Jalna with his 11-year-old son and acquaintance Narayan Maroti Kamble, who had hired his services to purchase a bull at the weekly cattle market at Deulgaon Raja town.

Used casteist abuses

A group claiming to be Bajrang Dal members and ‘cow protectors’ allegedly followed them on bikes and waylaid his enclosed pick-up trick in Kanhaiyanagar area of Jalna. One of the accused caught the victim’s shirt collar and asked him what was in the truck, to which Mr. Hiwale said that they had a bull that was legally purchased by Mr. Kamble and even showed the documents for proof. However, they did not listen to him and slapped him. When Mr. Hiwale responded to their queries about his name and caste, they allegedly hurled casteist slurs at him.

One of the accused then brought some cow dung from the back of the truck and handed it to his accomplice who forced it into the victim’s mouth. They even tried to force it upon his son, but Mr. Hiwale apparently prevented him from doing so. The entire incident was recorded on a mobile phone and the accused threatened to leave Mr. Hiwale and his minor son naked on the road. They beat up and slapped Mr. Kamble as well, while also damaging the vehicle in the process.

Threatened to murder

The accused threatened to kill the victim and his family if he informed the police about the incident and accused Mr. Hiwale of planning to sell the bull to a Muslim butcher.

None of the six accused has been arrested so far, and an investigation is ongoing.

​

According to Mr. Hiwale’s complaint, the police arrived at the spot where a crowd had gathered on May 23 and all three victims were taken to a local police station in Jalna. According to Jalna Deputy Superintendent of Police Anant Kulkarni, Mr. Hiwale was allegedly found transporting three cows and two other cattle in closed trailers attached to the pick-up trick. Police seized the vehicle along with the animals and registered a complaint under relevant provisions of the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960. That probe is also still under way, police said.

World.title: PML-N's Syed Iftikhar Ali Gillani elected new AJK prime minister
World.content:
MUZAFFARABAD: PML-N’s Barrister Syed Iftikhar Ali Gillani was elected Azad Jammu and Kashmir’s prime minister on Friday, securing 30 of the 44 votes polled in the assembly.

His sole contender was PPP’s Sardar Mukhtar Ahmed Abbasi, who bagged 14 votes in the contest for the top office.

The AJK Assembly comprises 53 members, but its present strength is 46 — PML-N’s being 32, including its allies, and PPP’s 14 — because elections to seven seats in Poonch and Sudhnoti districts have yet to be held.

However, 44 votes were polled in Friday’s elections as the speaker did not cast his vote and PML-N regional president Shah Ghulam Qadir was not present in the assembly.

Qadir, along with former AJK premier Raja Farooq Haider, had previously opposed Gillani’s nomination for the post. However, when assembly proceedings began on Friday, Haider entered the House alongside Gillani.

After the votes were counted, Speaker Chaudhry Tariq Farooq announced the result, declaring Gillani as the winner amid clapping and slogans from the galleries.

Gillani has succeeded PPP’s Rathore, who was elected as the prime minister in November 2025.

Following his election, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif congratulated him and expressed hope that he would “play an effective role in the development of AJK and the welfare of its people”, state broadcaster Radio Pakistan reported.

Citing an official statement, the report said PM Shehbaz credited PML-N leadership and workers’ “hard work” for the party’s victory in AJK.

He said the federal government would continue extending all possible support for the development, prosperity and improved living standards of the people of AJK and termed the “continuation of the democratic process in Azad Jammu and Kashmir a welcome development”.

Gillani’s nomination

PML-N’s decision to nominate Gillani was announced by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif at a meeting with four senior PML-N leaders from AJK in Islamabad, late on Wednesday night.

The meeting, which took place at the Prime Min­ister’s House, was attended by PML-N AJK President Shah Ghulam Qadir, his predecessor and former AJK premier Raja Farooq Haider, the party’s regional secretary general and asse­mbly speaker, Chaudhry Tariq Farooq, and Deputy Spe­a­ker Ahmed Raza Qadri.

The prime minister was accompanied by his aide, Rana Sanaullah, and senior PML-N leader Saad Rafique.

Gillani was also invited to the PM House but did not join the meeting, where PM Shehbaz infor­med the visiting leaders that party supremo Nawaz Sharif had decided to nominate Gillani as the party’s candidate for the AJK premiership.

The decision, however, triggered a sharp reaction from Qadir and Haider, who reportedly expressed their disagreement and announced that they would not participate in Friday’s election process.

However, only Qadir did not participate in the election.

Speculation that Gillani could be chosen for the premiership had been rife since he was elected to the assembly on a reserved seat on Aug 24.

However, the party’s regional leadership believed that the formula followed in 2016, when Haider was elevated as prime minister, would be repeated this time as well.

Following the reaction of the two senior leaders, Sanaullah and Rafique held another meeting with them, but it remained inconclusive, sources told Dawn.

In a post-midnight message on X, Qadir assured the “self-respecting people of Azad Kashmir” that he would not compromise on their honour and dignity. “Nawaz Sharif’s slogan of giving respect to the vote will be ensured,” he added.

On Thursday afternoon, however, PML-N central information secretary and Punjab senior minister Marriyum Aurangzeb posted on X that PM Shehbaz had finalised Gillani as the party’s candidate and directed him to submit his nomination papers for election as AJK prime minister.

AJK polls

The elections in the region, originally scheduled for July 27, were divided into phases over security concerns amid unrest in the region. The first phase was held on July 27, the second on Aug 2 and the third on Aug 10.

Meanwhile, the third phase was originally meant to cover all of Poonch Division, which comprises 11 constituencies, including three in Bagh, one in Haveli, five in Poonch district and two in Sudhnoti district.

However, the AJK Election Commission announced that polling would only go ahead as scheduled in Bagh and Haveli because of concerns over the law and order situation.

So far, in the direct elections to 38 constituencies, the PML-N has secured 25 seats while the PPP won 12. The lone MLA-elect of the Awami Dast-o-Bazu party has also joined hands with the PML-N .

As for the reserved seats, the PML-N has bagged six and the PPP two.

The PPP has alleged widespread rigging and irregularities in the elections.

World.title: Pims fire: Mustafa Kamal says 'no one will be spared', calls for reforming health sector
World.content:
Health Minister Mustafa Kamal on Friday vowed that “no one will be spared” while talking about the fire at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims) that claimed the lives of 14 infants, adding that the country’s health sector needed to be reformed.

Speaking in the Senate, Kamal said: “No one intends to spare or save anyone. I am saying this on behalf of the prime minister and the entire government that not a single person will be spared”.

He said that the tragedy cannot be an “episode lasting merely a few days,” as he called for accountability and for efforts to prevent such incidents in the future.

The minister warned against “suppressing the issue” and invited the House to work towards a way forward, agreeing to a proposal seeking the formation of a parliamentary committee comprising opposition members to investigate Wednesday’s incident.

“Look at your resources, management and actions and then involve everyone to suggest a way forward,” he said, assuring that the government will support such an approach.

“This is a matter of children’s lives, and we are answerable to God for it. The ministry is nothing; we cannot ruin our afterlife for these ministries,” he remarked.

At the outset of his address, the minister expressed sorrow at the lives lost in the incident.

“There can be no explanation for this. I am holding myself responsible, and I have presented myself to be held accountable.”

He called for a holistic approach toward investigating the incident, urging that any committee formed to probe should not be “time-bound and should remain open”.

“When you go investigate this incident, you will find so many things associated with it,” he said, pointing to a larger “rot” within the sector.

Kamal held that the health sector was not “ideal”.

“Four hundred thousand children between the ages of one and five die every year, 1,300 die every day; they are all dying preventable deaths,” he said.

He continued: “It is not possible to bring back the infants who died at Pims, but let us look at it as a test from God and prevent the next kid from dying.”

Kamal maintained that there was “no point” in making speeches if the government failed to learn from the incident.

“Start from me,” Kamal said, offering himself up for accountability.

“Sit with us and save the next from dying. I am putting the entire ministry at your disposal; every person will be answerable to you,” he said.

He noted that the system was “rotten” and went on to say: “Where do I find a better person after removing an incompetent one?”

Kamal said that when the day ended, “1,300 children would have died across the country”.

Speaking about the inquiry committee’s report on the incident, which he said would be presented by tonight, Kamal assured the House: “If you don’t trust it, fair enough [..] we will listen to you.”

The health minister once again reassured the House that, “No one will be spared, no matter how influential they are”.

“We have to come up with a solution, and I am inviting you to guide us and [..] give us a strategic roadmap,” he said. Kamal said that the health ministry would provide all the relevant input and information.

“Sit with us and find a way forward on how to prevent the next child from dying due to negligence within the resources that we have. I assure you of its implementation”.

However, he added that if matters were to move in that direction, “no MNA should call and ask why a certain doctor was removed”.

Calling for “radical reforms” in the health sector, Kamal urged that the Pims fire “can serve as a basis for how we can prevent more children from dying”.

The minister further stated that he was “withholding his information” on the fire until the committee’s report.

“If you are dissatisfied (with the report), then form a committee, and everyone stands ready to be held accountable”.

Concluding his address, Kamal urged that the “issue should be only closed at a point where we can prevent similar incidents in the future”.

“I am willing to sit here all night and listen,” he added.

The minister, during his address, in response to calls for his resignation, said: “Let the investigation be completed. I have already taken action beyond what they are thinking.”

Sherry Rehman calls for accountability; PTI’s Ali Zafar proposes formation of committee

The routine business in the Senate was suspended on a motion moved by PPP parliamentary leader in the House Senator Sherry Rehman for a thorough discussion on the Pims fire.

Speaking in the Senate, Rehman stressed that the incident raised serious questions of governance, accountability and public safety.

“Wherever there is a failure, there must be accountability. Audit and accountability are an integral part of politics. Working for public interest in the Senate is politics. Politics is to work for the good of people, to work for public interest. Politics is all about accountability.“ she stressed.

Rehman said her concerns were also rooted in her own experience as a former health minister. “I have served as health minister for six months. I was also given reasons to close the emergency gates, but I did not. Instead, I posted guards there and checked myself. Why are incompetent people who don’t care about basic safety protocols even allowed to continue?”

“The executive director of Pims was lying when he said that the emergency gate was not closed. The firefighters and the Capital Development Authority (CDA) have stated that the gate was closed. What is the purpose of an emergency exit? It is supposed to remain open for emergencies,” Rehman questioned.

Rehman also pointed to contradictions between the Pims report and the findings of CDA, particularly concerning the hospital’s fire-safety arrangements.

“The PIMS report contradicts the CDA’s findings. The CDA has repeatedly stated that the hospital’s fire-safety arrangements are inadequate. Why was no notice taken? The hospital does not even have a fire NOC.”

Senator Rehman highlighted the substantial federal funding provided to Pims, and questioned why basic safety standards had not been ensured despite the availability of resources.

PTI leader Barrister Ali Zafar proposed the formation of a special committee comprising an equal number of government and opposition members, with an opposition member as its head.

He said the committee should examine hospital safety and emergency preparedness and develop comprehensive Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for dealing with foreseeable hazards and emergencies.

The committee, he proposed, should also ensure that these SOPs are available, properly implemented and regularly reviewed in every hospital “Let us start with Islamabad,” he said.

Zafar further proposed that the committee be empowered to inspect hospitals, call for records, seek explanations from hospital administrations and co-opt medical, fire-safety, engineering, disaster-management and other relevant experts whenever required.

He said the administrations of all hospitals should be directed to fully cooperate with the committee and provide all necessary information, records, facilities and assistance required for it to perform its mandate.

“This should not be another committee that merely produces a report which sits on a shelf,” he said.

According to Zafar, the committee should be focused on identifying failures, correcting them, establishing enforceable safety protocols and ensuring compliance.

“We owe this not only to those who lost their lives in this tragedy, but to every patient and every family who will have to depend on our hospitals in the future,” he said.

The Senate also passed unanimously a resolution calling for the formation of a special Senate committee to investigate the incident on Friday. It was moved by Senator Rehman.

NA passes resolution for inquiry into fire

Meanwhile, the National Assembly unanimously approved a resolution, calling for an impartial inquiry into the incident and expressing condolences to the affected families.

Through the resolution, a copy of which is available with Dawn, lawmakers expressed “profound grief and sorrow” over the incident and strongly condemned it. They raised alarm at the circumstances surrounding the fire, with the resolution stating that the circumstances were a result of “sheer negligence”.

It called upon the government to “take strict action against anyone responsible for negligence or safety lapses in accordance with the law”.

Lawmakers also called on the government to ensure that fire safety and emergency preparedness measures were strictly implemented in federal government hospitals, particularly in neonatal and paediatric units, to prevent such incidents in the future.

“The House […] extends its heartfelt condolences to the bereaved families and prays for strength and fortitude for them in this hour of profound grief,” the resolution added.

Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar expressed his condolences and informed the NA about the steps taken by the prime minister.

He said that PM Shehbaz had constituted two committees — one headed by Dr Azhar Kiani and the other by former Secretary Shahid Khan. The committee headed by Dr Kiani would provide information on what was required for the improvement of Pims.

The minister also asked for concrete suggestions to be made in the House instead of the issue being politicised.

Former prime minister and PPP leader Raja Pervez Ashraf said that the nation had a “habit” of forming a committee or a commission on such matters to keep it alive, but eventually forgetting about the incident within a few weeks.

“We need to have a change of approach towards hazards and the health sector,” he said.

Ashraf criticised that even after days, nobody was clear about the reasons for the accident, calling for a committee of parliamentarians belonging to all parties in the House to investigate the matter and “at least” inquire into the cause of the fire.

PTI senior leader Asad Qaiser noted that the fateful incident occurred at the same hospital that the government claimed had the best facilities when it came to the treatment of incarcerated PTI founder Imran Khan. Last week, Imran had undergone a medical check-up at Pims — rather than Islamabad’s private Shifa International Hospital as per the directions of the Supreme Court — before being shifted back to Adiala jail.

Rs5m compensation announced for affected families

Earlier in the day, Parliamentary Affairs Minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry announced Rs5 million compensation for each family affected by the fire.

Recalling Wednesday’s incident while speaking to the media at Pims, Chaudhry lamented that 14 infants had fallen victim to “someone’s criminal negligence”.

He added that the prime minister had constituted an inquiry committee that was expected to present its report today, assuring that all those “on-duty individuals found guilty of negligence will be given exemplary punishment”.

The minister said the grief of the affected families could not be compensated for.

“Neither can their children be brought back, nor can their grief be reduced,” he added. “But to provide some relief […] the prime minister has announced that Rs5 million will be given to all the affected families.”

Chaudhry said he was visiting Pims to hand over a cheque to one of the affected families on behalf of the prime minister, adding that the compensation amount would be deposited in the accounts of the deceased children’s mothers.
